note: Facilitator-only teaching library, second of the planned set. Sits alongside library-strengths-gifts.json and never replaces it. Rows are the 72 unique 16Personalities strength descriptors, deduplicated across the 16 types; weakness descriptors are deliberately out of scope. Served from an authenticated endpoint. Never ship inside the page. blends[descriptor|gift] holds recognize (what it looks like in a person) and ask (a question the facilitator can put to them). Purpose is unblocking, not teaching.

Altruistic|Administration.recognize: You take the job nobody claimed and then build the routine that keeps it running. People stop asking who will handle it, because you always have. What nobody has noticed is that everything now rests on one person.
Altruistic|Administration.ask: Who would have to be trained if you were gone a month?

Altruistic|Apostleship.recognize: You go where the work is hardest and stay long enough to get it standing, then hand it off and go again. What nobody sees is that you have never once been the person somebody went back for.
Altruistic|Apostleship.ask: Who checked on you after the last thing you started?

Altruistic|Discernment.recognize: You read a room and move quietly toward whoever is struggling in it, and you are usually right about who that is. The trouble is you spend that read on other people and never turn it on yourself.
Altruistic|Discernment.ask: When did you last name what you needed out loud?

Altruistic|Evangelism.recognize: Nobody doubts you mean it, because they watched you live it before you said it. The risk is that you give the whole of yourself to a stranger and arrive home with nothing left for the people who live there.
Altruistic|Evangelism.ask: Which person at home got your leftovers this week?

Altruistic|Exhortation.recognize: You put your own reserves behind somebody else's next step, and it lands because they can tell it cost you something. The blind spot is how long you keep spending on people who are not moving.
Altruistic|Exhortation.ask: Who have you been propping up who has not moved in a year?

Altruistic|Faith.recognize: You will hand over what you cannot spare on the conviction that it will be all right, and often it is. What you may not see is that you have made your own margin the offering every single time.
Altruistic|Faith.ask: What did you give last month that you actually needed?

Altruistic|Giving.recognize: You do not wait to be asked and you never mention it afterward. Half the room has been helped by you and does not know it. The quiet part is that you have never let anyone do the same for you.
Altruistic|Giving.ask: When did someone last help you and you allowed it?

Altruistic|Healing.recognize: You sit with people in the worst of it and something in them eases. You will stay past the point anyone else would. What you carry out of those rooms goes somewhere, and it is usually into you.
Altruistic|Healing.ask: Where do you put what you take on from other people?

Altruistic|Interpretation.recognize: You put words to what somebody is going through and they feel understood for the first time. The cost is that you are so used to speaking for other people that your own account goes untold.
Altruistic|Interpretation.ask: Who knows what this year has actually been like for you?

Altruistic|Knowledge.recognize: You learn a person's situation in detail because you intend to be useful in it, and nobody asked you to. The strain shows when you hold a dozen situations at once with nowhere to set any of them down.
Altruistic|Knowledge.ask: Whose situation are you keeping track of right now?

Altruistic|Leadership.recognize: You go first into the part nobody wants, and people follow because of it. The difficulty is that a team built on your willingness to take the worst never learns to share it.
Altruistic|Leadership.ask: What is the last unpleasant job you let someone else have?

Altruistic|Mercy.recognize: You move toward pain that other people step around, and you do not flinch at it. The question is not whether you have room for someone else. It is whether anyone is holding room for you.
Altruistic|Mercy.ask: Who calls to ask how you are?

Altruistic|Miracles.recognize: You put yourself in situations that only work if God shows up, and you do it on somebody else's behalf rather than your own. The pattern worth watching is that you will ask heaven for anything except something for you.
Altruistic|Miracles.ask: What have you never prayed for on your own behalf?

Altruistic|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You notice who is missing and you go after them. Nobody drifts out of your care quietly. What goes unnoticed is that your own drifting would not set off anybody's alarm.
Altruistic|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who would notice if you went quiet for two weeks?

Altruistic|Prophecy.recognize: You will say the hard thing when it is for someone's good, and you take the fallout yourself rather than let it land on them. The hidden cost is that you absorb every hard thing said back to you as well.
Altruistic|Prophecy.ask: What criticism from this year are you still carrying?

Altruistic|Service.recognize: The chairs are stacked, the room is reset, and you are already gone. You prefer it that way. The risk in preferring it is that a person nobody thanks slowly becomes a person nobody sees.
Altruistic|Service.ask: When were you last thanked, and how did it feel?

Altruistic|Teaching.recognize: You will sit with the person who is not getting it long after everyone else has moved on, and they get it because of you. What you may not weigh is what those hours cost the things nobody is asking about.
Altruistic|Teaching.ask: What did you set aside to make time for that person?

Altruistic|Tongues.recognize: You give up your own place in a moment without anybody noticing you did. It comes easily and it is real. But a thing given up too easily is rarely counted, including by you.
Altruistic|Tongues.ask: What did you let go of this week that mattered?

Altruistic|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you their decisions because you think about their good ahead of your own and they can feel it. The pattern to watch is that you have made yourself so available to their choices that you never sit with your own.
Altruistic|Wisdom.ask: What decision of yours have you been putting off?

Analytical|Administration.recognize: You want to see how the whole thing works before you agree to run any part of it, and once you do, it runs well. The delay is that you keep taking the machine apart while people are waiting to use it.
Analytical|Administration.ask: What are you still evaluating that the team needed decided weeks ago?

Analytical|Apostleship.recognize: You are the one who asks what happens in year three before anybody has bought the land, and that question has saved ventures. It also arrives at the exact moment the people around you needed courage instead.
Analytical|Apostleship.ask: When did your question stop something that should have gone ahead?

Analytical|Discernment.recognize: You will not accept a read on somebody until you can say what produced it, which keeps you from being wrong about people cheaply. It also means you can talk yourself out of something you knew in thirty seconds.
Analytical|Discernment.ask: What did you know early about someone and then argue yourself out of?

Analytical|Evangelism.recognize: You will not overstate the case, so when you do speak about faith, people believe you. The cost is spending so long getting the argument airtight that the conversation ended two weeks ago.
Analytical|Evangelism.ask: Who were you going to talk to once you had the answer ready?

Analytical|Exhortation.recognize: You encourage with specifics, which is why it lands when general praise does not. Where it stalls is when someone needed to hear that they are loved and you handed them an assessment instead.
Analytical|Exhortation.ask: Who needed encouragement from you and got feedback?

Analytical|Faith.recognize: You want the reasoning and God rarely supplies it in advance. You have learned to move anyway, which has cost you more than it costs other people. Watch for asking one more question when the answer has already come.
Analytical|Faith.ask: What are you waiting for evidence of that you already know?

Analytical|Giving.recognize: You want to know where it goes and what it accomplishes, and your generosity is more effective because of it. The risk is that a need standing in front of you waits while you finish the diligence.
Analytical|Giving.ask: What did you research instead of simply meeting?

Analytical|Healing.recognize: You look for the cause underneath what somebody presents, and you often find it. What that misses is the person who does not need their situation solved yet, only sat with.
Analytical|Healing.ask: Who wanted your company and got your diagnosis?

Analytical|Interpretation.recognize: You will not let a vague account stand, so what you hand back is genuinely clearer than what you were given. The strain falls on the person whose experience you keep asking to be more precise.
Analytical|Interpretation.ask: Who stopped telling you things because of the follow-up questions?

Analytical|Knowledge.recognize: You go further down than anybody asked and you come back with something real. The trap is that going down is more comfortable than coming back, and there is always one more layer.
Analytical|Knowledge.ask: What have you been studying that you should have delivered by now?

Analytical|Leadership.recognize: People trust your decisions because you can show your work. The bottleneck is that a team moving at your pace of confidence spends a great deal of time standing still.
Analytical|Leadership.ask: Which decision has your team not been given yet?

Analytical|Mercy.recognize: You want to understand what happened to somebody before you decide how to help, and it makes your help fit. Where it goes wrong is treating a person's grief as a problem with an input you have not yet identified.
Analytical|Mercy.ask: Who did you try to solve when they only needed you there?

Analytical|Miracles.recognize: You test what other people accept without question, which has protected your church from real nonsense. It also means you have quietly reasoned away the two or three things you could not account for.
Analytical|Miracles.ask: What have you seen that you still have no explanation for?

Analytical|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You track how people are actually doing rather than what they say, and your reading is usually right. The gap is that a person is not a set of measurements and can feel when they are being one.
Analytical|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who feels assessed by you rather than known?

Analytical|Prophecy.recognize: You will not say a hard thing until you are sure of it, so when you say it, it carries weight. The delay is the problem: by the time you are sure, the moment has usually passed.
Analytical|Prophecy.ask: What did you finally say that should have been said months earlier?

Analytical|Service.recognize: You find the inefficiency nobody else noticed and the whole job gets easier for everyone. The friction is that people wanted help and got a review of their method first.
Analytical|Service.ask: Who asked for help and heard how they were doing it wrong?

Analytical|Teaching.recognize: You take a thing apart far enough down that people finally understand it, and they remember what you taught. The risk is handing somebody the whole structure when they needed one step.
Analytical|Teaching.ask: Who got the full picture when they asked one question?

Analytical|Tongues.recognize: You are honest about what you cannot account for instead of pretending, and that honesty is worth more than manufactured enthusiasm. What it can become is a standing reason to stay outside anything you cannot map.
Analytical|Tongues.ask: What have you kept at arm's length because it does not resolve?

Analytical|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you the tangled thing because you can lay the pieces out. The limit shows when what is needed is not a better breakdown but a decision made this week.
Analytical|Wisdom.ask: What advice have you given that needed a deadline attached?

Bold|Administration.recognize: You make the call the committee has been going around for a month, and the thing finally moves. What follows is the cleanup, because the call was made without the paperwork behind it.
Bold|Administration.ask: Who cleaned up after your last fast decision?

Bold|Apostleship.recognize: You go first into the place that has nothing, and your going is the reason anybody else comes. The cost lands on the second wave, who arrive to something you have already left.
Bold|Apostleship.ask: What did you begin that somebody else had to finish?

Bold|Discernment.recognize: You act on your read of a person immediately instead of waiting, and you are right often enough that it works. The times it does not are the times you never checked.
Bold|Discernment.ask: When was your first impression of someone flatly wrong?

Bold|Evangelism.recognize: You will start the conversation nobody else will start, and people respect that even when they disagree. The risk is walking into a heart at the pace you walk into a room.
Bold|Evangelism.ask: Who did you push too fast last month?

Bold|Exhortation.recognize: You tell people to go before they feel ready, and some of them go and are changed by it. The others were not stalling, they were genuinely not ready, and your push cost them.
Bold|Exhortation.ask: Who did you send who was not ready?

Bold|Faith.recognize: You will step out with nothing underneath you, and it is the reason people around you believe God moves. Watch for the step you took because you enjoy stepping rather than because you were sent.
Bold|Faith.ask: What did you step into that God never asked of you?

Bold|Giving.recognize: You give an amount that makes other people uncomfortable, and it frees something in the room. The exposure is that a decision made at speed is still binding on everyone who depends on you.
Bold|Giving.ask: Who else was affected by your last large gift?

Bold|Healing.recognize: You will walk into the hospital room or the argument that everybody else has been avoiding, and your presence is most of what was needed. What you skip is asking before you enter.
Bold|Healing.ask: Whose situation did you walk into uninvited?

Bold|Interpretation.recognize: You will say plainly what everyone has been going around, and the naming is a relief to the room. Sometimes what you named was yours and not theirs.
Bold|Interpretation.ask: What did you announce that the room had not agreed to?

Bold|Knowledge.recognize: You ask the question everybody considers off limits, and the answer often matters. The damage is done when the person was not ready for it to be asked in front of others.
Bold|Knowledge.ask: What did you ask publicly that should have been private?

Bold|Leadership.recognize: You pick up responsibility in a vacuum before anybody appoints you, and things move because of it. The problem arrives when the vacuum was not real and somebody was already carrying it.
Bold|Leadership.ask: Whose role did you step into without asking?

Bold|Mercy.recognize: You go straight at somebody's pain instead of tiptoeing, and many people find that a relief after weeks of careful voices. Others needed the careful voice.
Bold|Mercy.ask: Who flinched the last time you were direct about their loss?

Bold|Miracles.recognize: You will pray the specific prayer out loud with people listening, which is rarer than it should be and builds faith in a room. It also puts other people's disappointment on your account.
Bold|Miracles.ask: What did you pray for publicly that did not happen?

Bold|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You will go after the person who is drifting instead of hoping they come back, and many do come back because of it. The one who does not is often the one who needed a slower approach.
Bold|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who left after you went after them?

Bold|Prophecy.recognize: You say it in the room, at the time, to the face, and people change because of it. What you rarely measure is how long the person needed afterward to recover.
Bold|Prophecy.ask: Who needed weeks to recover from a conversation with you?

Bold|Service.recognize: You see the job and start it without a meeting about it, and whole days get saved this way. Where it costs is when the job was already assigned to somebody who wanted it.
Bold|Service.ask: Whose task did you take over this month?

Bold|Teaching.recognize: You will teach the passage everybody else avoids, and people come because of it. The exposure is going into a subject at full speed with the preparation of a subject you already know.
Bold|Teaching.ask: What did you teach that you had not studied enough?

Bold|Tongues.recognize: You will look foolish in front of people if you believe it is from God, and that freedom gives everyone else permission. Worth examining is how much of it is faith and how much is that you enjoy not minding.
Bold|Tongues.ask: When were you last genuinely embarrassed?

Bold|Wisdom.recognize: You move while other people are still weighing it, and often the move was right. The cases worth revisiting are the ones where waiting a week was the entire answer and you did not have a week in you.
Bold|Wisdom.ask: What would have solved itself if you had waited?

Calm and Practical|Administration.recognize: The thing runs because you do the unremarkable parts on time, every time, without being watched. What that steadiness hides is that you will work around a broken process for years rather than raise it.
Calm and Practical|Administration.ask: What have you been working around instead of fixing?

Calm and Practical|Apostleship.recognize: You are who they send when the new thing is chaos, because chaos does not move you. The limit is that a new thing sometimes needs urgency and you supply the opposite.
Calm and Practical|Apostleship.ask: What needed to happen faster than you let it?

Calm and Practical|Discernment.recognize: You form a read slowly and it is usually sound. Where it costs is when you can tell something is wrong and decide it is not yet big enough to mention.
Calm and Practical|Discernment.ask: What is wrong that you have decided is not big enough yet?

Calm and Practical|Evangelism.recognize: Your life is the argument, and people who never respond to enthusiasm respond to you. What you may be avoiding is that being steady does not require being silent.
Calm and Practical|Evangelism.ask: Who have you known for years and never actually asked?

Calm and Practical|Exhortation.recognize: You give people confidence by being unbothered when they are not. The gap shows when somebody needed you to be as alarmed as they were, and you were not.
Calm and Practical|Exhortation.ask: Who felt dismissed the last time you stayed level?

Calm and Practical|Faith.recognize: You keep going when the outcome is unclear, without needing a feeling to sustain it, and that holds up over decades. What it can quietly become is a low ceiling on what you will ask for.
Calm and Practical|Faith.ask: What have you stopped asking God for?

Calm and Practical|Giving.recognize: You give on a plan rather than in reaction to appeals, and over ten years your total is larger than the dramatic givers. What you rarely do is the unplanned thing that meets tonight's need.
Calm and Practical|Giving.ask: When did you last give outside your plan?

Calm and Practical|Healing.recognize: People want you in the room in a crisis because nothing about you escalates. The cost is that some wounds need somebody to be angry on your behalf, and you will not be.
Calm and Practical|Healing.ask: Whose anger did you smooth over that deserved to be spoken?

Calm and Practical|Interpretation.recognize: You put a plain version of a complicated situation in front of people and the panic drops. Where it misses is when the situation genuinely was as bad as they thought.
Calm and Practical|Interpretation.ask: What did you make sound smaller than it was?

Calm and Practical|Knowledge.recognize: You keep what is useful and let the rest go, and you can produce it years later at the moment it is needed. The waste is everything you know and never mention because nobody asked.
Calm and Practical|Knowledge.ask: What do you know that nobody has thought to ask you?

Calm and Practical|Leadership.recognize: People follow you because nothing rattles you and the plan does not change weekly. The ceiling is that a team who never sees urgency in you will not generate it on their own.
Calm and Practical|Leadership.ask: When did your team last see you concerned?

Calm and Practical|Mercy.recognize: You stay through the long unglamorous part of somebody's suffering, months after the casseroles stop. What you may skip is the acute hour, where a level voice can read as not caring.
Calm and Practical|Mercy.ask: Who needed you to react and got your composure?

Calm and Practical|Miracles.recognize: You are not swept along by atmosphere, so when you say God did something, people take it seriously. Worth checking is whether the bar you set for calling something God is now so high that nothing clears it.
Calm and Practical|Miracles.ask: What would God have to do for you to call it a miracle?

Calm and Practical|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You are constant, and people who have been let down by unreliable care can rest in it. What they may not get from you is any sense that they were missed.
Calm and Practical|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: When did you last tell somebody you noticed they were gone?

Calm and Practical|Prophecy.recognize: When you finally say the hard thing, people believe it, because you are not someone who says hard things often. The cost of that credibility is how much you let pass to keep it.
Calm and Practical|Prophecy.ask: How many times did you let it go before you spoke?

Calm and Practical|Service.recognize: You work at the same pace whether anybody is watching or the deadline is tomorrow, and nothing you touch has to be done twice. Where it costs is the emergency, which needs a gear you do not carry.
Calm and Practical|Service.ask: When did your steadiness make something late?

Calm and Practical|Teaching.recognize: You teach in a way people can use on Monday, with no theatre in it. The risk is that a room which is never stirred rarely changes.
Calm and Practical|Teaching.ask: When did something you taught actually move somebody?

Calm and Practical|Tongues.recognize: You are not chasing an experience, so what you do have is not manufactured. What that can harden into is a standing suspicion of anything you cannot picture happening quietly.
Calm and Practical|Tongues.ask: Which expression of faith makes you uncomfortable, and why?

Calm and Practical|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you things because you will not react, and your advice holds up years later. The limit is that some decisions need heat and yours arrive at room temperature.
Calm and Practical|Wisdom.ask: What advice of yours was right and went unheeded?

Charismatic|Administration.recognize: You can get people to sign up for something that is not built yet, which is worth more than it sounds. The bill comes when they arrive and find nothing behind the invitation.
Charismatic|Administration.ask: What have you recruited people into that is not ready?

Charismatic|Apostleship.recognize: You can gather a room in a town where nobody knows you, inside a week. That is genuinely rare. The question is who holds it together when you are three towns away.
Charismatic|Apostleship.ask: Who leads the group you gathered last year?

Charismatic|Discernment.recognize: You read people quickly and adjust in real time, so conversations go well. Watch for the moment adjusting becomes agreeing, and you leave having said nothing you meant.
Charismatic|Discernment.ask: When did you last disagree with someone to their face?

Charismatic|Evangelism.recognize: People want to be near you, so they will hear it from you when they would hear it from nobody else. The risk is that they responded to you, and from the front you cannot tell the difference.
Charismatic|Evangelism.ask: Who followed you and not Christ?

Charismatic|Exhortation.recognize: One sentence from you changes somebody's week, which is a real thing to be able to do. What you may not track is how many people are now waiting on their next sentence from you.
Charismatic|Exhortation.ask: Who leans on your encouragement more than is healthy?

Charismatic|Faith.recognize: You can make a room believe a thing is possible, and belief in a room is not nothing. The exposure is that your confidence spreads before you have checked whether it was warranted.
Charismatic|Faith.ask: What did you talk a group into that you were unsure of?

Charismatic|Giving.recognize: You can raise money nobody else can raise, and the cause is better off for it. What deserves examining is how much of the yes was the cause and how much was you asking.
Charismatic|Giving.ask: Would that gift have come if somebody else had asked?

Charismatic|Healing.recognize: People open up to you fast, which puts you inside things it takes others years to reach. The danger is the depth of what gets told and the shallowness of the follow-up.
Charismatic|Healing.ask: Who told you something serious that you never returned to?

Charismatic|Interpretation.recognize: You can make a hard idea land for a room that would not sit still for anybody else. The slip is when a thing becomes true in your mouth because of how well you said it.
Charismatic|Interpretation.ask: What have you said well that you had not thought through?

Charismatic|Knowledge.recognize: You can hold a room on a subject with a fraction of the preparation other people need. That is a real ability and also the trap, because the room cannot tell.
Charismatic|Knowledge.ask: Where are you running on presence instead of study?

Charismatic|Leadership.recognize: People will go where you go without needing the reasons, which lets you move faster than most leaders. The exposure is a team built on your personality rather than the mission.
Charismatic|Leadership.ask: What happens to your team if you leave?

Charismatic|Mercy.recognize: You make a hurting person feel singled out and truly seen, which few can do. The strain is that being seen this way is a spotlight, and spotlights move on.
Charismatic|Mercy.ask: Who did you make feel important and then not call?

Charismatic|Miracles.recognize: Faith rises in a room you are in, and that is often exactly where God moves. The line worth watching is the one between real expectancy and an atmosphere you generated yourself.
Charismatic|Miracles.ask: How would you know the difference in that room?

Charismatic|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Everybody feels close to you. The arithmetic problem is that a hundred people believe they have a relationship with you and you have capacity for twelve.
Charismatic|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: How many people think they are close to you?

Charismatic|Prophecy.recognize: You can say something confronting and keep the person, because they know you like them. That is rare and useful. It also means you can soften a word until it costs nothing.
Charismatic|Prophecy.ask: What did you take the edge off to stay liked?

Charismatic|Service.recognize: When you turn up to work, other people turn up, and the job takes half the time. Where it thins out is the jobs nobody sees, which get no benefit from your being there.
Charismatic|Service.ask: What have you skipped because nobody was there to see it?

Charismatic|Teaching.recognize: People remember your sessions, and being remembered is most of the battle. The check is whether they remember the content or the hour.
Charismatic|Teaching.ask: What did somebody take away from your last talk?

Charismatic|Tongues.recognize: You are comfortable expressing faith in front of people, and that frees a room to do the same. The examination is whether being in front of people has become the reason for it.
Charismatic|Tongues.ask: What does your faith look like when nobody is watching?

Charismatic|Wisdom.recognize: People take your advice because of how you say it, which means your advice had better be good. The danger is that yours is rarely questioned.
Charismatic|Wisdom.ask: Who tells you when you are wrong?

Charming|Administration.recognize: Hard conversations about process go smoothly with you in the room, which is why you keep being put in the room. The cost is that the smooth version is often the one where nothing got decided.
Charming|Administration.ask: What has been pleasant and unresolved for a month?

Charming|Apostleship.recognize: You can arrive anywhere and be welcomed inside a day, which is a serious advantage in new work. The question is what you build once the welcoming is over.
Charming|Apostleship.ask: What have you started that outlasted the introductions?

Charming|Discernment.recognize: You read what a person wants and give it to them, so almost nobody dislikes you. What you may be avoiding is that you also read what they need, and choose the other one.
Charming|Discernment.ask: Who did you tell what they wanted to hear?

Charming|Evangelism.recognize: You get to a spiritual conversation without it feeling like one, which carries you further than most. Where it stops is the moment it turns uncomfortable, because you are very good at getting out.
Charming|Evangelism.ask: When did you last let a conversation stay awkward?

Charming|Exhortation.recognize: You lift people without effort and they leave lighter than they came. What does not happen is the harder encouragement, which requires the room to be tense first.
Charming|Exhortation.ask: Who needed a challenge from you and got a compliment?

Charming|Faith.recognize: You can hold a group steady when things are uncertain, because nothing feels like a crisis around you. The exposure is that uncertainty deserves to be felt sometimes, including by you.
Charming|Faith.ask: What are you worried about that you have made light of?

Charming|Giving.recognize: You are generous in ways that cost little and land well, and people feel cared for. Worth weighing is the ratio between how generous you seem and what you have actually gone without.
Charming|Giving.ask: What did your last act of generosity cost you?

Charming|Healing.recognize: You can put somebody at rest inside a few minutes, which is the doorway to everything else. But the doorway is not the room, and you spend most of your time in doorways.
Charming|Healing.ask: Who have you put at rest without ever asking what happened?

Charming|Interpretation.recognize: You can restate a conflict so both sides relax. Sometimes the restatement was true. Sometimes it was only easier to hear, and the conflict is still sitting there.
Charming|Interpretation.ask: What disagreement did you smooth over that is still live?

Charming|Knowledge.recognize: You can carry a conversation on nearly anything, and people assume you know more than you have claimed. You have never had to correct that assumption.
Charming|Knowledge.ask: What are you assumed to be an expert in and are not?

Charming|Leadership.recognize: You get cooperation without conflict, which makes you pleasant to work for. The gap is what happens when cooperation is not enough and somebody has to be told no.
Charming|Leadership.ask: Who should have heard no from you this quarter?

Charming|Mercy.recognize: You are easy to be sad around, which is rarer than it sounds. The limit is grief that is ugly rather than sad, and does not respond to lightness.
Charming|Mercy.ask: Whose grief have you not been able to stay near?

Charming|Miracles.recognize: You can hold a room's attention while something unusual happens and keep it from tipping into spectacle. Worth checking is whether you are managing the room instead of seeking God in it.
Charming|Miracles.ask: What are you managing that you should be praying about?

Charming|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People come back to you because being with you is not hard work. The care that is hard work is the care that changes somebody, and you have to choose it deliberately.
Charming|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Which relationship have you kept pleasant instead of honest?

Charming|Prophecy.recognize: You can say a difficult thing so gracefully that it does not offend anybody. The question is whether it also did not land.
Charming|Prophecy.ask: What have you said so kindly that it changed nothing?

Charming|Service.recognize: You make working alongside you enjoyable, and volunteers come back because of it. What is easy to miss is that a good hour and a finished job are not the same thing.
Charming|Service.ask: What is still unfinished from a good day of work?

Charming|Teaching.recognize: Nobody is bored in your class. The measure is what anyone can do differently on Wednesday.
Charming|Teaching.ask: What has somebody changed because of your teaching?

Charming|Tongues.recognize: You move through unfamiliar spiritual settings without discomfort, and that adaptability is real. The risk is a faith that fits every room and is never inconvenient in any of them.
Charming|Tongues.ask: Where has your faith cost you socially?

Charming|Wisdom.recognize: People find your advice easy to take, which means more of it gets used. The counterweight is the advice that should be hard to take, and whether you ever give it.
Charming|Wisdom.ask: What have you softened that should have stayed sharp?

Clear Communication|Administration.recognize: Your instructions do not need a follow-up email. People know what to do and by when. What gets lost is the reasoning, so the team executes well and cannot adapt when the situation shifts.
Clear Communication|Administration.ask: Who on your team could explain why, not just what?

Clear Communication|Apostleship.recognize: You can describe a thing that does not exist yet in a way people can picture, which is how new work gets funded and staffed. The gap is that the picture is always tidier than the ground.
Clear Communication|Apostleship.ask: What did you describe that turned out messier on arrival?

Clear Communication|Discernment.recognize: You name what you notice about a person out loud, and half the time it unlocks them. The other half, you named something you were eighty percent sure of as though it were settled.
Clear Communication|Discernment.ask: What did you say about somebody that you were not actually certain of?

Clear Communication|Evangelism.recognize: You can explain the gospel without jargon to somebody who has never been inside a church, which is rarer among church people than it should be. Watch for the version so tidy it no longer costs anything.
Clear Communication|Evangelism.ask: When did your explanation last make somebody uncomfortable?

Clear Communication|Exhortation.recognize: You tell people exactly what you see in them with no hedging, and they believe you because you are not a flatterer. The risk is delivering a verdict when they needed a conversation.
Clear Communication|Exhortation.ask: Who got your assessment when they needed your time?

Clear Communication|Faith.recognize: You can put what you believe into words other people are able to carry, and it steadies them. Where it thins is that the parts of faith which resist wording get left out of your account entirely.
Clear Communication|Faith.ask: What do you believe that you cannot put cleanly into words?

Clear Communication|Giving.recognize: You are direct about money where most people go vague, which is why your generosity actually reaches what you intended. The friction is that being this clear can land on the receiving end as a transaction.
Clear Communication|Giving.ask: Who felt like a line item the last time you helped?

Clear Communication|Healing.recognize: You can say the true thing about somebody's situation without dressing it up, and there is real relief in hearing it named. What that skips is the long part, where nothing needs saying at all.
Clear Communication|Healing.ask: When did you last stay quiet with somebody who was hurting?

Clear Communication|Interpretation.recognize: You take the confusing thing and hand it back in a sentence people can repeat, and they do repeat it. The danger is that your sentence becomes the official version and whatever it left out stops existing.
Clear Communication|Interpretation.ask: What got dropped from the short version everyone now uses?

Clear Communication|Knowledge.recognize: You can hand somebody a finding without the forty pages behind it, and that is a service. It also means people trust conclusions they have never seen the working for.
Clear Communication|Knowledge.ask: Which conclusion of yours has nobody ever checked?

Clear Communication|Leadership.recognize: Nobody leaves your meetings unsure what happens next, and that is most of leading. The exposure is that a team clear on the plan is not the same as a team who believes in it.
Clear Communication|Leadership.ask: Who is doing what you asked without agreeing with it?

Clear Communication|Mercy.recognize: You give somebody in pain a straight account while everyone else is circling, and more often than not that is the kindest thing available to them. Sometimes straight is simply early.
Clear Communication|Mercy.ask: Who was not ready to hear what you said?

Clear Communication|Miracles.recognize: You say specifically what you are asking God for, which makes it possible to know whether it happened. That honesty is rare. The pressure it creates lands on you when it does not.
Clear Communication|Miracles.ask: What did you name out loud that you now avoid mentioning?

Clear Communication|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People always know where they stand with you, which is a kind of safety most leaders never manage to provide. What can be missing is the unspoken side of care, which does not survive being made explicit.
Clear Communication|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needs something from you that has never been said aloud?

Clear Communication|Prophecy.recognize: You can put a hard reality into one sentence and it reaches everybody in the room at once. The cost is that a sentence cannot carry the care a paragraph would have.
Clear Communication|Prophecy.ask: What did you say in one line that deserved ten?

Clear Communication|Service.recognize: You ask exactly what is needed and then do exactly that, so nothing gets wasted. Where it costs is the person who could not have told you what they needed.
Clear Communication|Service.ask: Who could not answer when you asked what they needed?

Clear Communication|Teaching.recognize: Students can put what you taught into their own words on the drive home, and being able to say it is the start of owning it. The question is whether the version they carry is the whole one.
Clear Communication|Teaching.ask: What have you left out to keep it simple?

Clear Communication|Tongues.recognize: You are honest about what you do and do not experience, and that keeps a room from pretending. The blind spot is that some things are real before anybody can describe them.
Clear Communication|Tongues.ask: What have you dismissed because nobody could put it into words?

Clear Communication|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is usable, which is more than most advice manages. What can go missing is the hesitation, because some situations are genuinely unresolved until they have been lived.
Clear Communication|Wisdom.ask: What did you answer quickly that deserved a slower reply?

Creative|Administration.recognize: You will redesign a form nobody asked you to redesign, and the new one is better. The friction is with the people who had finally learned the old one.
Creative|Administration.ask: What did you improve that somebody else had to relearn?

Creative|Apostleship.recognize: New ground is where your ideas have room, and you are genuinely useful in it. The pattern to watch is the moment a new work turns into maintenance and stops holding your attention.
Creative|Apostleship.ask: What stopped interesting you once it started working?

Creative|Discernment.recognize: You catch that something is off before you can say why, because you notice form and something in the shape was wrong. The risk is calling a person wrong when what bothered you was style.
Creative|Discernment.ask: What did you mistrust that was only unfamiliar?

Creative|Evangelism.recognize: You find ways into the conversation nobody else would try, and they work on people who are tired of the standard version. Watch for making it interesting to yourself rather than clear to them.
Creative|Evangelism.ask: Who found your approach clever instead of compelling?

Creative|Exhortation.recognize: You can show a person a picture of who they might become, and pictures move people that advice does not. The exposure is when your picture of them is grander than anything they asked for.
Creative|Exhortation.ask: Whose future have you been more excited about than they are?

Creative|Faith.recognize: You can imagine what God might do here, and imagination is often the first step of obedience. The line worth watching runs between what you were shown and what you thought up.
Creative|Faith.ask: What plan of yours have you been calling God's?

Creative|Giving.recognize: Your generosity takes forms other people would not think of, and it fits the person rather than the category. The cost is that an unusual gift can end up being more about the giving than the need.
Creative|Giving.ask: What did you give that was more interesting than useful?

Creative|Healing.recognize: You find ways for somebody to say what they could not say straight, and that opens what nothing else opens. The care required is that a person is not a project.
Creative|Healing.ask: Whose story have you been arranging?

Creative|Interpretation.recognize: You give people images for what they are living through, and an image sticks where an explanation slides off. The danger is that your image is memorable and slightly wrong.
Creative|Interpretation.ask: What picture did you give somebody that they took too literally?

Creative|Knowledge.recognize: You connect things that are not usually connected, and some of those connections are real discoveries. Others are merely pleasing.
Creative|Knowledge.ask: Which of your connections has anyone else confirmed?

Creative|Leadership.recognize: You give people something to build that they had not imagined, and that pulls harder than a target does. The problem is that a team cannot follow something that changes whenever you get bored.
Creative|Leadership.ask: How many times has the plan changed this year?

Creative|Mercy.recognize: You find a way to be present that fits the particular person rather than the standard casserole. Where it goes wrong is when the effort is visible and they now have to appreciate it.
Creative|Mercy.ask: Who had to thank you for something they did not need?

Creative|Miracles.recognize: You look for God to do something you have not seen before, and that hope is not a small thing. What to watch is preferring the unusual answer to the plain one.
Creative|Miracles.ask: Would an ordinary answer disappoint you?

Creative|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You care for people in ways fitted to them specifically, and they feel known rather than processed. What slips is the repetitive side of care, which has no room for invention.
Creative|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needs the same boring check-in every week?

Creative|Prophecy.recognize: You can put a hard word into a form people will actually receive, getting past defenses a direct statement would raise. The risk is that a beautiful delivery gets admired instead of obeyed.
Creative|Prophecy.ask: Who complimented you on something that should have convicted them?

Creative|Service.recognize: You find a better way to do the job while doing it, and the next person benefits. The friction is that you were asked to do the job, not to change it.
Creative|Service.ask: What did you rework that was fine as it was?

Creative|Teaching.recognize: People remember your illustrations for years, and the illustration is often how the truth got in. The check is whether they remember the illustration or what it was for.
Creative|Teaching.ask: What do people quote back to you, and does it still carry the point?

Creative|Tongues.recognize: You are comfortable at the edge of what can be put into words, which is exactly where this operates. What deserves examination is enjoying the mystery for its own sake.
Creative|Tongues.ask: What would be lost if this became ordinary to you?

Creative|Wisdom.recognize: You see options nobody else had listed, and often the third one is right. The limit is that some decisions have exactly two options and inventing a third is avoidance.
Creative|Wisdom.ask: What choice have you been avoiding by looking for another way?

Curious|Administration.recognize: You want to know why a process exists before you follow it, and sometimes the answer is that nobody knows. Your questions have retired real waste. They have also held up things that only needed doing.
Curious|Administration.ask: What did you hold up asking about?

Curious|Apostleship.recognize: Unfamiliar ground energises you, so you will go where others will not. The pattern is that the next unfamiliar place always looks more interesting than the one you are standing in.
Curious|Apostleship.ask: How long do you usually stay?

Curious|Discernment.recognize: You keep asking about a person until something real comes out, and it usually does. The care needed is that not every silence is hiding something.
Curious|Discernment.ask: Who did you keep questioning after they had answered?

Curious|Evangelism.recognize: You are genuinely interested in what people believe, and that interest opens conversations arguing would close. Watch for the conversation you enjoyed so much that you never said anything.
Curious|Evangelism.ask: Who did you find fascinating and never actually tell?

Curious|Exhortation.recognize: You ask people about themselves until they hear their own answer, which does more than encouragement usually does. The gap is when somebody needed a statement rather than another question.
Curious|Exhortation.ask: Who needed you to tell them something plainly?

Curious|Faith.recognize: You are comfortable with what you do not understand about God, and it keeps you from small answers. The line to watch is where investigating becomes a way of not deciding.
Curious|Faith.ask: What have you been examining instead of obeying?

Curious|Giving.recognize: You want to understand a need properly before you meet it, and your generosity is well aimed because of it. The risk is that the understanding is interesting and the meeting keeps not happening.
Curious|Giving.ask: What have you learned all about and never given to?

Curious|Healing.recognize: You ask the questions that get somebody to the actual thing, past whatever they came in with. What that requires is knowing when to stop, because there is always another layer.
Curious|Healing.ask: When did you keep going past what they could handle?

Curious|Interpretation.recognize: You want to know what something actually signified rather than settling for the surface, and you often get there. The danger is treating a person's plain statement as a puzzle.
Curious|Interpretation.ask: What did somebody say plainly that you decided was code?

Curious|Knowledge.recognize: You will follow a subject for months because it interests you, and you end up genuinely expert. The waste is the six subjects you got two-thirds through.
Curious|Knowledge.ask: What did you abandon at the point it stopped being new?

Curious|Leadership.recognize: You ask better questions than most leaders make statements, and it lifts the thinking of everyone around you. The cost is a team who cannot tell whether a decision has been made.
Curious|Leadership.ask: What does your team think is still open that you closed?

Curious|Mercy.recognize: You want to know what somebody actually went through rather than assuming, and being asked is itself a kindness to most people. Some pain does not want an interviewer.
Curious|Mercy.ask: Who did you ask one question too many?

Curious|Miracles.recognize: You are drawn to what cannot be explained rather than unsettled by it, and that openness is where faith often begins. What to check is whether you are seeking God or seeking the unexplained.
Curious|Miracles.ask: Which of those do you want more?

Curious|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know things about the people in your care that they have told nobody else, because you asked and kept asking. What goes missing is the ordinary steady part, which requires no discovery.
Curious|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who have you known for years and stopped asking anything new?

Curious|Prophecy.recognize: You ask the question that surfaces what the room was avoiding, without having to accuse anybody, and it is a gentler route to the same place. The risk is asking because you want to see what happens.
Curious|Prophecy.ask: What did you raise mainly because you wanted to watch?

Curious|Service.recognize: You are interested in the work itself, which makes you good at jobs other people find dull. The pattern is that the interest runs out before the job does.
Curious|Service.ask: What did you leave half done once you understood it?

Curious|Teaching.recognize: You teach out of what you are currently learning, so it is alive rather than recycled. The strain falls on students who need last year's material taught again.
Curious|Teaching.ask: What do you need to teach again even though you are done with it?

Curious|Tongues.recognize: You move toward the parts of faith that resist explanation rather than avoiding them. What deserves attention is whether you are participating or observing.
Curious|Tongues.ask: When did you last stop studying it and simply do it?

Curious|Wisdom.recognize: You gather far more of a situation than most people bother with before saying anything, and it makes what you say worth more. The limit is that some questions are not answered by more information.
Curious|Wisdom.ask: What are you still researching after the answer arrived?

Decisive Action|Administration.recognize: You will close the open item that has sat on the list for six weeks, and the whole list moves. What can be lost is the reason it was open, which was occasionally a real objection.
Decisive Action|Administration.ask: What did you close that somebody had a concern about?

Decisive Action|Apostleship.recognize: You will start the new work before conditions are right, and conditions are never right. The cost is whatever option you eliminated by moving, which nobody will ever know about.
Decisive Action|Apostleship.ask: What else could this have been if you had waited a month?

Decisive Action|Discernment.recognize: You act on what you sense about a person quickly, which spares everybody weeks of drift. The exposure is that a first read hardens into a verdict once you have acted on it.
Decisive Action|Discernment.ask: Who have you never revised your opinion of?

Decisive Action|Evangelism.recognize: You ask for a response rather than leaving it open, and people appreciate being asked more often than not. The care needed is that a choice pressed early can close something that needed to stay open.
Decisive Action|Evangelism.ask: Who said yes to you before they understood?

Decisive Action|Exhortation.recognize: You tell somebody what to do next and they do it, because you sound like you know. The weight of that is that you are often choosing for people who were capable of choosing.
Decisive Action|Exhortation.ask: Who have you been making decisions for?

Decisive Action|Faith.recognize: You will move on what you believe God said without waiting for a confirmation, and that is real obedience. The pattern to check is whether the speed is faith or discomfort with waiting.
Decisive Action|Faith.ask: How long can you sit with an unanswered question?

Decisive Action|Giving.recognize: You decide and transfer, so needs get met while other people are still discussing them. The exposure is a yes given at speed that constrains a later yes you cared about more.
Decisive Action|Giving.ask: What could you not do because of an earlier quick yes?

Decisive Action|Healing.recognize: You get somebody into treatment, out of the house, to the appointment, while everyone else is still talking about it. What that can skip is whether they were ready to be moved.
Decisive Action|Healing.ask: Who did you move before they chose to?

Decisive Action|Interpretation.recognize: You settle what a confusing situation was about so the group can proceed, and proceeding matters. The risk is that your settlement becomes the record when it was one reading.
Decisive Action|Interpretation.ask: What have you declared settled that others still question?

Decisive Action|Knowledge.recognize: You know when you have enough to act, which most thorough people never learn. Where it costs is the piece that would have arrived next week and changed everything.
Decisive Action|Knowledge.ask: What did you find out afterward that you would have wanted first?

Decisive Action|Leadership.recognize: Your team is never stuck, because you will choose. The exposure is that a group who never has to decide loses the capacity to.
Decisive Action|Leadership.ask: When did you last let your team make the call?

Decisive Action|Mercy.recognize: You do something rather than say something, and for many people in pain that is the whole difference. The gap is the situation where nothing can be done and you have to stay anyway.
Decisive Action|Mercy.ask: Where have you been unable to fix anything, and did you stay?

Decisive Action|Miracles.recognize: You act as though the answer is coming and arrange things accordingly, which is often what expectant faith looks like. Watch for the point where arranging replaces asking.
Decisive Action|Miracles.ask: What have you handled that you should have prayed about?

Decisive Action|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You step in early, before a small drift becomes a departure, and people stay because of it. The risk is stepping into something that was theirs to work out.
Decisive Action|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Whose situation did you enter that was not yours?

Decisive Action|Prophecy.recognize: You say it and then live with having said it, without the long agonising afterward, and that steadiness is a gift to whoever heard it. What it can skip is whether the timing was theirs.
Decisive Action|Prophecy.ask: Whose readiness did you not wait for?

Decisive Action|Service.recognize: The thing gets done because you started it rather than scheduling it. Where it costs is the coordination you skipped, which somebody else then had to redo.
Decisive Action|Service.ask: What had to be redone because you went first?

Decisive Action|Teaching.recognize: You will answer the hard question directly instead of leaving it hanging, and students trust that. The risk is closing off an area a person needed to sit inside for a while.
Decisive Action|Teaching.ask: Whose question did you answer too well?

Decisive Action|Tongues.recognize: You step into things you cannot control without needing to think it over. The examination is whether that is trust or momentum.
Decisive Action|Tongues.ask: What would it take for you to hesitate?

Decisive Action|Wisdom.recognize: You will call the moment, and calling the moment is half of wisdom. The other half is the situation that only resolves with time, which cannot be brought forward by choosing.
Decisive Action|Wisdom.ask: What have you tried to settle that is not ready?

Dedicated|Administration.recognize: You keep the thing running for years after whoever started it left, and it runs because of you. What nobody examines is whether it should still be running.
Dedicated|Administration.ask: What are you maintaining that should have ended?

Dedicated|Apostleship.recognize: You stay with the new work through the years when nothing visible happens, which is when most new works die. The risk is staying past the point where staying became the point.
Dedicated|Apostleship.ask: What would have to happen for you to leave?

Dedicated|Discernment.recognize: You have watched people long enough to know the difference between a bad week and a pattern, and that cannot be shortcut. Where it costs is holding an old read of somebody who has changed.
Dedicated|Discernment.ask: Who have you not updated your view of?

Dedicated|Evangelism.recognize: You are still praying for the same person after eleven years, and one day they may walk in because of it. What can happen is that the praying quietly becomes the relationship.
Dedicated|Evangelism.ask: When did you last actually talk to them?

Dedicated|Exhortation.recognize: You keep showing up for a person long after everybody else stopped, and being kept on somebody's list is itself a message. The blind spot is the thing you have said so long it has become background.
Dedicated|Exhortation.ask: Who has stopped hearing you because you always say it?

Dedicated|Faith.recognize: You hold on through years of nothing, which is the version of faith Scripture spends most of its pages on. The check is whether you are still asking or only enduring.
Dedicated|Faith.ask: When did you last ask God for something new?

Dedicated|Giving.recognize: You have given to the same work for a decade, and steady money is what actually builds things. What deserves review is whether it still does what it did when you started.
Dedicated|Giving.ask: When did you last look at what they do with it?

Dedicated|Healing.recognize: You are there in month fourteen, when the meals stopped in week three, and that is where most of it actually happens. The cost lands on the other parts of your life that got nothing.
Dedicated|Healing.ask: What have you neglected while carrying this?

Dedicated|Interpretation.recognize: You have watched something long enough to say what it actually was, which nobody with less time could do. The risk is defending an old account of events because you have held it so long.
Dedicated|Interpretation.ask: Which old story is yours, and who would tell it differently?

Dedicated|Knowledge.recognize: You keep working the same subject and end up knowing it the way few people know anything. What can happen is that it stopped being useful and you kept going.
Dedicated|Knowledge.ask: What have you mastered that nobody needs?

Dedicated|Leadership.recognize: You have led the same group through everything, and the group is what it is because you did not leave. The exposure is that nobody has ever had to grow into your place.
Dedicated|Leadership.ask: Who would step up if you stopped?

Dedicated|Mercy.recognize: You stay with the person everybody else wrote off, year after year, and that is rare. The question is whether staying has come to include accepting harm.
Dedicated|Mercy.ask: What have you tolerated that you would tell a friend to leave?

Dedicated|Miracles.recognize: You have prayed the same prayer for years without stopping, which is exactly the posture the parable commends. Worth checking is whether you still anticipate an answer or only keep the habit.
Dedicated|Miracles.ask: Do you still believe it could happen?

Dedicated|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know the family across three generations because you never went anywhere, and nobody can manufacture that. What it costs is the newcomer, who arrives into a history they are not in.
Dedicated|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who is new and still on the outside?

Dedicated|Prophecy.recognize: You have said the same true thing for years and been ignored for most of them, and you kept saying it. Sometimes that is faithfulness. Sometimes the word stopped fitting and you did not notice.
Dedicated|Prophecy.ask: Is what you are saying still the right word for now?

Dedicated|Service.recognize: You have done the same job every week for years without being asked twice, and whole ministries stand on people like you. What nobody asks is what it has cost at home.
Dedicated|Service.ask: What has your family given up for this?

Dedicated|Teaching.recognize: You have taught the same group long enough to see what took root, which most teachers never get. The risk is teaching from what worked in 2014.
Dedicated|Teaching.ask: What in your material have you not changed in five years?

Dedicated|Tongues.recognize: You practise this when there is no meeting and no audience, which is where it is actually formed. What can settle in is habit without hunger.
Dedicated|Tongues.ask: When did this last feel alive rather than familiar?

Dedicated|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you because you have been through what they are in, and lived experience carries what advice cannot. The limit is that their version may not be yours.
Dedicated|Wisdom.ask: What is different about their situation from yours?

Determined|Administration.recognize: You get the process approved after four rejections, because you kept bringing it back. What deserves examination is which of those attempts were about the process and which were about the rejection.
Determined|Administration.ask: What are you pursuing that you have stopped evaluating?

Determined|Apostleship.recognize: You keep the new work alive through the stretch where it should have died, and that is often the whole reason anything exists. The risk is the one that genuinely should have ended.
Determined|Apostleship.ask: What are you keeping alive by force?

Determined|Discernment.recognize: Once you have concluded something about a person you do not let it go easily, and that steadiness keeps you from being played. It also means new evidence has a hard time reaching you.
Determined|Discernment.ask: What would change your mind about them?

Determined|Evangelism.recognize: You go back to the same person a seventh time, and the seventh is sometimes the one. The line is where persistence stops being love and becomes a project.
Determined|Evangelism.ask: Have you asked whether they want to keep talking about it?

Determined|Exhortation.recognize: You do not let somebody quit on themselves, and people have finished things because you would not accept their resignation. The care needed is that some people are not quitting, they are being honest about capacity.
Determined|Exhortation.ask: Whose limit did you treat as an excuse?

Determined|Faith.recognize: You keep believing past the point where it stopped being comfortable, which is what perseverance actually looks like. The check is whether you are holding to God or to the outcome you settled on.
Determined|Faith.ask: What would you still trust Him for if this never happens?

Determined|Giving.recognize: You committed to an amount and you have met it in years when it hurt, and that reliability funds what nothing else funds. The exposure is a commitment kept long past a change in your circumstances.
Determined|Giving.ask: What are you still paying that you can no longer afford?

Determined|Healing.recognize: You do not accept the first prognosis, and people are alive because somebody in their corner would not stop. Where it costs is the person who has accepted it and needs you to as well.
Determined|Healing.ask: Whose acceptance have you been overriding?

Determined|Interpretation.recognize: You work at a confusing situation until it makes sense, long after other people gave up on understanding it. The risk is forcing coherence onto something that was genuinely chaotic.
Determined|Interpretation.ask: What have you explained that may just have been a mess?

Determined|Knowledge.recognize: You get to the bottom of things other people abandon, and what you bring back is what nobody else has. The waste is the question that had no answer and took two years.
Determined|Knowledge.ask: What have you been chasing with nothing to show?

Determined|Leadership.recognize: Your team does things they did not believe they could, because you never offered the option of stopping. The exposure is what that costs the people who cannot say no to you.
Determined|Leadership.ask: Who on your team is exhausted and has not told you?

Determined|Mercy.recognize: You keep reaching toward somebody who has not responded in a year, and one day they may. What to weigh is whether the silence is a wound or a boundary.
Determined|Mercy.ask: Have they asked you to stop?

Determined|Miracles.recognize: You keep asking after most people would have concluded the answer was no, and Scripture is on your side about that. Worth examining is the difference between persisting and bargaining.
Determined|Miracles.ask: What have you promised God in exchange?

Determined|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You go after the one who left, and more than once, and some of them came back only because you did. The risk is the person whose leaving was the healthiest thing they have done.

Determined|Prophecy.recognize: You say the hard thing again when it was not received the first time, and repetition is sometimes exactly what was needed. It is also how a word turns into a grievance.
Determined|Prophecy.ask: How many times have you said this to them?

Determined|Service.recognize: You finish jobs other people abandon at eighty percent, and the last twenty is where the value was. What deserves attention is the job you finished that should have been stopped.
Determined|Service.ask: What did you complete that nobody was waiting for?

Determined|Teaching.recognize: You stay with the student who is not getting it until they do, and some of them have never had that from anyone. The risk is that the difficulty was not the subject.
Determined|Teaching.ask: Who kept struggling because something else was going on?

Determined|Tongues.recognize: You keep at this without the experience other people describe, and continuing without confirmation is its own kind of faith. What can grow underneath is resentment you have never named.
Determined|Tongues.ask: What are you disappointed about that you have never said?

Determined|Wisdom.recognize: You keep working a problem after everyone else accepted it, and some problems yield only to that. The limit is that some things resolve only by waiting, and effort cannot bring that forward.
Determined|Wisdom.ask: What are you trying to force that only time will settle?

Diligent and Observant|Administration.recognize: You spot the error in the spreadsheet three rows before anybody else has opened it, and the whole thing stays clean because of you. What can go missing is that being right about a decimal does not make the meeting shorter.
Diligent and Observant|Administration.ask: What small correction cost the room twenty minutes?

Diligent and Observant|Apostleship.recognize: You see what the new work actually needs on the ground rather than what the plan said it would, and that saves ventures. It also means you are often correcting somebody who is still excited.
Diligent and Observant|Apostleship.ask: What did you point out that dampened a room?

Diligent and Observant|Discernment.recognize: You register the small change in somebody before they mention it, the missed Sunday, the shorter answers, and you are usually right. The care needed is what you do with a detail you were never actually told.
Diligent and Observant|Discernment.ask: What have you observed about somebody that you should ask them about?

Diligent and Observant|Evangelism.recognize: You find whoever is on the edge of the room and go there, which is where the real conversation usually is. Watch for spending a whole evening reading somebody and never saying anything.
Diligent and Observant|Evangelism.ask: Who did you study all night and never speak to?

Diligent and Observant|Exhortation.recognize: You encourage people about things nobody else noticed they did, and that lands harder than praise for the obvious. The blind spot is that you register the flaws at exactly the same rate.
Diligent and Observant|Exhortation.ask: What ratio of your noticing do they actually hear?

Diligent and Observant|Faith.recognize: You watch how things turn out rather than how they were promised, so your trust is built on what you have seen hold. Where it costs is the step that has no track record to look at.
Diligent and Observant|Faith.ask: What have you refused to try because nothing proves it works?

Diligent and Observant|Giving.recognize: You see the need before it is announced, the coat, the car, the light bill, and you meet it quietly. The strain is holding a running tally of what everybody around you lacks.
Diligent and Observant|Giving.ask: How many needs are you keeping count of right now?

Diligent and Observant|Healing.recognize: You register the thing somebody is not saying and stay near it without forcing it open, and that patience is where a lot of it starts. What can happen is watching for months and never asking.
Diligent and Observant|Healing.ask: What have you been waiting for them to bring up?

Diligent and Observant|Interpretation.recognize: You can point at the exact moment a situation turned, because you were paying attention when it did. The risk is that a detail you remember correctly may not be the reason.
Diligent and Observant|Interpretation.ask: What are you sure caused this, and who would disagree?

Diligent and Observant|Knowledge.recognize: You collect the small facts other people walk past and they turn out to matter later. The waste is the enormous amount you have gathered that nobody has asked for.
Diligent and Observant|Knowledge.ask: What do you know that you have never been asked?

Diligent and Observant|Leadership.recognize: Nothing gets past you, so your team's work is clean. The cost is that people working under a close eye stop taking chances.
Diligent and Observant|Leadership.ask: When did somebody on your team last try something risky?

Diligent and Observant|Mercy.recognize: You see who is struggling before they say so, which means you are often the first person who could reach them. The limit is that seeing is not the same as going.
Diligent and Observant|Mercy.ask: Who have you seen struggling and not gone to?

Diligent and Observant|Miracles.recognize: You are hard to fool, so when you say something happened that you cannot account for, it carries weight. Worth checking is whether you have been so busy checking that you missed the thing itself.
Diligent and Observant|Miracles.ask: What did you analyse in a moment you should have received?

Diligent and Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know who has been absent two weeks running and who left early, and that knowledge is the beginning of real care. The line runs between attention and surveillance, and only they can tell you which it feels like.
Diligent and Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Would they call your attention care or being watched?

Diligent and Observant|Prophecy.recognize: You have the specific example, so what you say is hard to wave away. The risk is that the specific example is also the part that lasts longest.
Diligent and Observant|Prophecy.ask: What example did you use that they still remember?

Diligent and Observant|Service.recognize: You see the job that needs doing and how it ought to be done, and you do it properly the first time. The friction is with the person who did it adequately and then heard about it.
Diligent and Observant|Service.ask: Whose adequate work did you remark on?

Diligent and Observant|Teaching.recognize: You find the exact place a student went wrong instead of making them redo the whole thing, and that precision saves people years. The risk is a class that becomes a series of corrections.
Diligent and Observant|Teaching.ask: What did you praise in your last session?

Diligent and Observant|Tongues.recognize: You attend to what is actually happening rather than what people say is happening, and that keeps a room honest. What can grow is a habit of assessing an experience while everyone else is inside it.
Diligent and Observant|Tongues.ask: When did you last stop evaluating and join in?

Diligent and Observant|Wisdom.recognize: You bring the detail that changes the advice, because you saw what other people missed. The limit is that somebody in a mess does not need an inventory of it.
Diligent and Observant|Wisdom.ask: What did you list for a person who needed one thing?

Direct|Administration.recognize: Your emails are three lines and nothing in them is ambiguous, so systems move faster around you. What gets skipped is the part where somebody needed to feel consulted before they complied.

Direct|Apostleship.recognize: You will announce that the new thing is not working while everybody is still celebrating that it started, and that saves years. It also lands on people who gave up a great deal to be there.
Direct|Apostleship.ask: Who had the most invested in what you just criticised?

Direct|Discernment.recognize: You put what you sense about somebody into words immediately, and the words are usually accurate. Accurate and welcome are two different things.
Direct|Discernment.ask: What true thing did you name at the wrong moment?

Direct|Evangelism.recognize: You ask people what they actually believe instead of circling it, and most of them find that a relief. The ones who do not, you may never hear from again.
Direct|Evangelism.ask: Who stopped talking to you after one conversation?

Direct|Exhortation.recognize: You give people the real assessment, which is worth more than encouragement they cannot trust. The gap is that some people need three true things before they can take in the fourth.
Direct|Exhortation.ask: How much did you say before the hard part?

Direct|Faith.recognize: You are plain about what you believe and plainer about what you doubt, and that honesty gives other people permission. Watch for a doubt announced so firmly that it hardens into a position.
Direct|Faith.ask: What did you declare uncertain and never revisit?

Direct|Giving.recognize: You answer on the spot and people always know where they stand. The exposure is a no delivered so cleanly that they will not come back with the next thing.
Direct|Giving.ask: Who has not asked you again?

Direct|Healing.recognize: You name what happened to somebody without softening it, and being told the truth of it is often the first step. Some people need weeks before that step.
Direct|Healing.ask: Who was not ready for the plain version?

Direct|Interpretation.recognize: You describe what the situation actually is while everybody else is choosing their words, and the room usually needed it. The risk is that your version arrives with no room to be wrong.
Direct|Interpretation.ask: How would somebody disagree with you without a fight?

Direct|Knowledge.recognize: You will tell somebody they are working from bad information, which most people will not do. The cost is that a public correction is remembered far longer than what it corrected.
Direct|Knowledge.ask: Where did that last happen, and who else was there?

Direct|Leadership.recognize: Nobody wonders what you think, and that clarity is why people can work for you. The exposure is that a leader who is never unsure out loud gets a team who hides being unsure too.
Direct|Leadership.ask: When did you last say you did not know?

Direct|Mercy.recognize: You go at the thing itself instead of talking around the edges, and for a lot of grieving people that is the kindest thing available. For others it arrives like a shove.
Direct|Mercy.ask: Who pulled back the last time you named their pain?

Direct|Miracles.recognize: You will state exactly what you believe God is going to do, with no cover on it, and that takes more nerve than most people have. It also leaves nowhere to stand if nothing comes.
Direct|Miracles.ask: What have you claimed publicly that you would now word differently?

Direct|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People know you will not manage them, and there is safety in that. What can be missing is the gentle version, which some people are only able to receive.
Direct|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needs it soft, and can you do soft?

Direct|Prophecy.recognize: You have the shortest distance between seeing a thing and saying it of anybody in the room, and that is the gift. It is also why what lands is usually deeper than you intended.
Direct|Prophecy.ask: What did you mean as a sentence that arrived as a verdict?

Direct|Service.recognize: You will tell somebody their plan for the work is wrong and then help anyway. Both halves are real. Only one of them gets remembered.
Direct|Service.ask: Do people remember your help or your opinion of their plan?

Direct|Teaching.recognize: You tell students plainly when they are wrong, and the confident ones improve quickly because of it. The quiet ones stop answering.
Direct|Teaching.ask: Who has stopped speaking up in your class?

Direct|Tongues.recognize: You will not fake an experience you are not having, and that keeps a whole room from putting on a show. What can harden is announcing your scepticism in a moment somebody else needed.

Direct|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is short and people can act on it. The limit is that some situations have to be talked around for an hour before the answer will land.
Direct|Wisdom.ask: Who needed to be heard before they were advised?

Direct and Authentic|Administration.recognize: You will admit in a meeting that your own part is behind, which almost nobody does, and it makes the entire status report trustworthy. The friction is with people who preferred the polished version.
Direct and Authentic|Administration.ask: Who was uncomfortable the last time you owned a miss?

Direct and Authentic|Apostleship.recognize: You arrive in a new place as yourself rather than as a representative, and people who distrust institutions trust you. The cost is that you cannot switch it off when a situation calls for restraint.
Direct and Authentic|Apostleship.ask: Where did being fully yourself cost you the room?

Direct and Authentic|Discernment.recognize: You say out loud what you are picking up instead of filing it away, and people often confirm it. The care needed is that a hunch spoken aloud sounds like a conclusion.
Direct and Authentic|Discernment.ask: What did you voice that they heard as settled?

Direct and Authentic|Evangelism.recognize: You talk about your faith including the parts that have not worked, and that is precisely why people listen. Watch for a story so honest that it becomes about you.
Direct and Authentic|Evangelism.ask: When did your testimony last point somewhere other than yourself?

Direct and Authentic|Exhortation.recognize: You tell people what you actually went through, and hearing it from somebody who has been there does what advice cannot. The exposure is assuming their situation is your situation.
Direct and Authentic|Exhortation.ask: Where does their story stop matching yours?

Direct and Authentic|Faith.recognize: You will say the doubt out loud in a room where everybody else sounds sure, and somebody there needed the permission. The danger is that your honesty carries further than your hope does.
Direct and Authentic|Faith.ask: When did anyone last hear you sure about something?

Direct and Authentic|Giving.recognize: You are open about what you give and what you cannot, and that plainness makes money less strange in your church. The cost is that not everybody wanted to know.
Direct and Authentic|Giving.ask: Who did not want that information?

Direct and Authentic|Healing.recognize: You will tell somebody about your own worst year, and it puts them on level ground with you. The care needed is that your worst year can take over the conversation.
Direct and Authentic|Healing.ask: Who came to talk and ended up listening?
