Generous|Miracles.recognize: You give as though the supply were not yours to manage, and it is a genuine witness when you keep having enough. Worth weighing is whether you are trusting God or leaning on the fact that it has always worked out.
Generous|Miracles.ask: What would you do if the next gift left you short?

Generous|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know you would give them anything, and that knowledge holds a lot of them steady. What it can hide is that being endlessly available is not the same as being present.
Generous|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who has all of your resources and none of your attention?

Generous|Prophecy.recognize: You deliver hard news gently, and because you have already given so much they can take it from you. The risk is banking that goodwill for years and never spending it.
Generous|Prophecy.ask: What have you earned the right to say and still not said?

Generous|Service.recognize: You say yes before you know what is being asked, and an enormous amount gets done because of people like you. The friction is a yes that was already spent when it was given.
Generous|Service.ask: What did you agree to that you cannot actually do?

Generous|Teaching.recognize: You give your material away, the notes, the slides, the outlines, and other people's ministries run on it. What can go missing is the credit and, eventually, your own appetite for preparing it.
Generous|Teaching.ask: Who is teaching your work without knowing it is yours?

Generous|Tongues.recognize: You hold your spiritual life loosely enough to let other people into it, where many keep it entirely private. The question is whether anything remains that is only between you and God.
Generous|Tongues.ask: What part of your prayer life has nobody heard about?

Generous|Wisdom.recognize: You give your advice freely and do not charge for access, so the people who need it can reach you. What that costs is the person who needed three hours and got the same fifteen minutes as everyone else.
Generous|Wisdom.ask: Who got fifteen minutes from you and needed an afternoon?

Good Practical Skills|Administration.recognize: When something breaks you repair it rather than reporting it, and whole facilities run on that. The cost is a hundred fixes nobody has written down, all of which stop working the week you are away.
Good Practical Skills|Administration.ask: What only works because you know how to make it work?

Good Practical Skills|Apostleship.recognize: A new work needs somebody who can make a rented room usable by Sunday, and that is you. The gap is that a functioning room is not yet a church, and the room is the easier thing to keep working on.
Good Practical Skills|Apostleship.ask: How long has the room been ready?

Good Practical Skills|Discernment.recognize: You can tell when something is not right long before there is evidence, the way you can hear a bearing going. Where it misfires is applying that to people, who do not fail the way machines do.
Good Practical Skills|Discernment.ask: Who did you diagnose from the outside?

Good Practical Skills|Evangelism.recognize: You get into people's lives through a broken fence and a dead alternator, and that is a door most preachers never find. Watch for a friendship that stays at the level of the repair for years.
Good Practical Skills|Evangelism.ask: What would you say if there was nothing to fix at their house?

Good Practical Skills|Exhortation.recognize: You lift somebody by showing them how and then handing them the tool, and confidence gained that way holds. The limit is the person whose problem cannot be demonstrated.
Good Practical Skills|Exhortation.ask: Who needed words from you and got a demonstration?

Good Practical Skills|Faith.recognize: You trust God and also check the oil, which is a healthier combination than most sermons allow for. Worth examining is the point where preparation becomes the reason you never have to depend on Him.
Good Practical Skills|Faith.ask: What in your life is not covered by your own capability?

Good Practical Skills|Giving.recognize: You give your hours and your tools rather than money, and to people who can afford neither that is worth more. What is easy to miss is that your hours run out in a way a bank balance does not.
Good Practical Skills|Giving.ask: How many Saturdays did you give away last month?

Good Practical Skills|Healing.recognize: You turn up at a crisis and start doing the things that need doing, and the family remembers that for twenty years. What is harder is the visit where there is nothing to do at all.
Good Practical Skills|Healing.ask: Who needed you present when there was no job to do?

Good Practical Skills|Interpretation.recognize: You can turn an abstract idea into something a person can picture, usually with a comparison from a workshop or a truck. The risk is a comparison that fits so well it decides the answer.
Good Practical Skills|Interpretation.ask: Which of your analogies has stopped being questioned?

Good Practical Skills|Knowledge.recognize: You learn things by taking them apart, so what you know is real rather than remembered. The narrow part is a subject that cannot be taken apart, which you tend to leave alone.
Good Practical Skills|Knowledge.ask: What subject have you left alone because it will not come apart?

Good Practical Skills|Leadership.recognize: You lead by working alongside people, and they follow because they have seen what you can do. What can be missing is the part of leading that is not visible work, like deciding what the team should stop doing.
Good Practical Skills|Leadership.ask: What decision have you postponed by staying busy?

Good Practical Skills|Mercy.recognize: You meet suffering with a casserole, a ride and a repaired water heater, which is love in the form people can actually use. The limit is the pain that no practical act touches.
Good Practical Skills|Mercy.ask: Whose suffering could you do nothing about?

Good Practical Skills|Miracles.recognize: You know exactly what human effort can accomplish, so when something exceeds it you are the credible witness. Worth asking is whether anything is left on your list that only God could do.
Good Practical Skills|Miracles.ask: What are you praying about that you could not fix yourself?

Good Practical Skills|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People let you into their homes and their problems because you arrive useful, and that access is real. What can stall is the move from the garage to the kitchen table.
Good Practical Skills|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Whose house have you been in fifty times without a real conversation?

Good Practical Skills|Prophecy.recognize: You say plainly when something will not work, and you are usually right because you have made the thing before. The cost is that being right about the mechanism does not make you right about the people.
Good Practical Skills|Prophecy.ask: What did you call unworkable that somebody made work?

Good Practical Skills|Service.recognize: You are the reason the lights come on and the van runs, and almost nobody knows your name. The friction is that invisible is comfortable, and it can become a place to hide.
Good Practical Skills|Service.ask: When did you last take a job where people would see you?

Good Practical Skills|Teaching.recognize: You teach by putting the thing in somebody's hands and correcting as they go, and skills learned that way stay learned. What resists the method is anything that cannot be practised on a bench.
Good Practical Skills|Teaching.ask: What did you try to teach with nothing to put in their hands?

Good Practical Skills|Tongues.recognize: You are wary of anything you cannot see working, and that instinct has kept more than one group out of nonsense. The risk is refusing what is real simply because it produces nothing measurable.
Good Practical Skills|Tongues.ask: When did you last do something with God that produced nothing?

Good Practical Skills|Wisdom.recognize: You answer the question people actually asked, which is what to do, and they leave knowing where to start. The limit is the situation with no action in it, where waiting is the only faithful move.
Good Practical Skills|Wisdom.ask: What advice did you give when the honest answer was wait?

Good at Connecting with Others|Administr.recognize: You know who in the building can solve a given problem, so requests reach the right desk without a chart. What is missing is anything written down, which means the routing lives in your head and dies with your calendar.
Good at Connecting with Others|Administr.ask: Who could route these requests if you were out for a month?

Good at Connecting with Others|Apostlesh.recognize: You can put a new work in touch with the six people it needs in a city you arrived in last month. The exposure is a network that belongs to you rather than to the work, so it leaves when you do.
Good at Connecting with Others|Apostlesh.ask: What relationships would the work lose if you moved away?

Good at Connecting with Others|Discernme.recognize: You know which two people should never be put on the same team, and you are usually right about why. The cost is a judgement made once and never revisited as the person changed.
Good at Connecting with Others|Discernme.ask: Who are you still keeping apart for a reason from years ago?

Good at Connecting with Others|Evangelis.recognize: You get people into the room by way of somebody they already trust, which is how most people actually come to faith. Watch for a chain of warm handoffs where nobody ever says anything costly.
Good at Connecting with Others|Evangelis.ask: Who did you pass along instead of talking to yourself?

Good at Connecting with Others|Exhortati.recognize: You find the one person whose story will unlock somebody, and you put them together. What that can replace is the harder thing, which is you saying it yourself.
Good at Connecting with Others|Exhortati.ask: Who needed you and got a referral?

Good at Connecting with Others|Faith.recognize: When something needs to happen you know who to call, and things do happen. Worth examining is whether you have prayed about anything you could not solve with a phone call.
Good at Connecting with Others|Faith.ask: When did a problem last have nobody you could call?

Good at Connecting with Others|Giving.recognize: You are better at moving other people's money toward a need than most people are at giving their own, and more gets met that way. The examination is what has left your own account this year.
Good at Connecting with Others|Giving.ask: What did you give that did not come from somebody else?

Good at Connecting with Others|Healing.recognize: You know the person who has already walked through what this family is walking through, and that meeting is worth more than any advice. What can be avoided is your own presence in the hard part.
Good at Connecting with Others|Healing.ask: Whose hospital room have you not been in yourself?

Good at Connecting with Others|Interpret.recognize: You can lay two groups out to each other because you have real standing in both, which is uncommon. The risk is that neither side ever hears the version they would find offensive.
Good at Connecting with Others|Interpret.ask: What have you smoothed between two groups this year?

Good at Connecting with Others|Knowledge.recognize: You know who knows, which in practice is faster than knowing. What can quietly stop is your own reading, because there is always somebody to ask.
Good at Connecting with Others|Knowledge.ask: What have you never studied because you know an expert?

Good at Connecting with Others|Leadershi.recognize: You can assemble a team out of people who did not know each other three weeks ago, and it works. The gap is that a team of your relationships is not the same as a team with relationships.
Good at Connecting with Others|Leadershi.ask: Which two people on your team have never spoken without you?

Good at Connecting with Others|Mercy.recognize: You make sure nobody grieves alone, because you know exactly who to send. The limit is that being sent is not the same as coming, and some people wanted you.
Good at Connecting with Others|Mercy.ask: Who did you arrange support for and never visit?

Good at Connecting with Others|Miracles.recognize: You gather the people who will pray for a thing, and there is real weight in a room like that. Worth weighing is whether you have ever asked God for something alone.
Good at Connecting with Others|Miracles.ask: What did you take to God without gathering anyone?

Good at Connecting with Others|Pastor/Sh.recognize: Everyone in your church is one conversation away from you, and that is why nobody goes missing for long. What is hard to see is that a wide net is thin at every point.
Good at Connecting with Others|Pastor/Sh.ask: Who knows the parts of your life you do not put in front of people?

Good at Connecting with Others|Prophecy.recognize: You know who a person will actually listen to, so hard things reach them by a route they can accept. The risk is never being the one who says it, which keeps your name clean.
Good at Connecting with Others|Prophecy.ask: When did somebody last hear something hard directly from you?

Good at Connecting with Others|Service.recognize: You can staff anything, because you know who is available and who owes you a Saturday. The friction is a favour economy, where help arrives out of obligation rather than love.
Good at Connecting with Others|Service.ask: Who helps you because they owe you?

Good at Connecting with Others|Teaching.recognize: You bring in the person who can teach it better than you can, and your people get the best available. What can go undeveloped is your own subject, since there is always somebody else to put in front.
Good at Connecting with Others|Teaching.ask: When did you last stand up and teach it yourself?

Good at Connecting with Others|Tongues.recognize: You are at home across very different traditions and can move between them without offending anyone. The question is which of them you actually belong to.
Good at Connecting with Others|Tongues.ask: Where do you pray when nobody has asked you anywhere?

Good at Connecting with Others|Wisdom.recognize: Your best advice is usually a name, and the name is usually right. The limit is the person who needed you to sit with the question rather than pass it on.
Good at Connecting with Others|Wisdom.ask: Who wanted your judgement and got a phone number?

Good-Natured and Positive|Administration.recognize: People bring you bad news early because you do not make it worse, and early bad news is worth a great deal. What can follow is a report that arrives sunny and understates how much trouble the project is in.
Good-Natured and Positive|Administration.ask: What problem got described upward as smaller than it was?

Good-Natured and Positive|Apostleship.recognize: A new work is mostly discouragement, and you are the reason people are still there in month nine. The exposure is a venture that should have been stopped in month six with you keeping spirits up instead.
Good-Natured and Positive|Apostleship.ask: Who is still working on something you know will not survive?

Good-Natured and Positive|Discernment.recognize: You assume the best about people and you are right often enough that it works as a strategy. The cost is the once you were not right, and how long it took to admit what you had already seen.
Good-Natured and Positive|Discernment.ask: Who did you defend while holding private doubts?

Good-Natured and Positive|Evangelism.recognize: People find faith attractive around you because you are visibly glad, and gladness argues better than argument does. Watch for a gospel that has quietly lost the part about sin because it does not match your tone.
Good-Natured and Positive|Evangelism.ask: What part of the gospel do you leave out because it is heavy?

Good-Natured and Positive|Exhortation.recognize: You can get somebody back on their feet in a five-minute conversation, and they leave believing it. The risk is that they needed to stay down long enough to find out why they fell.
Good-Natured and Positive|Exhortation.ask: Who did you get moving again before they understood what happened?

Good-Natured and Positive|Faith.recognize: You do not panic, and a room full of anxious people steadies around you. Worth examining is whether that is trust in God or a temperament that has never been tested.
Good-Natured and Positive|Faith.ask: What has frightened you in the last year?

Good-Natured and Positive|Giving.recognize: You give with no strings and no lecture, so people can receive from you without humiliation. What can be missing is the follow-up conversation about what caused the need.
Good-Natured and Positive|Giving.ask: What is causing the need you keep covering?

Good-Natured and Positive|Healing.recognize: You are easy to be around during recovery, which is long and mostly boring and drives other visitors away. The limit is the stretch where somebody needs a person willing to be as bleak as they feel.
Good-Natured and Positive|Healing.ask: Who needed you to agree that it was terrible?

Good-Natured and Positive|Interpretation.recognize: You find the reading of events that people can live with, and sometimes that reading is also correct. The danger is a habit of settling on the bearable version before checking which one is accurate.
Good-Natured and Positive|Interpretation.ask: What explanation did you land on because it was easier?

Good-Natured and Positive|Knowledge.recognize: You make learning feel unthreatening, so people admit what they do not know in front of you. What can go unsaid is the finding that is genuinely bad news.
Good-Natured and Positive|Knowledge.ask: What have you learned and not passed on because it would upset people?

Good-Natured and Positive|Leadership.recognize: Morale on your team is real rather than manufactured, and people work harder because of it. The gap is the quarter where the honest message was that things are not fine.
Good-Natured and Positive|Leadership.ask: When did you last tell your team something discouraging?

Good-Natured and Positive|Mercy.recognize: You bring warmth into a room that has gone heavy, and people are grateful for it. The limit is grief that needs the room to stay heavy a while longer.
Good-Natured and Positive|Mercy.ask: Whose sadness did you try to move too soon?

Good-Natured and Positive|Miracles.recognize: You assume God is good and you say so, which is not naivety but a settled conviction. Worth asking is what you do with the prayer that was answered no.
Good-Natured and Positive|Miracles.ask: What has God not done that you still avoid mentioning?

Good-Natured and Positive|Pastor/Shepher.recognize: People feel better after time with you, which is why they keep coming back. What can be missed is the person who has felt better forty times and changed nothing.
Good-Natured and Positive|Pastor/Shepher.ask: Who has been lifted by you for years and is still stuck?

Good-Natured and Positive|Prophecy.recognize: When you say something is wrong people believe it, because you are not somebody who complains. That gives you one of the most valuable voices in the room, and you have used it perhaps twice.
Good-Natured and Positive|Prophecy.ask: What would people believe from you that you have never said?

Good-Natured and Positive|Service.recognize: You make a long unpleasant job bearable for everybody else on it, which is why your crews finish. What can go unsaid is that the job was badly planned and should never have taken nine hours.
Good-Natured and Positive|Service.ask: What did you make bearable that should have been fixed?

Good-Natured and Positive|Teaching.recognize: Nobody is afraid to ask you a stupid question, and that is most of whether people learn anything. The risk is a class where nothing is ever hard enough to fail at.
Good-Natured and Positive|Teaching.ask: When did somebody last get something wrong in your class?

Good-Natured and Positive|Tongues.recognize: You are open to what you do not understand rather than wary of it, and that openness has let real things happen around you. The question is whether you would recognise something that was not from God.
Good-Natured and Positive|Tongues.ask: What have you welcomed without testing?

Good-Natured and Positive|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice leaves people hopeful, and hope is often what they came for. The limit is the situation where the wise answer is that this will cost them something and there is no way around it.
Good-Natured and Positive|Wisdom.ask: Who left you hopeful about something that will not work?

Grounded|Administration.recognize: Processes you own do not wobble when the year gets hard, and people rely on that more than they ever say. The cost is a process that stopped fitting two years ago and survives because it is stable.
Grounded|Administration.ask: What still runs because changing it felt unnecessary?

Grounded|Apostleship.recognize: You are what a new work needs in year two, when the excitement is gone and somebody has to keep showing up. The gap is year one, where nothing is settled and you find the ground unpleasant.
Grounded|Apostleship.ask: What early-stage thing did you turn down?

Grounded|Discernment.recognize: You are hard to move with a compelling story, so you catch the thing everybody else got swept into. The cost is the genuine move of God that also arrives as enthusiasm.
Grounded|Discernment.ask: What did you stand against that turned out to be right?

Grounded|Evangelism.recognize: Your faith is visibly not a phase, and to somebody who has watched people burn hot and vanish, that is the argument. Watch for a steadiness that has stopped saying anything at all.
Grounded|Evangelism.ask: Who has known you a decade without hearing what you believe?

Grounded|Exhortation.recognize: You neither flatter nor panic, so when you tell somebody they are doing fine they believe you. The gap is the person who needed to be pushed rather than settled.
Grounded|Exhortation.ask: Who did you reassure when they needed to be moved?

Grounded|Faith.recognize: Your trust does not rise and fall with the week, which is worth more across ten years than anyone's intensity. Worth examining is whether it also fails to move when God asks for something new.
Grounded|Faith.ask: What change have you outlasted rather than obeyed?

Grounded|Giving.recognize: Your giving is the same in a bad year as a good one, which is rarer than any large gift. The narrow part is a figure set a long time ago that has never been revisited.
Grounded|Giving.ask: Who decided that number, and when?

Grounded|Healing.recognize: You are still there in month eight, when everybody who came in week one has gone back to their lives. What can be missing is the early intensity, which is also part of being loved.
Grounded|Healing.ask: Who needed you upset on their behalf and got calm?

Grounded|Interpretation.recognize: You do not get pulled into the first reading of a confusing event, and you are often the only one still asking a week later. The risk is a settled conclusion that survives evidence it should not have.
Grounded|Interpretation.ask: What have you concluded that new information has not touched?

Grounded|Knowledge.recognize: What you know, you know all the way down, because you were never in a hurry to have an opinion. The narrow part is the number of subjects you have decided are not worth the descent.
Grounded|Knowledge.ask: What have you refused to have a view on?

Grounded|Leadership.recognize: Your team knows you will be the same person in a crisis as you were last Tuesday, and that is most of what people mean by trust. The gap is that steady and moving are not the same, and some seasons need a change of speed.
Grounded|Leadership.ask: What has your team needed you to change and you have not?

Grounded|Mercy.recognize: You can be near ugly, long-running pain without needing it to resolve, and almost nobody manages that. The limit is that some suffering wants somebody to be angry about it on their behalf.
Grounded|Mercy.ask: Whose situation should have made you angry?

Grounded|Miracles.recognize: You are not swept up by a dramatic claim, so when you say something happened people take it seriously. Worth weighing is whether you have made room for God to do something you would find embarrassing.
Grounded|Miracles.ask: What would you dismiss if it happened in your own church?

Grounded|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You are the fixed point for a set of people, and they orient by you without ever saying so. What that costs is any admission that you are struggling, since a fixed point is not allowed to move.
Grounded|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who knows how you are actually doing?

Grounded|Prophecy.recognize: You say the same thing whether the room agrees or not, and over time that makes you very hard to dismiss. The cost is a message that has not changed even where the situation has.
Grounded|Prophecy.ask: What have you been saying for five years without adjusting it?

Grounded|Service.recognize: You are there every week, worth more than any burst of help, and everybody has quietly arranged their plans around it. The friction is that nobody has asked in years whether you still want the job.
Grounded|Service.ask: Who would you tell if you wanted to stop?

Grounded|Teaching.recognize: You teach the same material carefully rather than chasing whatever is new, and your students come away with something that lasts. The risk is notes that have not been reopened since you first made them.
Grounded|Teaching.ask: When did you last change your mind about something you teach?

Grounded|Tongues.recognize: You are not moved by atmosphere, so nothing you report as spiritual experience is atmosphere. The question is whether you have ever allowed a service to affect you at all.
Grounded|Tongues.ask: When did worship last do something to you?

Grounded|Wisdom.recognize: Your judgement does not swing with your mood, so people come to you when they cannot trust their own. The limit is a view formed long ago and never tested against how things are now.
Grounded|Wisdom.ask: Who did you advise from a world that no longer exists?

Hands-on and Observant|Administration.recognize: You see the thing going wrong on the floor and correct it before it reaches a form, which keeps a lot of small problems small. The cost is that nothing is recorded, so the same problem gets solved fresh every month by whoever is standing there.
Hands-on and Observant|Administration.ask: What have you fixed three times without telling anyone?

Hands-on and Observant|Apostleship.recognize: You get a new work moving by doing the first visible thing rather than waiting for a plan, and momentum is real. The exposure is everything that was never set up because it was not urgent that morning.
Hands-on and Observant|Apostleship.ask: What was never set up because nothing forced it?

Hands-on and Observant|Discernment.recognize: You catch what a person's face does before they answer, and you respond to that rather than to the words. The cost is a read taken in one second and treated as settled.
Hands-on and Observant|Discernment.ask: Who did you judge on a first impression you never revisited?

Hands-on and Observant|Evangelism.recognize: You start the conversation the moment it appears, at the counter or in the driveway, where most people wait for a better time. Watch for a conversation that never gets a second one because you moved on.
Hands-on and Observant|Evangelism.ask: Whose name did you never get?

Hands-on and Observant|Exhortation.recognize: You say the useful thing on the spot, which is when it counts, and people remember exactly where they were standing. What is harder is the long involvement afterward.
Hands-on and Observant|Exhortation.ask: Who quotes something you said and you have not spoken since?

Hands-on and Observant|Faith.recognize: You obey on the spot, before you have talked yourself out of it, and a great deal of good has come from that. Worth examining is what happens when obedience requires eighteen months rather than an afternoon.
Hands-on and Observant|Faith.ask: What obedience of yours has no finish date?

Hands-on and Observant|Giving.recognize: You give the moment you see the need, cash out of your own pocket, and it lands when it was needed. What can be missing is the sustained support that outlasts the moment you were present for.
Hands-on and Observant|Giving.ask: Who did you help once who needed help for a year?

Hands-on and Observant|Healing.recognize: You are the first one there, before anybody has decided what to do, and being first matters more than people admit. What can be missing is week six, when the doing is over and there is only sitting.
Hands-on and Observant|Healing.ask: Who did you arrive for and not return to?

Hands-on and Observant|Interpretation.recognize: You read a situation off what is happening in front of you rather than the account of it, and you are usually closer to the facts than the report is. The risk is a whole situation judged from the ten minutes you happened to see.
Hands-on and Observant|Interpretation.ask: What did you conclude from the part you witnessed?

Hands-on and Observant|Knowledge.recognize: You learn by handling the thing, so what you know is unusually accurate about how it behaves in practice. The narrow part is everything that has to be read before it can be handled.
Hands-on and Observant|Knowledge.ask: What have you never read about something you use daily?

Hands-on and Observant|Leadership.recognize: You lead in motion, deciding as things arise, and your team never waits on you. The gap is that a team led one decision at a time cannot see where any of it is going.
Hands-on and Observant|Leadership.ask: What have you settled this month that nobody could have predicted?

Hands-on and Observant|Mercy.recognize: You notice the person going quiet at the edge of the room and you go over, which most people never do. The limit is that going over is the beginning of something you may not stay for.
Hands-on and Observant|Mercy.ask: Who did you approach and then leave?

Hands-on and Observant|Miracles.recognize: You pray for people on the spot rather than promising to later, which puts you ahead of most of the church. Worth asking is whether you ever return to find out what happened.
Hands-on and Observant|Miracles.ask: Who did you pray over and never ask about again?

Hands-on and Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You catch what is going on with somebody from how they came through the door, and you deal with it that day. What a same-day response cannot reach is the slow trouble with no visible symptom.
Hands-on and Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who in your care has nothing visibly wrong?

Hands-on and Observant|Prophecy.recognize: You say it while it is happening, in the room, which is the only moment it can change anything. The cost is a hard word delivered before you knew the half of it.
Hands-on and Observant|Prophecy.ask: What did you say in the room that you would take back?

Hands-on and Observant|Service.recognize: You see the job and you are already doing it, which is why things get done around you without meetings. The friction is the job that needed three people and now needs redoing.
Hands-on and Observant|Service.ask: What did you do alone that should have waited for help?

Hands-on and Observant|Teaching.recognize: You teach in the middle of the work, at the moment somebody needs to know, and that is when learning sticks. What resists the method is anything that has to be understood before the work starts.
Hands-on and Observant|Teaching.ask: What did somebody learn from you too late to use?

Hands-on and Observant|Tongues.recognize: You respond to what is happening in a service rather than to what was scheduled, and rooms open up around people like you. The question is whether anything in your spiritual life survives outside a moment.
Hands-on and Observant|Tongues.ask: What do you do with God on an ordinary Tuesday?

Hands-on and Observant|Wisdom.recognize: Your judgement in the moment is better than most people's after a week, and decisions get made that would otherwise rot. The limit is the decision that only comes clear after you have slept twice.
Hands-on and Observant|Wisdom.ask: What decision would look different after a night's sleep?

Handy and Resourceful|Administration.recognize: You get things working with whatever is available, so the ministry runs on a budget that should not support it. The cost is a system nobody else can follow, made of parts that were never meant to go together.
Handy and Resourceful|Administration.ask: What would a replacement have to reverse-engineer?

Handy and Resourceful|Apostleship.recognize: A new work has no money and no equipment, and you are the reason it has both. The exposure is a church that never gets the real thing because you can always make do.
Handy and Resourceful|Apostleship.ask: What temporary arrangement is now five years old?

Handy and Resourceful|Discernment.recognize: You work out what is really going on from what does not add up, the way you find a leak by where the stain is. Where it misfires is a person whose oddness had an innocent cause you never went looking for.
Handy and Resourceful|Discernment.ask: Whose behaviour did you account for without asking them?

Handy and Resourceful|Evangelism.recognize: You find a way into a conversation that nobody scripted, using whatever the situation gives you. Watch for cleverness that gets you the opening and then has nothing behind it.
Handy and Resourceful|Evangelism.ask: What do you say after you have got their attention?

Handy and Resourceful|Exhortation.recognize: You find something usable in a person's situation when they can see nothing at all, and that is often the turn. The limit is a workaround offered where the honest answer was that this cannot be worked around.
Handy and Resourceful|Exhortation.ask: Who needed to hear that there was no way out?

Handy and Resourceful|Faith.recognize: You have never been stopped by not having what was required, which has carried several things past the point where they should have died. Worth examining is whether you have ever had to wait on God for a resource.
Handy and Resourceful|Faith.ask: When did you last run out of options?

Handy and Resourceful|Giving.recognize: You meet a need with what is already lying around, so your generosity costs the church nothing and reaches further than the budget. What is easy to miss is that the family may have needed a new one.
Handy and Resourceful|Giving.ask: Who got your workaround when they needed the real thing?

Handy and Resourceful|Healing.recognize: You make a hard situation liveable, ramps and rides and rearranged rooms, and that practical mercy is what lets people recover at home. What no arrangement reaches is the part of them that is not liveable.
Handy and Resourceful|Healing.ask: What could you not make easier for somebody?

Handy and Resourceful|Interpretation.recognize: You can make sense of a situation from incomplete information, which is the only kind anybody ever has. The risk is a story assembled well enough that nobody goes looking for the missing pieces.
Handy and Resourceful|Interpretation.ask: What did you fill in that nobody ever verified?

Handy and Resourceful|Knowledge.recognize: You know an enormous amount that is written nowhere, learned from getting something to work at eleven at night. The narrow part is that none of it transfers unless somebody is standing next to you.
Handy and Resourceful|Knowledge.ask: Who is beside you often enough to learn any of it?

Handy and Resourceful|Leadership.recognize: You keep a team going through shortages that would stop other teams, and things feel possible around you. The gap is that permanent scarcity becomes normal, and nobody asks for what the work actually needs.
Handy and Resourceful|Leadership.ask: What does your team need that nobody has requested in years?

Handy and Resourceful|Mercy.recognize: You turn up with the thing that helps rather than the thing that was expected, and people feel seen by it. The limit is pain with nothing to bring.
Handy and Resourceful|Mercy.ask: Where did you show up with nothing in your hands?

Handy and Resourceful|Miracles.recognize: You are used to things working out with less than was needed, which has trained a real confidence that what is required arrives. Worth weighing is whether you could tell the difference between God moving and you being good at this.
Handy and Resourceful|Miracles.ask: What happened that you cannot take credit for?

Handy and Resourceful|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You find a way to keep somebody in the church who fits none of the categories, and they stay because of it. What can go missing is the ordinary care, since your attention goes to the awkward cases.
Handy and Resourceful|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who in your care has never been a problem to solve?

Handy and Resourceful|Prophecy.recognize: You say what is actually wrong with a plan, usually because you have already tried the version of it that fails. The cost is that you offer the remedy in the same breath, and the remedy lets everybody off the hook.
Handy and Resourceful|Prophecy.ask: What did you name and then immediately make bearable?

Handy and Resourceful|Service.recognize: There is no job you will refuse on the grounds that you do not have the right equipment. The friction is a repair that lasts just long enough that the real problem never gets funded.
Handy and Resourceful|Service.ask: What has been mended so often it should have been replaced?

Handy and Resourceful|Teaching.recognize: You can teach anything with whatever is in the room, a whiteboard, a coffee cup, three chairs. The risk is that your best material only exists in the moment you invented it, so nobody can carry it.
Handy and Resourceful|Teaching.ask: What have you taught brilliantly and never written down?

Handy and Resourceful|Tongues.recognize: You are pragmatic about spiritual practice and take what works, which keeps you out of a great deal of nonsense. The question is whether anything you do before God has no use at all.
Handy and Resourceful|Tongues.ask: What in your prayer life have you kept even though it does nothing?

Handy and Resourceful|Wisdom.recognize: You can always find a next step, and for somebody who is stuck that is worth more than an analysis. The limit is the situation where every available step is wrong and the honest answer is to stop moving.
Handy and Resourceful|Wisdom.ask: Who got a next step from you and needed to stand still?

Hardworking|Administration.recognize: You will do the tedious part nobody else will touch, so the records are current and the reconciliations are done. The cost is that your willingness means it never gets automated and never gets split.
Hardworking|Administration.ask: What are you doing by hand that a system should do?

Hardworking|Apostleship.recognize: New work runs on somebody willing to do four jobs for two years, and that has been you. The exposure is a work that cannot survive your schedule, because it was designed around what you can absorb.
Hardworking|Apostleship.ask: How many of your jobs has anybody else ever done?

Hardworking|Discernment.recognize: You can tell who is actually carrying weight and who is describing weight, and you are rarely wrong. The cost is a low view of people whose contribution does not look like exertion.
Hardworking|Discernment.ask: Who have you written off as lazy?

Hardworking|Evangelism.recognize: People take you seriously about faith because they have seen how you work, and character is the argument for anyone who will not sit through a sermon. Watch for a witness that is all example and never reaches words.
Hardworking|Evangelism.ask: Who has watched you work for years and never heard why?

Hardworking|Exhortation.recognize: You lift people by staying alongside them until the thing is done, which is more convincing than a speech. The limit is the person whose problem is not solved by more hours.
Hardworking|Exhortation.ask: Who did you tell to push harder when that was not the problem?

Hardworking|Faith.recognize: You do your part completely, so when you pray you are not asking God to cover for you. Worth examining is whether you have left Him anything to do.
Hardworking|Faith.ask: What have you prayed about without also attacking it yourself?

Hardworking|Giving.recognize: You give what you earned the hard way, which makes every gift cost something visible to you. The narrow part is a quiet contempt for generosity that came easily to somebody else.
Hardworking|Giving.ask: Whose generosity have you privately discounted?

Hardworking|Healing.recognize: You will do the unglamorous months, the driving and the laundry and the night shifts, long after the casseroles stop. What can go missing is your own recovery, since there is always more to be done.
Hardworking|Healing.ask: When did you last take a day off while somebody needed you?

Hardworking|Interpretation.recognize: You judge a situation by what people have actually put in, which cuts through a great deal of talk. The risk is a reading where the only evidence that counts is visible strain.
Hardworking|Interpretation.ask: What did you dismiss because it looked easy for them?

Hardworking|Knowledge.recognize: You have gone through material other people skim, so what you know is unusually complete. The narrow part is a quiet belief that anything learned quickly was not learned properly.
Hardworking|Knowledge.ask: Who understood something faster than you and got no credit?

Hardworking|Leadership.recognize: You set the pace by outworking everybody you lead, and nobody can accuse you of asking too much. The gap is that a team measuring itself against you will always be behind, and some of them have families.
Hardworking|Leadership.ask: Whose family is paying for your pace?

Hardworking|Mercy.recognize: You show up and you do, which is what suffering usually needs first. The limit is that your instinct to be useful can read as impatience to somebody who only wanted you there.
Hardworking|Mercy.ask: Who wanted you to sit down and got another job done?

Hardworking|Miracles.recognize: You have seen what sustained work accomplishes, so you are slow to call anything supernatural, and that makes your testimony credible. Worth asking is whether you have ever stopped long enough for God to do something you did not.
Hardworking|Miracles.ask: What have you refused to stop working on long enough to pray about?

Hardworking|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people are cared for because you put in hours nobody sees, and the load you carry is real. What is hard to see is that carrying it alone teaches everyone else that care is somebody else's job.
Hardworking|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who could carry part of this and has never been asked?

Hardworking|Prophecy.recognize: You have standing to say a hard thing about commitment, because nobody can point at you. The cost is a message that only ever lands on the same failing, since it is the one you can see.
Hardworking|Prophecy.ask: What sin do you never mention because it is not laziness?

Hardworking|Service.recognize: You outlast everybody, and a great deal exists because you stayed after the crew went home. The friction is that staying late has become how you know you are worth something.
Hardworking|Service.ask: Who are you when the work is finished?

Hardworking|Teaching.recognize: You prepare properly, so your class gets the whole thing rather than what you could recall on Saturday night. The risk is preparation that grows until teaching stops being possible alongside everything else.
Hardworking|Teaching.ask: How many hours went into your last lesson?

Hardworking|Tongues.recognize: You are wary of anything offering a shortcut to spiritual maturity, and that instinct is largely right. The question is whether you have made growth into another job you can be behind on.
Hardworking|Tongues.ask: What in your walk with God feels like a task list?

Hardworking|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice comes from having done the thing rather than read about it, and people can tell the difference. The limit is a default answer of more diligence, which is right often enough that you have stopped checking.
Hardworking|Wisdom.ask: Who needed permission from you to quit something?

Honest|Administration.recognize: Your status reports are accurate including the parts that make you look bad, and leadership can plan on them. The cost is that accuracy delivered without any preparation lands as a crisis when it was only a number.
Honest|Administration.ask: What did you report that caused more alarm than it needed to?

Honest|Apostleship.recognize: You tell people what a new work is actually like before they sign up, which is why the ones who come stay. The exposure is that the same plain account early can talk somebody out of a calling that was real.
Honest|Apostleship.ask: Who did you talk out of coming?

Honest|Discernment.recognize: You will say what you actually think about a person rather than the acceptable version, so people know where they stand with you. The cost is that a first impression said out loud becomes permanent for everybody who heard it.
Honest|Discernment.ask: Whose reputation did you set with one remark?

Honest|Evangelism.recognize: You do not oversell the Christian life, so nobody who comes to faith through you arrives expecting the wrong thing. Watch for a version so carefully unexaggerated that it stops sounding like good news.
Honest|Evangelism.ask: What is good about following Jesus that you never mention?

Honest|Exhortation.recognize: You give somebody the real assessment, which is why your encouragement is worth having when it comes. The risk is a true thing said the moment you thought it, before they could hear it.
Honest|Exhortation.ask: What did you say the second it occurred to you?

Honest|Faith.recognize: You say out loud when you are not sure, which is why people believe you about the rest of it. Worth examining is whether your doubts get more airtime than what you actually hold to.
Honest|Faith.ask: When did you last say something about God with no qualifier?

Honest|Giving.recognize: You state plainly what you can and cannot afford, which spares everybody the dance. The friction is that a limit put this flatly can sound like a refusal of the person rather than the amount.
Honest|Giving.ask: Who heard a no from you and thought it was about them?

Honest|Healing.recognize: You do not tell somebody it will be fine when you do not know that, and people in trouble can feel the difference. What can go missing is the hope that is also true and that you leave out because it cannot be proved.
Honest|Healing.ask: What true and comforting thing have you left unsaid?

Honest|Interpretation.recognize: You say what a situation actually is, including the part everybody is being polite about. The risk is that the impolite part is not always the truest part, only the one nobody else said.
Honest|Interpretation.ask: What did you name that turned out not to be the real issue?

Honest|Knowledge.recognize: You say when you do not know, which makes everything you do claim reliable. The narrow part is a reluctance to offer anything you cannot fully stand behind, and some questions never get a better answer than a guess.
Honest|Knowledge.ask: What did you keep back because you were only ninety percent sure?

Honest|Leadership.recognize: Your team is never managing a gap between what you said and what is true, which is worth more than most leadership technique. The gap is that some information needs a plan attached before it is passed on.
Honest|Leadership.ask: What did your team learn before you knew what to do about it?

Honest|Mercy.recognize: You do not pretend somebody's situation is better than it is, and there is real relief in being with a person who is not performing. The limit is that some moments need tenderness more than they need accuracy.
Honest|Mercy.ask: Who did you correct while they were crying?

Honest|Miracles.recognize: You will say plainly when nothing happened, and that is why anybody believes you about the times something did. Worth weighing is whether your caution has closed a door you were meant to walk through.
Honest|Miracles.ask: Which unanswered prayer made you cautious?

Honest|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People trust you with real things because you have never sold them a version of yourself. What can be underdeveloped is discretion, which is not dishonesty but a different skill entirely.
Honest|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What have you said out loud that was not yours to say?

Honest|Prophecy.recognize: You have no ability to sit on something that needs saying, and more than once that has been exactly right. The cost is that a word with no preparation behind it is heard as an attack even when it was not one.

Honest|Service.recognize: You say when you cannot take on another thing, which is rarer among willing people than it should be. The friction is a refusal delivered so flatly that nobody asks you again.
Honest|Service.ask: What did you turn down that you would actually have wanted?

Honest|Teaching.recognize: You tell a class what is disputed rather than presenting your own side as settled, and thinking people trust you for it. The risk is a room left with so many open questions that nobody can move on any of them.
Honest|Teaching.ask: What have you taught that nobody could do anything with?

Honest|Tongues.recognize: You will not claim an experience you did not have, which in some rooms takes more nerve than claiming one. The question is whether you have ever asked God for something you would afterwards have to describe.
Honest|Tongues.ask: What have you never asked for because of how it would sound?

Honest|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice arrives with the parts you are unsure of attached, so nobody acts on it thinking it is firmer than it is. The limit is that a person in crisis cannot always carry your uncertainty as well as their own.
Honest|Wisdom.ask: Who needed you to sound more certain than you were?

Honest and Direct|Administration.recognize: Nobody has to work out what you meant, so decisions stop being relitigated in the corridor afterwards. The cost is that a position put this plainly is very hard for you to change later without looking unreliable.
Honest and Direct|Administration.ask: What position are you keeping because you already stated it?

Honest and Direct|Apostleship.recognize: You give a launch team the terms at the outset, so nobody arrives with a private version of the deal. The exposure is that the terms were set before you knew what the work would actually need.
Honest and Direct|Apostleship.ask: What did you commit to before you understood the ground?

Honest and Direct|Discernment.recognize: You put your read on the table rather than hinting at it, so it can actually be tested. The cost is that once you have said it, nobody in the room will bring you evidence against it.
Honest and Direct|Discernment.ask: Who has stopped bringing you the other side?

Honest and Direct|Evangelism.recognize: You tell people what following Christ costs before you tell them what it gives, and the ones who come know what they signed. Watch for a presentation weighted so far toward the cost that grace never gets a hearing.
Honest and Direct|Evangelism.ask: When did you last lead with what God gives?

Honest and Direct|Exhortation.recognize: You say the thing plainly, which is exactly what somebody drowning in vagueness needs. The limit is that plain words land harder than you intend and stay longer than you meant them to.
Honest and Direct|Exhortation.ask: What have you said once that somebody has quoted back to you years later?

Honest and Direct|Faith.recognize: You state what you believe without softening it for the room, and that has held people steady in bad weeks. Worth examining is whether a stated position has become something you defend rather than something you are still living.
Honest and Direct|Faith.ask: What do you defend that you no longer feel?

Honest and Direct|Giving.recognize: You say what you will give and then you give it, so nobody is left guessing or hoping. The friction is that a number said out loud can end a conversation the family needed to keep having.
Honest and Direct|Giving.ask: What did a clear answer from you close too early?

Honest and Direct|Healing.recognize: You will tell somebody the actual prognosis, and there are people who cannot rest until someone has said it. The limit is the person who needed it delivered across a week rather than in one sentence.
Honest and Direct|Healing.ask: Who got all of it in one sentence?

Honest and Direct|Interpretation.recognize: You state what a situation is rather than laying out the possibilities, and a group can move once somebody has done that. The risk is a definitive account of something you had only seen from one side.
Honest and Direct|Interpretation.ask: What did you define that you had only half seen?

Honest and Direct|Knowledge.recognize: You give the conclusion first rather than making people wait through the working, and busy people are grateful for it. The narrow part is that a conclusion said flatly is very hard to qualify afterwards.
Honest and Direct|Knowledge.ask: What caveat got lost after you gave the headline?

Honest and Direct|Leadership.recognize: People know exactly where they stand with you, which removes most of the anxiety out of working under somebody. The gap is that a standard announced once is not the same as a standard anybody was coached toward.
Honest and Direct|Leadership.ask: Who did you tell what was wrong and never help fix it?

Honest and Direct|Mercy.recognize: You do not leave a hurting person guessing what you think, and guessing is its own kind of suffering. The limit is that a plain word to somebody already raw leaves a mark you will never see.
Honest and Direct|Mercy.ask: Who has been careful around you since?

Honest and Direct|Miracles.recognize: You say what you actually saw and no more, so your account of God moving can be taken at face value. Worth weighing is whether a firm early verdict has kept you from looking again.
Honest and Direct|Miracles.ask: What would make you look at this again?

Honest and Direct|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people never have to decode you, and to anybody raised around indirect adults that is a profound safety. What can be missing is the pace, because care is usually slow and your words are not.
Honest and Direct|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needed three conversations from you and got one?

Honest and Direct|Prophecy.recognize: You put the hard thing as a position rather than an accusation, which is why it can be argued with instead of resented. The cost is that a position is public, and public words are the hardest to walk back when you were wrong.
Honest and Direct|Prophecy.ask: Which public word of yours did not hold up?

Honest and Direct|Service.recognize: You say yes or no and you mean it, so nobody is left holding a maybe. The friction is that a fast no also closes off the version of the ask you would have said yes to.
Honest and Direct|Service.ask: What did you refuse before hearing the whole request?

Honest and Direct|Teaching.recognize: You say what you actually think about the text rather than surveying the options, and a class can push against a real position. The risk is students who take your view as the settled one because it was the only one said with force.
Honest and Direct|Teaching.ask: Who holds your opinion without knowing it is an opinion?

Honest and Direct|Tongues.recognize: You will say where you stand on this rather than staying diplomatically vague, which lets people around you be honest as well. The question is whether your stated position has hardened into something you can no longer revise.
Honest and Direct|Tongues.ask: When did you last revise a position publicly?

Honest and Direct|Wisdom.recognize: You give a clear answer, and somebody drowning in options needs one more than they need a framework. The limit is that a clear answer given fast is remembered as certainty long after you would have qualified it.
Honest and Direct|Wisdom.ask: Whose decision are you responsible for?

Idealistic|Administration.recognize: You will not settle for a process that merely functions, so the things you own are genuinely good rather than adequate. The cost is a standard that keeps the work unfinished while adequate would have served people this month.
Idealistic|Administration.ask: What is still not running because it is not good enough?

Idealistic|Apostleship.recognize: You start things because of what they could be, and nobody starts anything without that. The exposure is the gap between the church you described and the eleven people in a school hall.
Idealistic|Apostleship.ask: Who is discouraged by the distance you keep naming?

Idealistic|Discernment.recognize: You see what a person is meant for, and holding that over somebody can genuinely raise them. The cost is that you also see every way they fall short of it, and they can feel that in the room.
Idealistic|Discernment.ask: Who feels measured when they are with you?

Idealistic|Evangelism.recognize: You describe the life God offers rather than a set of rules, and that description is genuinely attractive. Watch for new believers who cannot find what you described anywhere in the ordinary Tuesday they actually have.
Idealistic|Evangelism.ask: Who came in hoping for more than you had told them was normal?

Idealistic|Exhortation.recognize: You call people up to something rather than telling them they are fine, and some of them have become who you said they were. The risk is the one who heard the standard and not the affection.
Idealistic|Exhortation.ask: Who heard your challenge as a verdict?

Idealistic|Faith.recognize: You believe God intends more than what you are looking at, and refusing to accept the current thing as final is scriptural. Worth examining is whether you are trusting Him or holding out for a church that has never existed anywhere.
Idealistic|Faith.ask: What are you refusing to accept that God may have permitted?

Idealistic|Giving.recognize: You give toward what something could become rather than what it is, which is how the good projects get funded at all. The friction is the ordinary need with no story of transformation attached to it.
Idealistic|Giving.ask: What unglamorous need did you pass over this year?

Idealistic|Healing.recognize: You keep hold of who somebody is when they have lost it themselves, and that has carried people a long way. The limit is that recovery is usually partial, and a person who reads your face knows when they have not reached it.
Idealistic|Healing.ask: Who has recovered less than you hoped?

Idealistic|Interpretation.recognize: You read events against what ought to be rather than what usually is, and that reading is often the prophetic one. The risk is a standard applied to people who were doing their best inside a bad situation.
Idealistic|Interpretation.ask: Who did you judge by a bar nobody could have cleared?

Idealistic|Knowledge.recognize: You are not satisfied by an answer that merely works, so you keep going until you have the real one. The narrow part is a question left open for years because no available answer is good enough.

Idealistic|Leadership.recognize: You give a team something worth doing, and people will accept a great deal for that. The gap is a leader whose face changes when the result is merely good, which a team learns to read fast.
Idealistic|Leadership.ask: Who has never heard you say that was good?

Idealistic|Mercy.recognize: You cannot make peace with somebody suffering, and that refusal is why you keep showing up when others have accepted it. The limit is that your distress at their situation becomes one more thing they have to manage.
Idealistic|Mercy.ask: Who has been consoling you about their own trouble?

Idealistic|Miracles.recognize: You believe God still does what He did, and you have not made peace with a faith that quietly stopped asking. Worth weighing is what happens in you when the answer comes back ordinary.
Idealistic|Miracles.ask: What did you pray for that resolved in the normal way?

Idealistic|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You want more for your people than they want for themselves, and several of them have grown into it. What is hard to see is the one for whom your vision has become another weight to carry.
Idealistic|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who is tired of who you think they should be?

Idealistic|Prophecy.recognize: You measure what is against what ought to be, which is the mechanism of the whole gift. The cost is that everything looks like failure from there, including the parts that were faithful.
Idealistic|Prophecy.ask: What good thing have you never acknowledged because it was not enough?

Idealistic|Service.recognize: You do the job properly rather than to the standard that was requested, and people notice the difference. The friction is a team that cannot hit your bar and has quietly stopped trying to.
Idealistic|Service.ask: Who stopped volunteering after working with you?

Idealistic|Teaching.recognize: You teach toward what a person could understand rather than what will get them through, and the serious students flourish. The risk is the ordinary student who concluded early that this was not for them.
Idealistic|Teaching.ask: Who quietly dropped out of your class?

Idealistic|Tongues.recognize: You are not satisfied with a spiritual life that runs on habit, and that hunger is itself a gift. The question is whether you can receive an ordinary season without treating it as failure.
Idealistic|Tongues.ask: What was the last dry month you accepted?

Idealistic|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice points at the best available outcome rather than the manageable one, and sometimes people reach it. The limit is the person whose situation has no good outcome and who needed help choosing between two bad ones.
Idealistic|Wisdom.ask: Who needed you to help pick the least bad option?

Imaginative|Administration.recognize: You can see how a system might work that nobody has run yet, which is where every good process begins. The cost is that the version in your head is frictionless and the real one has people in it.
Imaginative|Administration.ask: What did you design that nobody could actually operate?

Imaginative|Apostleship.recognize: You can hold a whole church in your mind before there is a building or a name, and that is what makes it fundable. The exposure is a founder already thinking about the next one by the time this one needs him.
Imaginative|Apostleship.ask: What is more interesting to you than what you are running?

Imaginative|Discernment.recognize: You can see how somebody's story might go, which lets you name a danger before it is visible to anyone else. The cost is a scenario you invented being treated by you as something you observed.
Imaginative|Discernment.ask: What did you imagine about somebody and then believe?

Imaginative|Evangelism.recognize: You can make the kingdom vivid to somebody who has only heard it described in church language, and vividness is most of why anyone listens. Watch for a version so vivid it has drifted from what is actually promised.
Imaginative|Evangelism.ask: What did you tell somebody God would do?

Imaginative|Exhortation.recognize: You can show a person a future they cannot see from where they are standing, and that has moved people out of real paralysis. The risk is a future you can see far more clearly than they ever will.
Imaginative|Exhortation.ask: Who has quietly declined the future you made for them?

Imaginative|Faith.recognize: You can conceive of God doing something that has not happened, which is closer to biblical faith than most caution. Worth examining is the difference between faith and a pleasant scenario you have rehearsed.
Imaginative|Faith.ask: What have you believed for and never moved on?

Imaginative|Giving.recognize: You can see what a gift would set in motion rather than only the amount, which is why yours goes to the right places. The friction is a need with no interesting outcome attached to it, only a bill.
Imaginative|Giving.ask: What boring need did you move past?

Imaginative|Healing.recognize: You can help somebody see themselves well again when they have lost the ability to, and that is genuinely part of getting there. The limit is a recovery you have already scripted, which makes their actual one look like a failure.
Imaginative|Healing.ask: Whose recovery has not gone the way you saw it?

Imaginative|Interpretation.recognize: You can hold several readings of the same event at once without needing to settle, which is why you catch the one everybody else ruled out early. The risk is a reading chosen because it was the more interesting one.
Imaginative|Interpretation.ask: Which reading did you keep because you liked it?

Imaginative|Knowledge.recognize: You ask what else might be true, which is where the findings that matter come from. The narrow part is a theory you enjoy enough that you stop looking for the evidence against it.
Imaginative|Knowledge.ask: What idea of yours have you never tried to disprove?

Imaginative|Leadership.recognize: You can describe a destination nobody has been to in a way that makes people willing to walk. The gap is the middle of the walk, which has no scenery and requires somebody to care about logistics.
Imaginative|Leadership.ask: Who is handling the part of this you find dull?

Imaginative|Mercy.recognize: You can enter what somebody else's life feels like from the inside, which is why your care lands rather than glancing off. The limit is that you can also do it without them, and imagining their pain is not the same as sitting in it.
Imaginative|Mercy.ask: Whose situation have you thought about more than you have visited them?

Imaginative|Miracles.recognize: You have no trouble conceiving of God doing the unusual, so you ask for things other people have quietly ruled out. Worth weighing is whether you would notice an answer that arrived plainly.
Imaginative|Miracles.ask: What ordinary help have you never called an answer?

Imaginative|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You hold somebody in mind when they are not in front of you, so your care does not stop when the conversation does. What can go missing is the actual visit, because you have already been with them in your head.
Imaginative|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who have you thought about all week and not contacted?

Imaginative|Prophecy.recognize: You can describe where a road ends while everybody else is looking at the road, which is what makes a warning land. The cost is that a vivid account of a future can be wrong in a way a plain statement cannot.
Imaginative|Prophecy.ask: What did you describe that never came?

Imaginative|Service.recognize: You can see a way to do the job that nobody has tried, and sometimes it is much better. The friction is a crew who would rather do the known thing and get home.
Imaginative|Service.ask: What did you change that nobody had asked to have changed?

Imaginative|Teaching.recognize: You can make a distant thing present, so a class is standing in Corinth rather than reading about it. The risk is that what they remember afterwards is your scene rather than the text.
Imaginative|Teaching.ask: What do your students recall that was not in the passage?

Imaginative|Tongues.recognize: You are at ease with what cannot be pinned down, which keeps you open where more literal people close. The question is whether you can tell the difference between God and your own inner life.
Imaginative|Tongues.ask: How do you check what you think God said?

Imaginative|Wisdom.recognize: You can run a decision forward and see how it plays out, which spares people from learning the hard way. The limit is that you can run it forward so many ways that no version ever feels solid enough to choose.
Imaginative|Wisdom.ask: What have you modelled a dozen times and never decided?

Independent|Administration.recognize: You need no supervision, so anything handed to you comes back finished and nobody spends a minute checking. The cost is a job done entirely your own way, which nobody else can pick up when you are gone.
Independent|Administration.ask: Who else knows how you do this?

Independent|Apostleship.recognize: You will go somewhere nobody is going and start without a team, which is how some works exist at all. The exposure is a work with no other adult in it, so nothing corrects you.
Independent|Apostleship.ask: Who has permission to tell you that you are wrong?

Independent|Discernment.recognize: You form your own read rather than absorbing the room's, so you catch what a consensus has missed. The cost is a read formed alone, with nothing to check it against but yourself.
Independent|Discernment.ask: Who has ever corrected your read on a person?

Independent|Evangelism.recognize: You will have the conversation without a programme, a team or anybody's permission, which is why yours actually happen. Watch for people who say yes and then have nowhere to go, because you are not attached to anything either.
Independent|Evangelism.ask: Where did you send the last person who said yes?

Independent|Exhortation.recognize: You do not need somebody to be doing well in order to be fine yourself, so your encouragement has no hook in it. The limit is that people who need you to need them slightly will read your steadiness as indifference.
Independent|Exhortation.ask: Who thinks you do not care because you never ask for anything?

Independent|Faith.recognize: Your faith does not depend on a church being good, a leader being right or a group being warm, so it survives what ends other people's. Worth examining is whether it has also stopped needing anybody, which is not what it was for.
Independent|Faith.ask: What part of following Christ requires other people from you?

Independent|Giving.recognize: You give without needing to be part of the thing you are funding, and no strings is genuinely rare. The friction is that giving from a distance is also the version that costs you nothing except money.
Independent|Giving.ask: What have you funded and never turned up to?

Independent|Healing.recognize: You will sit with somebody in trouble without needing anything from the encounter, and people can feel that. What can be missing is your own recovery, because there is nobody you go to.

Independent|Interpretation.recognize: You can keep a reading that the whole room disagrees with, and sometimes the room is wrong. The risk is a conclusion that has never been through anybody else's hands.
Independent|Interpretation.ask: Who last saw your thinking before you had finished it?

Independent|Knowledge.recognize: You will teach yourself anything, so you are never waiting on a course or a mentor. The narrow part is the error you cannot find because it sits in your foundation and nobody has ever looked at it.
Independent|Knowledge.ask: What do you hold confidently that has never been challenged?

Independent|Leadership.recognize: You can carry a decision alone when there is nobody to consult, and some seasons require exactly that. The gap is that deciding alone has become the default rather than the exception.
Independent|Leadership.ask: What was your last decision that somebody else shaped?

Independent|Mercy.recognize: You go to people nobody assigned you, so the ones outside every system get visited. The limit is that your care connects them to nothing, and when you move on they are on their own again.
Independent|Mercy.ask: Who is dependent on you alone?

Independent|Miracles.recognize: You will ask God for something without needing a room to agree it is reasonable. Worth weighing is that the New Testament pattern for this is almost always a group, and yours is almost always alone.
Independent|Miracles.ask: When did you last ask anybody to pray with you?

Independent|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You will care for somebody nobody has taken responsibility for, and you need no title to do it. What is hard to see is that you model a Christian life needing no one, and your people are learning it.
Independent|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What have your people learned from watching you handle trouble?

Independent|Prophecy.recognize: You can say the thing when nobody will back you, which is the condition under which it usually needs saying. The cost is that a word nobody else confirmed is a word nobody else tested.
Independent|Prophecy.ask: Who did you run your last hard word past?

Independent|Service.recognize: You see the job and do it unasked, unassigned and unthanked, and a great deal exists because of that. The friction is that nobody can plan around you, because you also never say what you have taken on.
Independent|Service.ask: What have you taken on that nobody has been told about?

Independent|Teaching.recognize: You prepare your own material from the sources rather than running somebody else's, and it shows. The risk is a body of teaching nobody has reviewed, developing its own quiet emphases.
Independent|Teaching.ask: What do you teach that you have never heard anybody else teach?

Independent|Tongues.recognize: Your spiritual life does not depend on a service, a leader or a room, so it holds up in a hotel and a hospital. The question is whether anything in it has ever required you to submit to somebody.
Independent|Tongues.ask: Who has any say in your walk with God?

Independent|Wisdom.recognize: You will not be talked into a course of action by pressure, which is why your judgement holds up against a crowd. The limit is that a mind this hard to move is also hard to correct.
Independent|Wisdom.ask: When were you last argued out of something?

Informed|Administration.recognize: You know the state of everything without being asked, so the reporting line is really just you. The cost is a meeting that becomes a briefing, where thirty minutes of detail arrives and no decision comes out.
Informed|Administration.ask: What decision did your last update fail to produce?

Informed|Apostleship.recognize: You know what has been tried in comparable places, so a new work does not repeat somebody else's failure. The exposure is a case for waiting, assembled entirely out of what went wrong elsewhere.
Informed|Apostleship.ask: What have you argued against using other people's failures?

Informed|Discernment.recognize: You know the background on everybody, so you can see why a dynamic is happening rather than only that it is. The cost is a person read through their history when they have actually changed.
Informed|Discernment.ask: Whose file in your head is out of date?

Informed|Evangelism.recognize: You know what people are actually thinking about faith because you follow the culture rather than assuming, and your conversations start where they are. Watch for a conversation that stays at the level of what is happening and never reaches Christ.
Informed|Evangelism.ask: When did a conversation last move past the news?

Informed|Exhortation.recognize: You bring somebody the specific thing that speaks to their situation, because you knew it existed. The limit is that information is not the same as being told you can do this.
Informed|Exhortation.ask: Who got a resource from you and needed a sentence?

Informed|Faith.recognize: You know what is happening in the world and have not let it make you cynical, which is harder than either ignorance or despair. Worth examining is how much of what you take in is actually shaping how you pray.
Informed|Faith.ask: What did you read this week and never pray about?

Informed|Giving.recognize: You know which organisations actually work, so your giving does more per dollar than most people's. The friction is that research can become the reason nothing has left your account yet.
Informed|Giving.ask: How long has a gift been waiting on your final check?

Informed|Healing.recognize: You know what the diagnosis means and what the next six months will hold, which is often exactly what a family is desperate for. The limit is that they may not have wanted to know all of it yet.
Informed|Healing.ask: What did you tell a family that they had not asked?

Informed|Interpretation.recognize: You put an event in its context, so a group is not reacting to a headline. The risk is so much context that nobody can see what to do with any of it.
Informed|Interpretation.ask: What did your account leave nobody able to act on?

Informed|Knowledge.recognize: You know where current thinking stands on almost anything that touches your work, and you are rarely out of date. The narrow part is breadth held at the level of the summary, so none of it has ever cost you a year.
Informed|Knowledge.ask: What have you spent a year on?

Informed|Leadership.recognize: Your team is never blindsided, because you saw it coming and you told them. The gap is that a team told everything is a team carrying your anxiety alongside their jobs.
Informed|Leadership.ask: What did you pass on that your team could do nothing about?

Informed|Mercy.recognize: You know what somebody is facing before they have told you, so they do not have to start at the beginning. The limit is that being known can feel like being handled when they never got to say it themselves.
Informed|Mercy.ask: Who never got to tell you their own news?

Informed|Miracles.recognize: You know what is medically and practically feasible, so when something exceeds it you can say so precisely. Worth weighing is whether the knowing has narrowed what you are willing to ask for.
Informed|Miracles.ask: Which prayer did you scale down to something likely?

Informed|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know what is going on in your people's jobs, families and health, and nothing catches you out. What is hard to see is that knowing about somebody is not the same as being with them.
Informed|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who do you know a great deal about and rarely sit with?

Informed|Prophecy.recognize: You can say what is wrong with the facts attached, which makes you very hard to dismiss as merely negative. The cost is a case so well documented that the person hears an indictment rather than a call.
Informed|Prophecy.ask: Who did you assemble a case against?

Informed|Service.recognize: You know what is needed before anybody announces it, so the supplies are there and the gap is filled. The friction is that you also know everything that is not being done, and you say so.
Informed|Service.ask: Who has heard from you about a job that was not theirs?

Informed|Teaching.recognize: Your material is current, so students are not learning something that was superseded a decade ago. The risk is a class that gets the latest rather than the settled, and cannot tell which is which.
Informed|Teaching.ask: What have you taught that you now doubt?

Informed|Tongues.recognize: You have read widely about this rather than reacting from instinct, which keeps you from both credulity and contempt. The question is whether reading about it has become a substitute for doing it.
Informed|Tongues.ask: What do you understand well and have never practised?

Informed|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is grounded in what is actually the case rather than what people assume, and that alone corrects a lot of decisions. The limit is that some situations are not short of information, only of nerve.
Informed|Wisdom.ask: Who left you better informed and no braver?
