Insightful|Administration.recognize: You find the actual cause of a recurring problem while everybody else is managing its symptoms, and the fix you propose usually works. The cost is a fix proposed before the people running it have accepted that there was a problem.
Insightful|Administration.ask: What did you solve before anybody agreed it was broken?

Insightful|Apostleship.recognize: You can tell what a place actually needs rather than what the last church did, which is why your work fits where it lands. The exposure is a diagnosis made in a fortnight and acted on for a decade.
Insightful|Apostleship.ask: What did you decide about this place in your first month?

Insightful|Discernment.recognize: You get to what is really going on with somebody in about four minutes, and you are right often enough that you have stopped checking. The cost falls on the person you were wrong about, who has no way to answer a conclusion you never said out loud.
Insightful|Discernment.ask: Who would be surprised by what you think of them?

Insightful|Evangelism.recognize: You find the real objection underneath the stated one, so a conversation gets somewhere in twenty minutes rather than three years. Watch for an objection identified correctly and answered before they had finished feeling it.
Insightful|Evangelism.ask: Who did you answer too fast?

Insightful|Exhortation.recognize: You name the thing a person cannot see about themselves, and when it lands it can change a life. The risk is naming it in week one of a friendship that had not earned it yet.
Insightful|Exhortation.ask: Who received a hard word from a near-stranger?

Insightful|Faith.recognize: You get to the point of a passage or a season quickly, so you are rarely stuck where other people are stuck. Worth examining is whether anything in your faith has ever taken you years to understand.
Insightful|Faith.ask: What in Scripture have you sat with for more than a month?

Insightful|Giving.recognize: What you give tends to arrive at the thing actually causing the trouble rather than the bill that prompted the call. The friction is that a person who asked for help with the bill can feel diagnosed instead.
Insightful|Giving.ask: Who asked you for one thing and got another?

Insightful|Healing.recognize: You understand what somebody is carrying before they have finished the first sentence, and that is a relief to a person too tired to lay it out. The limit is that saying it aloud takes away the telling, which was part of getting better.
Insightful|Healing.ask: Who never got to finish their own story with you?

Insightful|Interpretation.recognize: You go straight past what is being argued about to what the argument is actually about, and that usually ends it. The risk is a conclusion reached in one step that the room needed to walk through in five.
Insightful|Interpretation.ask: Who did not follow how you got there?

Insightful|Knowledge.recognize: You take in a body of material and come out with the two things that matter, which most people cannot do at any speed. The narrow part is that the discarded material occasionally contained the exception.
Insightful|Knowledge.ask: What did you skim that turned out to matter?

Insightful|Leadership.recognize: You understand a situation faster than your team can be brought along, and your calls are usually right. The gap is a team executing a decision they never saw the reasoning for, which works until it does not.
Insightful|Leadership.ask: Who is following a decision they do not understand?

Insightful|Mercy.recognize: You reach what is underneath somebody's distress rather than what they are presenting, and that lets you meet the real thing. The limit is that a person sometimes needs the surface honoured before anything below it is touched.
Insightful|Mercy.ask: Whose stated problem did you go straight past?

Insightful|Miracles.recognize: You see how a thing might come together when nobody else can, and more than once that has been faith rather than cleverness. Worth weighing is whether you would recognise an answer that made no sense to you.
Insightful|Miracles.ask: When did an answer arrive in a form you did not recognise?

Insightful|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You understand your people better than they understand themselves, which is why they come to you. What is hard is that being understood without being asked can feel like being read rather than known.
Insightful|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who have you never actually questioned?

Insightful|Prophecy.recognize: You reach the root of what is wrong rather than the incident everybody is discussing, and that is the difference between a complaint and a word. The cost is arriving there so fast that nobody can trace the path with you.
Insightful|Prophecy.ask: What landed as an accusation because you skipped the middle?

Insightful|Service.recognize: You can tell what actually needs doing rather than what has been asked for, so your work is never wasted. The friction is the person who wanted their request honoured, not improved.
Insightful|Service.ask: Whose instructions did you quietly override?

Insightful|Teaching.recognize: You get to the heart of a subject in one session, which is a gift to anybody with limited time. The risk is students who received your conclusion and never developed the ability to reach one.
Insightful|Teaching.ask: Who can repeat your point and not rebuild it?

Insightful|Tongues.recognize: You understand what is happening in a room spiritually while others are still working out how they feel. The question is whether understanding it has become a substitute for being in it.
Insightful|Tongues.ask: When did you last take part rather than assess?

Insightful|Wisdom.recognize: Your read on a situation is usually right and usually fast, and people rely on that combination. The limit is that being right early is not the same as being useful, and some people need to arrive at it themselves.
Insightful|Wisdom.ask: Who needed to get there themselves?

Kind and Encouraging|Administration.recognize: You deliver a process change without making anybody feel accused, so the change actually takes. The cost is a problem described so gently that nobody understood it has to stop.
Kind and Encouraging|Administration.ask: What did you raise so carefully that nothing changed?

Kind and Encouraging|Apostleship.recognize: You make a new team feel valued before there is anything to show for the work, and that is what carries a launch. The exposure is that praise for effort can outlast the point where results were needed.
Kind and Encouraging|Apostleship.ask: Who is being praised for work that is producing nothing?

Kind and Encouraging|Discernment.recognize: You see what is admirable in somebody that they have never been told, and telling them can change how they carry themselves. The cost is that you see the other thing too, and you have decided it is not your place.
Kind and Encouraging|Discernment.ask: What have you seen and filed as none of your business?

Kind and Encouraging|Evangelism.recognize: People feel safe enough with you to say what they actually believe, which is where any real conversation begins. Watch for a safety so complete that nothing is ever put to them.
Kind and Encouraging|Evangelism.ask: Who has felt accepted by you for years and never been asked anything?

Kind and Encouraging|Exhortation.recognize: You find the true good thing to say at the moment somebody most needs to hear it, which is a real gift rather than flattery. The risk is that a person who only ever hears the good thing stops believing you about any of it.
Kind and Encouraging|Exhortation.ask: Who would believe you if you praised them tomorrow?

Kind and Encouraging|Faith.recognize: You protect people from cynicism about the church, and a lot of faith has survived in your orbit because of it. Worth examining is whether you are protecting them or protecting yourself from the conversation.
Kind and Encouraging|Faith.ask: What about your church have you never let anybody say out loud?

Kind and Encouraging|Giving.recognize: You give in a way that leaves the person's dignity intact, which is most of whether help can be received at all. The friction is that dignity is sometimes preserved by never naming what caused this, and it will cause it again.
Kind and Encouraging|Giving.ask: Who have you helped without ever naming the pattern?

Kind and Encouraging|Healing.recognize: You are gentle with people in the worst weeks of their lives, and gentleness is not a small thing. The limit is that some recoveries need a hard conversation and you are not the one who will have it.
Kind and Encouraging|Healing.ask: Who needed a harder friend than you?

Kind and Encouraging|Interpretation.recognize: You put a charitable frame on what happened, and often that frame is the accurate one. The risk is a frame chosen to spare somebody, which leaves the group working from a version that is not true.
Kind and Encouraging|Interpretation.ask: What have you framed so gently the group got it wrong?

Kind and Encouraging|Knowledge.recognize: You put somebody right without making them feel stupid, which is why people are willing to learn from you. The narrow part is an error left standing because fixing it would have cost more warmth than you had that day.
Kind and Encouraging|Knowledge.ask: What mistake have you let stand?

Kind and Encouraging|Leadership.recognize: Your people are certain you are for them, and that belief will carry a team through a bad year. The gap is that being for somebody includes telling them they are failing, and you have deferred that with somebody specific.
Kind and Encouraging|Leadership.ask: Who on your team does not realise they are struggling?

Kind and Encouraging|Mercy.recognize: You have never made anybody feel like a burden, which to a person in a long illness is close to everything. The limit is that being easy to lean on can keep somebody in a state they should be moving out of.
Kind and Encouraging|Mercy.ask: Who has settled into needing you?

Kind and Encouraging|Miracles.recognize: You hold on to hope for other people when their own has gone, and that is a real ministry. Worth weighing is whether you would ever tell somebody plainly that this particular thing is not going to happen.
Kind and Encouraging|Miracles.ask: What have you let somebody keep hoping for?

Kind and Encouraging|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People are not afraid of you, so they tell you things they tell nobody else. What that access is for is the harder half of care, and access is easier to keep if you never use it.
Kind and Encouraging|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What have you been trusted with and done nothing about?

Kind and Encouraging|Prophecy.recognize: When you do say a hard thing it lands with unusual weight, because nobody can accuse you of enjoying it. The cost is how rarely you spend that, and how much has gone unsaid as a result.
Kind and Encouraging|Prophecy.ask: How long since you said something difficult?

Kind and Encouraging|Service.recognize: You make people glad they volunteered, which is why yours come back. The friction is the volunteer who is not doing the job and has been thanked for it four times.
Kind and Encouraging|Service.ask: Who is doing this badly and has never been told?

Kind and Encouraging|Teaching.recognize: Nobody leaves your class feeling small, and people learn far more when they are not defending themselves. The risk is a class that has never been told they are wrong about anything.
Kind and Encouraging|Teaching.ask: What error do your students still hold?

Kind and Encouraging|Tongues.recognize: You make room for people whose spiritual experience is unlike yours without making them feel odd, and that keeps a church together. The question is whether you would say so if you thought something was not from God.
Kind and Encouraging|Tongues.ask: What have you accommodated that troubles you?

Kind and Encouraging|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice arrives without judgement, so people tell you the whole situation before you give any. The limit is advice shaped by not wanting to add to their load, which is a poor guide to what is true.
Kind and Encouraging|Wisdom.ask: What did you soften because they were already struggling?

Knowledgeable|Administration.recognize: You carry the history of how everything came to be the way it is, so decisions are not made in ignorance of what has already been tried. The cost is an institution whose memory lives in one person and argues from it.
Knowledgeable|Administration.ask: What has not been reconsidered because you remember why?

Knowledgeable|Apostleship.recognize: You bring the accumulated learning of other works to a new one, so it starts further along than it otherwise would. The exposure is a template applied to a place that did not fit it.
Knowledgeable|Apostleship.ask: What did you import that this place did not need?

Knowledgeable|Discernment.recognize: You have seen enough situations to recognise the shape of this one, and that recognition is often what saves it. The cost is a person filed under a pattern you met fifteen years ago.
Knowledgeable|Discernment.ask: Who reminds you of somebody, and is being treated accordingly?

Knowledgeable|Evangelism.recognize: You can answer the hard question rather than deflecting it, and a thinking person will not move until somebody does. Watch for an answer that satisfied you and never touched what they were actually asking.
Knowledgeable|Evangelism.ask: Who got a good answer and stayed exactly where they were?

Knowledgeable|Exhortation.recognize: You can tell somebody that what they are going through has a name and that other people have come out of it, which is enormously settling. The limit is that being told it is common can land as being told it is small.
Knowledgeable|Exhortation.ask: Who felt diminished by your reassurance?

Knowledgeable|Faith.recognize: You have read enough to hold your faith with your eyes open, and that is worth more than an untested confidence. Worth examining is whether anything you believe still costs you something to hold.
Knowledgeable|Faith.ask: What do you believe that has cost you?

Knowledgeable|Giving.recognize: You understand where money actually goes, so nothing you give is wasted on a well-marketed failure. The friction is that being right about this can become a reason to give less.
Knowledgeable|Giving.ask: What did your judgement talk you out of funding?

Knowledgeable|Healing.recognize: You can tell a frightened family what is likely, and being told what is likely is often the first rest they get. The limit is that confidence about the general case tells them nothing about theirs.
Knowledgeable|Healing.ask: Whose particular case did you answer generally?

Knowledgeable|Interpretation.recognize: You can place a situation in a wider frame, so a group stops treating an ordinary difficulty as unprecedented. The risk is a frame that fits so well nobody examines what is different this time.
Knowledgeable|Interpretation.ask: What is new about this that you have treated as familiar?

Knowledgeable|Knowledge.recognize: What you have accumulated is real and was paid for in hours, and your church is better for somebody having it. The narrow part is a reflex to supply the missing detail, which shifts a room's attention from the point to the footnote.
Knowledgeable|Knowledge.ask: When did you last let a small error pass?

Knowledgeable|Leadership.recognize: Your team never has to research what has already been settled, because you carry it. The gap is that a leader who always has the answer removes the reason for anybody else to develop one.
Knowledgeable|Leadership.ask: Who on your team has had to work something out alone this year?

Knowledgeable|Mercy.recognize: You can tell somebody exactly what happens next, and to a person in chaos a map is mercy. The limit is that a map is not presence.
Knowledgeable|Mercy.ask: Who wanted you beside them and got a briefing?

Knowledgeable|Miracles.recognize: You are hard to fool, so your account of something unexplained carries weight with people who dismiss most of it. Worth weighing is whether you have ruled out whole categories rather than particular instances.
Knowledgeable|Miracles.ask: What have you decided in advance cannot happen?

Knowledgeable|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People bring you their questions and get a real answer rather than a reassurance, which is why they keep coming. What is hard to see is that some of them came with a question in order to be asked one back.
Knowledgeable|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who asked you something and needed to be asked something?

Knowledgeable|Prophecy.recognize: You can say what is wrong and cite where it has gone wrong before, which makes the warning very hard to wave away. The cost is a habit of establishing that you are right, which is a different aim than being heard.
Knowledgeable|Prophecy.ask: What did you win that you needed to land?

Knowledgeable|Service.recognize: You are the one who understands how the thing actually works, so nothing gets broken by well-meaning help. The friction is a reflex to say what was done wrong, arriving at the end of somebody's long Saturday.
Knowledgeable|Service.ask: Who finished a job and heard what they had missed?

Knowledgeable|Teaching.recognize: Your class is never thin, because you have far more than you are using and it shows in what you leave out. The risk is a lesson pitched at the two people who could follow all of it.
Knowledgeable|Teaching.ask: Who stopped following your class and did not say?

Knowledgeable|Tongues.recognize: You have studied what the text actually says about this rather than inheriting a position, which is rare on either side of it. The question is whether study has become the way you avoid the practice.
Knowledgeable|Tongues.ask: What have you concluded is legitimate and never done?

Knowledgeable|Wisdom.recognize: You have enough precedent in your head that your advice is rarely naive, and people are right to seek it. The limit is that a situation with no precedent is exactly the one somebody most needs help with.
Knowledgeable|Wisdom.ask: What have you been asked that you could not answer?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Administrat.recognize: The thing you took on eleven years ago still runs and nobody has thought about it since, which is the highest compliment an operation can receive. The cost is that nobody has thought about it since.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Administrat.ask: What have you carried so long that nobody remembers it is a job?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Apostleship.recognize: A new work needs somebody who will still be there in year four, and most of the people who start are gone by then. The exposure is remaining with something long after it stopped being what you signed up for.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Apostleship.ask: What are you still part of out of loyalty alone?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Discernment.recognize: You give people time rather than a verdict, so your read is built out of years instead of an afternoon. The cost is that you can see what somebody is doing and go on absorbing it.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Discernment.ask: Who have you been putting up with?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Evangelism.recognize: You are still praying for the same person after fifteen years, and that is how most people actually come in. Watch for a patience that has become a way of never having the conversation.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Evangelism.ask: How long since the subject came up between you?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Exhortation.recognize: You are the one still there after the crisis has passed and the interest has gone, which is when most people need somebody. The limit is that continued presence can substitute for saying the thing that would move them.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Exhortation.ask: What have you never said to somebody you have supported for years?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Faith.recognize: Your faith has survived seasons where nothing was happening, which is where most faith is actually lost. Worth examining is whether you are trusting God or simply carrying on because you do not quit things.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Faith.ask: When did God last actually meet you?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Giving.recognize: Your giving has arrived every month for years, and an organisation can plan around people like you in a way it cannot plan around a large gift. The friction is a commitment that continues after the thing it funds has drifted.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Giving.ask: What are you funding that you have not looked at recently?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Healing.recognize: You are there for all of the recovery rather than the dramatic part, and long illness is mostly the undramatic part. The limit is your own cost, which you will not mention because mentioning it would feel like a complaint.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Healing.ask: What has this cost you that you have never said?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Interpretat.recognize: You will not conclude early, so your account of a long-running situation is more accurate than anybody's. The risk is a reading so slow to form that the moment for it passed.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Interpretat.ask: What did you understand too late to say?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Knowledge.recognize: You will work through material for as long as it takes rather than finding the shortcut, so what you learn is properly yours. The narrow part is a subject you have been in for years that has stopped yielding anything.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Knowledge.ask: What have you been studying past the point of return?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Leadership.recognize: You do not leave when it gets hard, and your team feels that in their bones. The gap is that remaining is not the same as leading, and some situations need somebody to change them rather than outlast them.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Leadership.ask: What situation have you survived rather than changed?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Mercy.recognize: You are still visiting the person everybody else has stopped visiting, which is most of what mercy actually is. The limit is that some situations continue precisely because everybody involved is coping.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Mercy.ask: What is bearable now that should have been an emergency?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Miracles.recognize: You keep asking for the same thing for years without needing an answer in order to continue, which is the pattern Jesus actually commended. Worth weighing is whether you would recognise the answer if it came in another form.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Miracles.ask: What have you asked for so long you stopped looking for it?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Pastor/Shep.recognize: Your people have had the same shepherd for a decade, and that continuity does something no programme can. What is hard to see is the person you have been carrying who should have been handed on.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Pastor/Shep.ask: Who is your responsibility only because they always have been?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Prophecy.recognize: You have been saying the same thing quietly for years, and there is a weight to that which a single outburst never has. The cost is that quiet repetition is easy for an organisation to absorb without changing anything.

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Service.recognize: You have not missed a Sunday, and the whole rota is built on the assumption that you will be there. The friction is that you would come in ill rather than ask somebody to cover.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Service.ask: Who has ever taken your Sunday?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Teaching.recognize: Your class has had you for years, so they will tell you things a visiting teacher would never hear. The risk is a class that has outgrown you and will not say so out of affection.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Teaching.ask: Who should have moved on from your class?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Tongues.recognize: You have kept the same practice through dry years without needing it to produce anything, a discipline most people cannot manage. The question is whether it has become something you do rather than something you mean.
Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Tongues.ask: When did this last feel like anything?

Loyal, Patient, and Reliable|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice comes from having watched things play out across decades rather than from theory, which is why it holds. The limit is a preference for waiting, right most of the time and catastrophic occasionally.

Observant|Administration.recognize: You notice the small irregularity in the numbers that turns out to be the whole problem, weeks before it surfaces anywhere else. The cost is a finding you sat on because you were not certain enough to raise it.
Observant|Administration.ask: What is in the numbers that you have kept to yourself?

Observant|Apostleship.recognize: You read a new community accurately rather than assuming it is like the last one, which is why what you start actually fits. The exposure is a launch that never happens because you can still see something you have not accounted for.
Observant|Apostleship.ask: What are you waiting to understand before you begin?

Observant|Discernment.recognize: You see the thing everybody else missed, the glance, the absence, the change in somebody's routine. The cost is a great deal seen and very little said, which helps nobody.
Observant|Discernment.ask: What have you seen this month and told no one?

Observant|Evangelism.recognize: You can tell when somebody is ready to talk about God, and you are almost never wrong about it. What happens too often is a reading taken correctly and then not used, and the moment closes.
Observant|Evangelism.ask: Who was ready and you said nothing?

Observant|Exhortation.recognize: You notice what a person has done that nobody else registered, and being seen is most of what encouragement is. The limit is that noticing happens in your head and does not reach them unless you speak.
Observant|Exhortation.ask: Whose good work has never reached them from you?

Observant|Faith.recognize: You take in what God is doing rather than announcing what you intend to do, and that receptivity is scriptural. Worth examining is whether attention has become the whole of your obedience.
Observant|Faith.ask: What have you understood and not obeyed?

Observant|Giving.recognize: You notice the need nobody announced, the coat, the car, the absence at a paid event. The friction is a need seen and considered for so long that somebody else met it first.
Observant|Giving.ask: What did you consider giving and not give?

Observant|Healing.recognize: You can tell how somebody actually is rather than how they said they are, which is the central difficulty with hurting people. The limit is that seeing it does nothing for them until you say it aloud.
Observant|Healing.ask: Who is not fine and has no idea you can tell?

Observant|Interpretation.recognize: You have the details right, so your account of what happened is usually the reliable one. The risk is holding an accurate account back because you have not yet decided what it adds up to.
Observant|Interpretation.ask: What account of yours has never been given?

Observant|Knowledge.recognize: You gather far more than you were asked to, and the detail you picked up in passing is often the one that mattered. The narrow part is a finding that stayed in your notebook because nobody requested it.
Observant|Knowledge.ask: What is in your notes that nobody has seen?

Observant|Leadership.recognize: You can tell how your team actually is rather than what they report in a meeting, and you work from the real version. The gap is a leader who sees a problem forming and gives it another fortnight.
Observant|Leadership.ask: What have you been giving another fortnight for six months?

Observant|Mercy.recognize: You catch the person who is not coping while everybody else is attending to the one who said so. The limit is that catching it and going over are two different acts, and the second is the one that helps.
Observant|Mercy.ask: Who did you notice and not approach?

Observant|Miracles.recognize: You would be a credible witness to anything, because you are careful about what you claim to have seen. Worth weighing is whether care has become the reason you never ask for anything out loud.
Observant|Miracles.ask: What prayer have you rehearsed and never prayed aloud?

Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You can tell which of your people is different this month, and you can tell before they have said anything. What that is for is the conversation, which requires you to go first.
Observant|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who are you concerned about and have not called?

Observant|Prophecy.recognize: What you say rests on something you actually saw rather than a feeling, which is why it is hard to argue with. The cost is a pattern of gathering evidence long past the point where it needed saying.
Observant|Prophecy.ask: How long have you been collecting this?

Observant|Service.recognize: You see what needs doing without being told, down to the detail nobody would have specified. The friction is standing at the edge of a job waiting to be sure that it is yours.
Observant|Service.ask: What did you leave undone because nobody asked you?

Observant|Teaching.recognize: You can tell from the room who has understood and who is nodding, which is information most teachers never get. The risk is having that information and continuing to the end of the material anyway.
Observant|Teaching.ask: When did you last stop because a face told you to?

Observant|Tongues.recognize: You notice what is actually happening in a service rather than what is being said about it, and that keeps you honest. The question is whether you have ever been a participant rather than an audience.
Observant|Tongues.ask: What have you never joined in because you were assessing it?

Observant|Wisdom.recognize: Your judgement rests on more evidence than anybody else has, because you were paying attention when it did not matter yet. The limit is that a decision delayed until you are sure is often a decision made by default.
Observant|Wisdom.ask: What did you fail to decide in time?

Open-Minded|Administration.recognize: You will run somebody else's idea properly rather than only your own, so good proposals from junior people actually get tried. The cost is a process changed three times in a year because each new suggestion was reasonable.
Open-Minded|Administration.ask: What version of this are you on?

Open-Minded|Apostleship.recognize: You can start a work without needing it to resemble the church you came from, which is why yours reaches people the last one did not. The exposure is a work with no settled shape, which is exhausting for everybody inside it.
Open-Minded|Apostleship.ask: What about your work has been the same for two years?

Open-Minded|Discernment.recognize: You will revise your read on somebody when new information arrives, which most people simply do not do. The cost is a person who keeps getting another chance because you can always see their side.
Open-Minded|Discernment.ask: Who has had more chances from you than they should have?

Open-Minded|Evangelism.recognize: You can hear an objection without defending, and people will say things to you they would never say to a Christian who argues. What happens sometimes is a conversation where you conceded so much that nothing was left to come to.
Open-Minded|Evangelism.ask: Where did you agree with them against yourself?

Open-Minded|Exhortation.recognize: You take seriously what somebody says they want rather than telling them what they should want, and they can feel the difference. The limit is that some people need you to hold a line they are trying to talk you out of.
Open-Minded|Exhortation.ask: Who talked you out of a challenge?

Open-Minded|Faith.recognize: You can hold a question without needing it closed, which keeps you honest where a quicker answer would have been easier. Worth examining is whether anything is actually settled, because a life needs something underneath it.

Open-Minded|Giving.recognize: You will fund something that does not match your own convictions when the need is real, which is rarer than it should be. The friction is a giving pattern with no shape, so nothing you support ever gets enough to matter.
Open-Minded|Giving.ask: What have you given enough to actually change?

Open-Minded|Healing.recognize: You do not tell somebody what their experience signifies, so people describe things to you they have not said elsewhere. The limit is that at some point they need somebody to say what they think is happening.
Open-Minded|Healing.ask: Who left without the answer they came for?

Open-Minded|Interpretation.recognize: You can hold two accounts of the same event without collapsing them, which is why both sides talk to you. The risk is a group that needed a decision and got a survey.
Open-Minded|Interpretation.ask: What decision is still open because you can see both sides?

Open-Minded|Knowledge.recognize: You will follow evidence that goes against what you thought, which alone puts you ahead of most people who study anything. The narrow part is a position revised so often that nothing has ever been built on it.
Open-Minded|Knowledge.ask: What conclusion of yours has survived five years?

Open-Minded|Leadership.recognize: Your team can bring you anything, and they do, so you hear about problems while they are still small. The gap is that a leader who can be moved by the last good argument leaves a team unable to plan.
Open-Minded|Leadership.ask: What did your team stop planning around because you might change it?

Open-Minded|Mercy.recognize: You do not require somebody's grief to look like grief, which is why people who are not doing it properly come to you. The limit is that acceptance without direction can leave a person exactly where you found them.
Open-Minded|Mercy.ask: Who has been stuck in the same place through all your conversations?

Open-Minded|Miracles.recognize: You have ruled nothing out, so you can receive what God does without needing it to fit a category. Worth weighing is whether you would ever say that something was not Him.
Open-Minded|Miracles.ask: When did you last call something a work of God?

Open-Minded|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People with unusual histories can be themselves around you, and a church without somebody like that loses them all. What can be missing is a standard, because care with no shape eventually stops being care.
Open-Minded|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who is still doing the thing you have accepted?

Open-Minded|Prophecy.recognize: You consider that you might be wrong before you speak, so what you do say has been through something. The cost is a word so qualified by the time it arrives that nobody feels addressed by it.
Open-Minded|Prophecy.ask: What word of yours arrived with all the corners taken off?

Open-Minded|Service.recognize: You will do the job however the person wants it done rather than however you would do it, which makes you easy to work alongside. The friction is a job done badly because you deferred to somebody who was wrong.
Open-Minded|Service.ask: What did you go along with that you should have stopped?

Open-Minded|Teaching.recognize: You present positions you do not hold fairly enough that a student cannot tell which is yours, and that produces people who can think. The risk is a class that never finds out what you believe and concludes it does not matter.
Open-Minded|Teaching.ask: Do your students have any idea where you stand?

Open-Minded|Tongues.recognize: You are willing to be wrong about this in either direction, which is unusual on a subject where almost everybody has already decided. The question is whether willingness has ever turned into asking God for anything.
Open-Minded|Tongues.ask: What have you been willing to receive and never requested?

Open-Minded|Wisdom.recognize: You give people the considerations rather than the answer, and to somebody capable that is the better gift. The limit is the person who cannot carry that many considerations and needed you to choose.
Open-Minded|Wisdom.ask: Who left you with more options than they arrived with?

Organized and Effective|Administration.recognize: You map the work before anyone starts, and by the time the team arrives every step has an owner and a date. Things run. What you cannot tell from inside is how little room is left for someone to do it a different way.
Organized and Effective|Administration.ask: When did a volunteer last change how something ran on your watch?

Organized and Effective|Apostleship.recognize: You do not just want the work started, you want it started well, so the schedule and the roles exist before the first meeting. Ground gets covered fast. The risk is that a young thing is handed a shape it has not grown into yet.
Organized and Effective|Apostleship.ask: What did you set up before you knew what the work would need?

Organized and Effective|Discernment.recognize: You notice what is off in a room and your instinct is to fix it with a better arrangement, a new rota, a clearer brief. Often that works. What gets missed is that some of what you sense is spiritual and no rearrangement will touch it.
Organized and Effective|Discernment.ask: What did you reorganize last, when you should have prayed?

Organized and Effective|Evangelism.recognize: You build a path for someone toward faith with real care, the right conversation, the right event, the right person to meet them. Many have walked it. What you may not notice is when a soul stops being a person and becomes a sequence running late.
Organized and Effective|Evangelism.ask: Who are you following up with because they are overdue?

Organized and Effective|Exhortation.recognize: You do not just tell someone to keep going, you hand them the next three moves and a date to check back. People get going because you made it concrete. The cost is that a person who needed to be believed in was given a task list.
Organized and Effective|Exhortation.ask: Who did you give a to-do to when they needed to be heard?

Organized and Effective|Faith.recognize: You are willing to move on something unproven, but only once you have mapped what happens if it fails. That has saved good ventures. What you cannot always tell is when the mapping quietly became the reason you have not moved yet.
Organized and Effective|Faith.ask: What has God asked of you that you are still preparing for?

Organized and Effective|Giving.recognize: Your generosity arrives with a structure around it, a budget line, a schedule, a defined need. Nothing is wasted and nobody is embarrassed. What is harder to notice is that a gift with conditions on it still has your hand on the other end.
Organized and Effective|Giving.ask: What did you last give with no say in how it was used?

Organized and Effective|Healing.recognize: You meet a broken person with a workable first move, who to call, what to do this week, and often that is exactly the mercy they needed. What is invisible from where you stand is that a next step can be handed over to end a conversation you did not want to sit in.
Organized and Effective|Healing.ask: Who did you send somewhere instead of sitting with?

Organized and Effective|Interpretation.recognize: You take something tangled, a sermon, a season, a hard word, and lay it out so a person can hold it. They leave clearer than they came. The danger is that the frame you laid it in became the only shape it is allowed to have.
Organized and Effective|Interpretation.ask: Who has offered you a different reading of the same passage lately?

Organized and Effective|Knowledge.recognize: You do not just study a thing, you file it, notes, categories, a system you can pull from years later. That store has served a lot of people. What is easy to miss is that filing something can feel so much like finishing it that you never had to live it.
Organized and Effective|Knowledge.ask: What have you written down and never actually obeyed?

Organized and Effective|Leadership.recognize: People follow you because with you there is always a way forward already laid out, and it usually works. What you cannot feel from the front is how many of them have stopped bringing you their own thinking, because yours arrives complete.
Organized and Effective|Leadership.ask: Whose thinking did you build on last, instead of your own?

Organized and Effective|Mercy.recognize: When someone is suffering you get practical fast, meals arranged, rides covered, a rota of people checking in. The care is real and it lasts. What you may not notice is that organizing the help keeps you busy at the edge of a grief you never have to enter.
Organized and Effective|Mercy.ask: Who received meals from you and never a visit?

Organized and Effective|Miracles.recognize: You pray for the impossible and then get to work on the parts you can handle yourself, which is why things around you tend to move. The blind spot is that the parts you can handle have slowly grown until nothing is left that only God could do.
Organized and Effective|Miracles.ask: What are you asking God for that your own effort cannot reach?

Organized and Effective|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people are looked after in a way they can count on. Someone checks on them, nobody falls through, and it is quiet and faithful work. What you cannot see is how much of their life you are holding a slot for, and how little of it they now carry themselves.
Organized and Effective|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Which person in your care last made a decision without telling you?

Organized and Effective|Prophecy.recognize: When something is wrong you name it, but you bring the remedy in the same breath, so it lands as a proposal rather than a rebuke. That has spared people. It also means a hard thing has sometimes been softened into a scheduling problem.
Organized and Effective|Prophecy.ask: What did you turn into a fixable issue that was actually sin?

Organized and Effective|Service.recognize: You serve by making the work possible for everyone else, the run sheet, the setup, the list on the wall. Nothing you touch stays chaotic. The part you cannot feel is how much of your worth now rides on the day going smoothly.
Organized and Effective|Service.ask: How did you feel the last time something you ran went badly?

Organized and Effective|Teaching.recognize: Your lessons are built to be followed, numbered, sequenced, nothing missing, and people can take notes and use them on Monday. What is hidden from you is that a room following a structure is not the same as a room being changed by it.
Organized and Effective|Teaching.ask: Who in your last class understood you and did nothing?

Organized and Effective|Tongues.recognize: You bring shape even to your prayer life, a set hour, a rhythm, a way you know works. It has kept you praying when feeling did not. The cost is that God is rarely allowed to interrupt something you have already assigned to another purpose.
Organized and Effective|Tongues.ask: When did prayer last run long and ruin your morning?

Organized and Effective|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you decisions because your advice comes with a route attached: do this, then this. It is genuinely useful and it saves them months. What you cannot see is how often the route was ready before you had finished listening.
Organized and Effective|Wisdom.ask: Who came to you last week, and what did they actually say?

Original|Administration.recognize: You cannot run a system the way you inherited it, so you rebuild it into something nobody has seen, and it usually does work better. What is hard to notice is how much energy the people under it spend relearning a thing that was already fine.
Original|Administration.ask: What did you rebuild last that was not broken?

Original|Apostleship.recognize: You go where nothing exists yet, because untouched ground is the only place your instincts run free. Real work begins that way. The blind spot is that you are drawn to the beginning of things, and the beginning is also the easiest part to walk away from.
Original|Apostleship.ask: Which of your beginnings is still waiting on somebody else?

Original|Discernment.recognize: You take an angle on a situation that nobody else is taking, and yours is usually the one that turns out to matter. What you cannot check from inside is whether you landed there because it was true or because it was the one position still available.
Original|Discernment.ask: When did you last agree with the obvious answer?

Original|Evangelism.recognize: You will not use the script, so you find your own way in, and people who would never walk into a church will listen to you. The cost is that the gospel can arrive so wrapped in your own strangeness that some of them are following the wrapping.
Original|Evangelism.ask: Who did you reach who never found their way to a church?

Original|Exhortation.recognize: You never say the encouraging thing everyone else says, so when you speak, people believe it. That is rare. What you cannot feel is the moment you kept back the ordinary word someone badly needed, because it was ordinary.
Original|Exhortation.ask: Who needed a plain word from you and got a clever one?

Original|Faith.recognize: Your faith does not run on the well-worn assurances. You had to find your own reasons and they hold, which makes you unshakeable in odd places. The blind spot is that a faith worked out alone has never once been corrected.
Original|Faith.ask: Who has the standing to tell you that you are wrong about God?

Original|Giving.recognize: You give in ways nobody thought of, the odd need, the person no fund covers, the gift that fits no category. It reaches places giving usually misses. What is harder to admit is that the unusual gift is also the one nobody can hold you to.
Original|Giving.ask: What have you given that showed up in no record anywhere?

Original|Healing.recognize: You come at a hurting person from an angle they have not heard, and it reaches them when the standard words had stopped working. The risk is treating a wound as a puzzle that deserves your most interesting answer rather than your most patient one.
Original|Healing.ask: Who needed the ordinary kind thing said, and did not get it?

Original|Interpretation.recognize: You will not repeat the reading you were handed, so you go back to the text yourself and come out somewhere unexpected, and it is often right. What you cannot judge from inside is how much of the church's long agreement you have quietly set aside.
Original|Interpretation.ask: Which of your readings has no one else in history held?

Original|Knowledge.recognize: You chase the question nobody is asking, which is why you know things nobody around you knows. That has been worth a great deal. The cost is that the settled ground everyone else stands on is the ground you have never actually studied.
Original|Knowledge.ask: What basic thing have you never learned properly?

Original|Leadership.recognize: You lead by taking people somewhere they would not have gone, and they follow because you are never dull. What is invisible from the front is how tired they get when nothing they built last year is still standing this year.
Original|Leadership.ask: What have you left running unchanged for two years?

Original|Mercy.recognize: You show up for the person everyone else has stopped noticing, because the overlooked one is the one you are drawn to. That kindness is real. The blind spot is the ordinary sufferer in your own house who is not interesting enough to draw it.
Original|Mercy.ask: Who at home has stopped getting the version of you strangers get?

Original|Miracles.recognize: You believe God still does things that appear in nobody's handbook, and you pray accordingly, and that belief has opened doors. What you cannot always tell is whether you are seeking God or seeking a story nobody has heard before.
Original|Miracles.ask: Would you still want it if nobody ever heard about it?

Original|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You care for people in ways that fit them and not a program, so nobody in your circle feels processed. It is a rare thing to receive. The cost is that when you are unavailable there is no shared practice for anyone to fall back on.
Original|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What would your people do next week if you vanished tomorrow?

Original|Prophecy.recognize: You say the thing the room has agreed not to say, and you say it so that nobody can dismiss it as the usual complaint. It lands. What you cannot see is that being the lone voice has become part of how you know you are right.
Original|Prophecy.ask: When did you last speak up and turn out to be mistaken?

Original|Service.recognize: You find the job nobody assigned and do it in a way nobody would have thought of, and things improve. What is harder to notice is how often the assigned, dull, needed job stayed undone while you were improving something else.
Original|Service.ask: What boring task have you avoided in the last month?

Original|Teaching.recognize: You will not teach it the way you were taught it, so your class remembers your illustrations for years. The blind spot is that memorable and formative are not the same, and only one of them survives you.
Original|Teaching.ask: What has a student of yours carried into their life, not just recalled?

Original|Tongues.recognize: Your prayer life has never looked like anyone else's, and that kept it honest for you on the days borrowed words felt hollow. What you cannot check alone is whether a practice answerable to nobody is still being shaped by God.
Original|Tongues.ask: Who has ever prayed alongside you long enough to know?

Original|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you when the usual advice has failed, because you will find an angle nobody offered, and that has rescued situations. What is hidden from you is that some problems only ever had the boring answer, and you talked someone out of it.
Original|Wisdom.ask: Who did you steer away from the obvious right answer?

Passionate|Administration.recognize: You care enough about the mission to build the machinery it needs, which is rare. Most people with your intensity will not sit down with a spreadsheet. What you cannot feel is how your intensity lands on the volunteer who cares about it a normal amount.
Passionate|Administration.ask: Who left your team because they could not match you?

Passionate|Apostleship.recognize: You will go to the hard place and stay when it costs, because the work is not a project to you, it is the thing you are for. The blind spot is that intensity travels and rest does not, and nothing has been arranged for year three.
Passionate|Apostleship.ask: What will keep you in this work when the heat goes out?

Passionate|Discernment.recognize: You feel when something is wrong before you can argue it, and you feel it strongly, which is why you act while others are still weighing. What is hard to admit is that strength of feeling and accuracy of judgment are not the same thing.
Passionate|Discernment.ask: When were you sure about someone and wrong?

Passionate|Evangelism.recognize: Nobody doubts that you mean it, and that conviction is what makes strangers listen to you at all. The cost is that heat is hard to say no to, and some people agreed with you because the room got uncomfortable, not because they believed.
Passionate|Evangelism.ask: Who said yes to you and never came back?

Passionate|Exhortation.recognize: When you tell someone they can do it, they feel it in their chest, because you are not being polite, you actually believe it. What you cannot see is the person who could not tell you they were not going to try, and stopped answering instead.
Passionate|Exhortation.ask: Who stopped replying to you after you pushed them?

Passionate|Faith.recognize: Your faith is not an opinion you hold, it is the thing driving the car, and people are steadied by watching it. The blind spot is that heat this strong does not distinguish well between what God said and what you badly want.
Passionate|Faith.ask: What did you believe God promised that never came?

Passionate|Giving.recognize: You give the way you feel, fast, generously, sometimes past what you have, and people have been carried by it. What is harder to notice is who at home absorbed the shortfall you created for somebody else's need.
Passionate|Giving.ask: What did your family go without so you could give?

Passionate|Healing.recognize: You throw yourself at a hurting person and they feel the force of being cared about, which by itself does some good. The cost is that you take their pain into yourself and then need them to get better so that you can stop hurting.
Passionate|Healing.ask: Whose recovery are you needing more than they are?

Passionate|Interpretation.recognize: Scripture is not information to you, and when you open it up for people they can hear that it has cost you something. What you cannot judge from inside is when the heat you brought to the text was actually the heat you brought from your week.
Passionate|Interpretation.ask: What were you angry about the last time you taught?

Passionate|Knowledge.recognize: You do not study casually. You go at a subject until it is in your bones, and people trust what you know because of it. The blind spot is that you only ever go after what grips you, and half of what you need has never gripped you.
Passionate|Knowledge.ask: What must you learn that you find dull?

Passionate|Leadership.recognize: People follow you because standing near you makes ordinary work feel like it matters, and it does matter. What is invisible from the front is that your team has learned to check your mood before they bring you anything.
Passionate|Leadership.ask: Who waited for a good day to tell you something?

Passionate|Mercy.recognize: You cannot look at suffering and stay neutral, so you move, and the person in front of you knows they were not a case to you. The cost is that you can only carry a few this way, and you have never chosen which few on purpose.
Passionate|Mercy.ask: Who are you carrying that God did not give you?

Passionate|Miracles.recognize: You pray with your whole body for things other people have quietly given up on, and sometimes they happen. What you cannot always tell is whether the intensity is faith or leverage, whether you are asking God or wearing him down.
Passionate|Miracles.ask: What have you prayed for and never accepted a no on?

Passionate|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know you are for them at full strength, and that kind of loyalty is not common. The blind spot is that everything gets your whole self, so a small trouble draws the same heat as a crisis, and they have learned not to mention small things.
Passionate|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What has someone in your care stopped telling you about?

Passionate|Prophecy.recognize: You cannot leave a wrong thing standing, and you say so with a force that makes people take it seriously. What you cannot feel from where you stand is how long the heat stays in a room after you have moved on from the point.
Passionate|Prophecy.ask: Who is still recovering from something you said months ago?

Passionate|Service.recognize: You work like the outcome is personal, because it is, and the people beside you get pulled along by it. The cost is that you have no low gear. There is everything or there is nothing, and there has been a lot of nothing lately.
Passionate|Service.ask: How long was your last collapse after a big push?

Passionate|Teaching.recognize: Nobody sleeps in your class. You carry the material like it is urgent, and for you it is. The blind spot is that intensity fills a room the way volume does, and a full room can leave with a feeling and no content.
Passionate|Teaching.ask: What could someone repeat from your last lesson a week later?

Passionate|Tongues.recognize: Your prayer has heat in it and people around you can tell something real is happening. What is hard to check from inside is whether the feeling is the point, and what your prayer life looks like on a flat, cold week.
Passionate|Tongues.ask: How did you pray last time you felt nothing?

Passionate|Wisdom.recognize: You give advice you would stake something on, and people can tell the difference between that and a careful opinion. The cost is that the strength of your conviction never slows down for the question of whether today was the day to say it.
Passionate|Wisdom.ask: What did you say to someone at exactly the wrong moment?

Perceptive|Administration.recognize: You can tell which part of a plan will fail because you noticed who went quiet in the meeting about it. That has saved months of work. What you cannot verify is how often you rearranged something around a mood you assigned to somebody who was simply tired.
Perceptive|Administration.ask: Who did you last assume was unhappy without asking?

Perceptive|Apostleship.recognize: You walk into an unfamiliar community and within a week you know who actually holds it together and who only appears to. The work goes faster for it. The blind spot is that a place can take years to reveal what you concluded about it in a week.
Perceptive|Apostleship.ask: What did you decide about a place before it could show you?

Perceptive|Discernment.recognize: You pick up what a person is carrying before they say a word, and you are right often enough that people find it unnerving. What is impossible to check from inside is which impressions came from the Spirit and which came from your history with someone who resembled them.
Perceptive|Discernment.ask: Who does that person remind you of?

Perceptive|Evangelism.recognize: You know the moment a conversation has opened, and you step through it, which is why people talk to you about God at all. The cost is that you also know exactly which nerve to touch, and knowing where a person is soft is not permission.
Perceptive|Evangelism.ask: What did you use about someone to move them toward a decision?

Perceptive|Exhortation.recognize: You catch the discouragement someone is hiding and you speak to the real thing, not the thing they said, and it lands with a force that surprises them. What you cannot always tell is when you named something out loud that they were not ready to have named.
Perceptive|Exhortation.ask: Who went quiet after you told them what you had noticed?

Perceptive|Faith.recognize: You sense when a door is genuinely open and you move before the evidence is in, and it has worked often enough to trust. The blind spot is that a strong impression and a word from God feel identical from the inside.
Perceptive|Faith.ask: How do you tell your instinct from the Holy Spirit?

Perceptive|Giving.recognize: You notice the need nobody announced, the family who stopped signing up for things, the man whose shoes gave out, and you meet it quietly. The cost is that you also notice who was grateful, and you keep a tally you would deny keeping.
Perceptive|Giving.ask: Who did you help who never thanked you, and how did that sit?

Perceptive|Healing.recognize: You can tell the difference between someone who wants to talk and someone who wants to be left alone, and you get it right most of the time. What you cannot check is that the ones you decided wanted space may have been waiting for you to stay.
Perceptive|Healing.ask: Who did you give room to who wanted you to sit down?

Perceptive|Interpretation.recognize: You catch what a passage is doing underneath the words, and you can name it in a way that makes a room go still. The blind spot is that a mind this quick at finding what is underneath will find something underneath everything, including where nothing is.
Perceptive|Interpretation.ask: Which of your insights has anyone ever checked?

Perceptive|Knowledge.recognize: You learn as much from watching a person as from a book, and what you pick up about people is usually accurate. What is hard to admit is how much of what you know about others was never offered to you, and you have never asked what to do with it.
Perceptive|Knowledge.ask: What do you know about someone that they did not tell you?

Perceptive|Leadership.recognize: You know who on the team is close to done and you move the load before they ask, and they stay because of it. What is invisible from the front is how much of your team's life you are managing from behind, with none of them told.
Perceptive|Leadership.ask: Who have you been quietly shielding without telling them?

Perceptive|Mercy.recognize: You find the person on the edge of the room and you find them fast, because you registered them the moment you walked in. It is a real gift. The cost is that you also decide, quickly, what their pain is about, and that story is the one you answer.
Perceptive|Mercy.ask: Whose situation did you get wrong after being sure of it?

Perceptive|Miracles.recognize: You sense when God is about to move and you are usually not the only one, you are just the first to say it. The blind spot is that a room takes its cue from you, and a room that has been told what to feel will feel it.
Perceptive|Miracles.ask: What did the room feel because you named it first?

Perceptive|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Nobody drifts out of your care unnoticed. You catch the second week that someone stops coming, and they are found because of you. What you cannot feel is how it lands on a person who wanted to be gone for a fortnight and could not be.
Perceptive|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who has told you they need space, and did you give it?

Perceptive|Prophecy.recognize: You put your finger on the thing a group is avoiding, and you do it with unusual accuracy, and it clears the air. What you cannot verify is whether what you named was in the room, or whether you have simply grown confident about what people hide.
Perceptive|Prophecy.ask: When did you name something and get it wrong?

Perceptive|Service.recognize: You spot what will be needed an hour before anyone needs it, and it is already there when they turn around. The cost is that you have learned to serve people without ever having to ask them anything, and asking is now the harder thing.
Perceptive|Service.ask: When did you last ask someone what they wanted instead of guessing?

Perceptive|Teaching.recognize: You can feel a class losing the thread and change course without a break in your voice, so people learn from you who did not learn elsewhere. The blind spot is that you teach the room's mood, and a comfortable room has sometimes been let off.
Perceptive|Teaching.ask: What did you skip last week because the room got uneasy?

Perceptive|Tongues.recognize: You have a fine ear for what is happening among people when they pray, and it makes you a steady presence. What is hard to check is that a person watching a room is not fully in the prayer, and you may not have been alone with God in a while.
Perceptive|Tongues.ask: When did you last pray with nobody there to notice?

Perceptive|Wisdom.recognize: You know when a person is ready to hear something and when they are not, and you wait accordingly, and that judgment is worth a great deal. The cost is that waiting is indistinguishable from avoiding, and only you know which one this is.
Perceptive|Wisdom.ask: What are you waiting to tell someone, and for how long now?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Administration.recognize: You make the dull side of church life feel worth doing, and people sign up for rotas because you asked them cheerfully. The blind spot is that when a system is failing, the good mood you bring is the very thing that stops anyone saying so.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Administration.ask: Who told you something was not working, and when?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Apostleship.recognize: A room that had given up gets its appetite back when you describe what could be there, and that is how hard things get started. What you cannot feel is how the second year lands on the people you recruited with the first year's excitement.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Apostleship.ask: Who joined for the excitement and quietly stopped coming?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Discernment.recognize: You believe the best about people and it is not naivety. You have watched it draw the best out of them. The cost is that a warning in your gut has nowhere to go, because you have made a habit of turning heavy things aside.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Discernment.ask: What have you felt about someone and never said?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Evangelism.recognize: People come with you to things because being around you is a pleasure, and that has put strangers in front of the gospel. What is hard to notice is that a faith presented as good news for the mood has not been presented as a cross.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Evangelism.ask: When did you last tell someone what following Christ would cost?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Exhortation.recognize: You can get a discouraged person moving in one conversation, and they leave believing something they did not believe an hour before. The blind spot is that some of them needed to stay down long enough to learn what the discouragement was telling them.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Exhortation.ask: Who did you cheer up before they had finished grieving?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Faith.recognize: Your confidence that God will come through is contagious and it has held groups together through genuinely bad stretches. What you cannot check from inside is whether you are trusting God or simply unwilling to sit in a situation that looks bad.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Faith.ask: What situation are you refusing to call a disaster?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Giving.recognize: You give gladly and it never feels like a burden to receive from you, which is rarer than it sounds. The cost is that you steer away from the giving that would actually pinch, because a pinch would show on your face.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Giving.ask: What gift have you made that you actually felt?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Healing.recognize: Hurting people seek you out because you do not treat them as fragile, and they get to feel normal with you for an hour. What you may not notice is how quickly you steer a conversation upward, and how few of them ever finished a sentence about the worst part.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Healing.ask: Who tried to tell you something dark, and what did you say?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Interpretation.recognize: You find the hope in a passage and you find it honestly, which is why people leave your study wanting to keep going. The blind spot is the texts you never teach, and if you listed them they would all be the same kind of text.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Interpretation.ask: When did you last teach a passage with no consolation in it?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Knowledge.recognize: You make learning feel like an adventure and people follow you into subjects they had written off. The cost is that a question with a discouraging answer tends not to keep your attention long enough to reach the answer.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Knowledge.ask: What have you looked into and dropped because you did not like it?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Leadership.recognize: Morale around you is high and that is not nothing. People work harder because they enjoy being on your team. What is invisible from the front is that bad news now has to travel around you, and it arrives late every single occasion.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Leadership.ask: What did you find out too late that someone knew for weeks?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Mercy.recognize: You bring warmth into a room where somebody is suffering, and the warmth is real, not performed. What you cannot see is that grief wants someone to stay more than it wants improvement, and you are much better at improvement.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Mercy.ask: Who did you sit with in silence, and when?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Miracles.recognize: You pray as though God is about to move, and it raises the faith of everyone listening. The blind spot is what you do when nothing happens. You move the conversation on so fast that nobody, including you, has ever grieved a prayer God said no to.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Miracles.ask: What unanswered prayer have you never actually mourned?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Pastor/Shepher.recognize: People in your care feel encouraged and glad to be there, and that is a large part of why they stay. What is hidden from you is that a shepherd who is always bright is hard to bring a shameful thing to, and the worst may never reach you.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Pastor/Shepher.ask: When did someone last confess something serious to you?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Prophecy.recognize: You can name a hard thing and keep a room from despairing, which is a genuine pastoral skill. The cost is that you now soften every hard thing by reflex, and some of them needed to land with their full weight.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Prophecy.ask: What did you soften last that should have stung?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Service.recognize: You are the reason a long setup day feels short, and people sign up again because of how it felt to work beside you. What you cannot feel is how heavy your own tiredness gets when the person who keeps everyone else going has nowhere to put it.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Service.ask: When you are flattened, who hears about it?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Teaching.recognize: Your class is a place people want to be, and they keep hold of things because they enjoyed learning them. The blind spot is that the hard doctrine keeps getting scheduled for a week that never arrives.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Teaching.ask: What have you kept putting off teaching?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Tongues.recognize: Your prayer carries gladness, and it frees other people to pray without stiffness. What is hard to look at is lament, and whether you have ever brought God a complaint without ending it on a bright note.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Tongues.ask: When did you last pray angry and leave it there?

Positive and Enthusiastic|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you when they want to feel better about a decision, and they go out lighter than they arrived. The cost is that some of them came for a hard opinion and left with encouragement, and on that day the two were not the same thing.
Positive and Enthusiastic|Wisdom.ask: Who needed you to tell them not to do it?

Principled|Administration.recognize: The processes you build are fair, and people know the rules apply the same way to everybody, including you. That is worth a great deal. The blind spot is that a rule written for a good reason outlives the reason, and you enforce it years later.
Principled|Administration.ask: Which of your rules could you no longer explain the reason for?

Principled|Apostleship.recognize: You will not cut corners to get a work off the ground, so what you begin is built clean and can be passed on without embarrassment. The cost is that fresh ground is messy by nature, and you have refused good openings that arrived untidy.
Principled|Apostleship.ask: What did you turn down because of how it came to you?

Principled|Discernment.recognize: You can tell when something is off in a leader's conduct long before it surfaces, and you are usually right. What is hard to check is whether you are noticing sin or noticing a person doing a thing in a way you would never do it.
Principled|Discernment.ask: Whose behavior bothers you that is not actually wrong?

Principled|Evangelism.recognize: You will not soften what following Christ requires, so nobody who comes to faith through you is surprised later. The blind spot is that a person hears the requirement first and the welcome second, and some never got as far as the welcome.
Principled|Evangelism.ask: Who walked away from you and never heard the grace part?

Principled|Exhortation.recognize: You call people up to something and you do not lower the bar to make it easier, which is why your encouragement carries weight. The cost is that a person who has already failed hears the call as a verdict.
Principled|Exhortation.ask: Who did you challenge who was already ashamed?

Principled|Faith.recognize: Your obedience does not depend on how you feel about it. You do the right thing on the days it costs, and people have built their own faith on watching that. What you cannot feel is how far your faithfulness has drifted from affection.
Principled|Faith.ask: When did you last enjoy God rather than obey him?

Principled|Giving.recognize: You give what you said you would give, on schedule, whether or not it is convenient, and ministries can budget around you. The blind spot is the need in front of you that falls outside what you committed to, and how easily you walk past it.
Principled|Giving.ask: What need did you decline because you had already allocated?

Principled|Healing.recognize: You will not tell a hurting person a comforting lie, and there are people who trust you for exactly that reason. The cost is that honesty arriving early in a wound is not medicine, and you have handed some out early.
Principled|Healing.ask: Who did you tell the plain facts to before they could bear them?

Principled|Interpretation.recognize: You will not bend a text to make it easier, so what you teach can be relied on. What is invisible from inside is how often you reach for the passage that convicts and how rarely for the one that consoles.
Principled|Interpretation.ask: When did a passage last console you?

Principled|Knowledge.recognize: You do the work properly and refuse to speak on what you have not studied, so what you say is reliable. The blind spot is that this becomes a way of measuring everyone else, and you have quietly ranked the people around you.
Principled|Knowledge.ask: Who have you privately written off as unserious?

Principled|Leadership.recognize: Your team knows where the line is and that you will not move it for a favorite, which makes you safe to work for. What you cannot feel is that they now bring you finished work only, because unfinished work gets measured too.
Principled|Leadership.ask: When did someone last bring you a half-formed idea?

Principled|Mercy.recognize: Your kindness comes with honesty attached, so people know your care is not approval of everything they do. The cost is that a person in the worst week of their life needs the care to arrive alone, and yours rarely travels by itself.
Principled|Mercy.ask: Who got a correction from you in a week they were drowning?

Principled|Miracles.recognize: You will not manufacture a sign or inflate a story, so when you say God did something, it can be believed. The blind spot is that you have grown so careful about false claims that you no longer ask for the real thing.
Principled|Miracles.ask: What would you not dare pray for now?

Principled|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know what you require and nobody is confused about what you think of them, and that is a kindness. What is hidden from you is how much of their life they now edit before it reaches you.
Principled|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What is happening among your people that would shock you?

Principled|Prophecy.recognize: You say what is wrong and you say it whether or not it costs you, which is the rarest part of it. The cost is that being right has become a place to live, and living there is a good deal warmer than repentance.
Principled|Prophecy.ask: What have you named in others that is true of you?

Principled|Service.recognize: You do the job to the letter, on the day, whether anyone checks or not, and things are sound because of it. The blind spot is your quiet contempt for the person who did their part sloppily and got thanked for it anyway.
Principled|Service.ask: Whose sloppy work are you still annoyed about?

Principled|Teaching.recognize: You teach what the text says and not what the room wants, and mature believers seek you out for it. What you cannot feel is the young Christian who concluded from an hour with you that they will never get it right.
Principled|Teaching.ask: Who stopped coming to your class, and did you ask why?

Principled|Tongues.recognize: You are careful about what you attribute to the Spirit and you will not fake anything, which spares a room a lot of nonsense. The cost is that your caution is now the loudest thing in the room while people pray.
Principled|Tongues.ask: Who has felt judged praying near you?

Principled|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is the same whether the person asking is a friend or a stranger, and people know they are getting the real answer. The blind spot is that a right answer delivered on the wrong day is still a blow, and you have never treated the day as your business.
Principled|Wisdom.ask: What was right, and said far too soon?

Proactive Initiative|Administration.recognize: The gap gets filled before anyone has noticed there was one. You know what will be needed next month and it is handled well before it arrives. What you cannot tell from inside is how often the thing you handled was somebody else's job to do.
Proactive Initiative|Administration.ask: Whose task did you finish for them this month?

Proactive Initiative|Apostleship.recognize: You do not wait for the church to send you. You go and begin the thing and let the paperwork catch up, and work exists because of that. The blind spot is that a work begun without anyone sending you has nobody it answers to either.
Proactive Initiative|Apostleship.ask: Who could shut down what you started?

Proactive Initiative|Discernment.recognize: You act on a bad feeling early, and because you act early the damage is usually small. What is hard to check is that you never find out what would have happened, so you have no way of knowing how many of your instincts were wrong.
Proactive Initiative|Discernment.ask: What did you shut down that might have been fine?

Proactive Initiative|Evangelism.recognize: You begin the conversation nobody else begins, and strangers hear about Christ because you did not wait for a natural opening. The cost is that an opening you made yourself is one the other person never agreed to.
Proactive Initiative|Evangelism.ask: Who did you approach who had no way to decline?

Proactive Initiative|Exhortation.recognize: You go to a struggling person before they ask, and being sought out is half of what heals them. What you cannot feel is that arriving uninvited also tells someone you had already concluded they were failing.
Proactive Initiative|Exhortation.ask: Who did you check on who had not asked for help?

Proactive Initiative|Faith.recognize: You act on what you believe God wants without waiting for confirmation, and God has honored a good deal of it. The blind spot is that you have never learned the difference between faith and impatience, because both look exactly like this.
Proactive Initiative|Faith.ask: When did you last wait on God for longer than a week?

Proactive Initiative|Giving.recognize: You cover the need before it is announced, quietly, often before the person knew that you knew. The cost is that a gift arriving unasked leaves nobody able to refuse it, and some of them would have.
Proactive Initiative|Giving.ask: Who did you pay for who did not want you to?

Proactive Initiative|Healing.recognize: You show up at the hospital, the house, the funeral, without being called, and your presence has held people together. What is invisible from where you are is that some people need to invite you in first, or the help is something being done to them.
Proactive Initiative|Healing.ask: Who has never once asked you to come?
