Proactive Initiative|Interpretation.recognize: You bring a passage to bear on a situation while it is still live, and people get scripture when it can still change something. The blind spot is that a text applied quickly is a text you settled the sense of on the way over.
Proactive Initiative|Interpretation.ask: Which passage did you use before you had studied it?

Proactive Initiative|Knowledge.recognize: You go and find out rather than waiting to be told, so you usually know first. What is hard to admit is that knowing first has become its own reward, and you have brought people information they had not asked to have.
Proactive Initiative|Knowledge.ask: What did you look into that was not yours to look into?

Proactive Initiative|Leadership.recognize: Nothing stalls under you, because the second something stops you are already carrying it forward yourself. The cost is that your team has learned hesitation is expensive, so they no longer bring you anything they are unsure about.
Proactive Initiative|Leadership.ask: Who on your team is waiting to be allowed to try?

Proactive Initiative|Mercy.recognize: You are at the door with food the same day the news lands, and nobody in your church grieves alone. What you cannot see is that the grieving person now has a visitor to manage on the worst day of their life.
Proactive Initiative|Mercy.ask: Who did you go to on day one who needed you on day thirty?

Proactive Initiative|Miracles.recognize: You pray for it and then act as though it is already settled, and that boldness has been the doorway to real things. The blind spot is that acting on an answer you have not been given is a way of forcing God's hand and calling it faith.
Proactive Initiative|Miracles.ask: What did you commit to before God had answered?

Proactive Initiative|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You catch trouble in your people early because you go looking rather than waiting for them to come to you. The cost is that a person cannot bring you something themselves if you always got there first, and that bringing is part of how they grow.
Proactive Initiative|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who in your care has never had to come to you?

Proactive Initiative|Prophecy.recognize: You raise the hard thing while it is still small, which is why it rarely gets large around you. What you cannot verify is how many would have sorted themselves out, or what it costs a person to be corrected for something they had already noticed.
Proactive Initiative|Prophecy.ask: What did you name that they were already dealing with?

Proactive Initiative|Service.recognize: The chairs are out, the coffee is on, the mess is gone, and nobody saw it happen because you were there first. The blind spot is that the volunteer who came to help now has nothing to do, and stops coming.
Proactive Initiative|Service.ask: Who showed up to serve and found it all done?

Proactive Initiative|Teaching.recognize: You answer the question before the class has finished forming it, and they leave with what they needed. What is hidden from you is that a question a person never got to ask is one they will not remember the answer to.
Proactive Initiative|Teaching.ask: Who in your class has never finished asking something?

Proactive Initiative|Tongues.recognize: You are the one who begins praying when a room has gone quiet, and that has unlocked a lot of meetings. The cost is that a silence you fill quickly is a silence God was possibly using.
Proactive Initiative|Tongues.ask: How long can you let a room stay quiet?

Proactive Initiative|Wisdom.recognize: You give people the answer while it can still help them, and they have been spared real trouble by it. The blind spot is that a person handed the conclusion early skipped the part where they wrestled, and they will be back for the next one.
Proactive Initiative|Wisdom.ask: Who returns to you with the same kind of question?

Quick Thinkers|Administration.recognize: A problem lands and you have three workable answers before the meeting ends, which is why nothing sits. What you cannot feel is how that lands on the person who needed a night to think, and who learned there is no point offering it the next day.
Quick Thinkers|Administration.ask: Who brings you ideas a day late?

Quick Thinkers|Apostleship.recognize: You can improvise a whole work out of whatever is in the room, and things exist because you did not wait for the proper setup. The blind spot is that what you can throw together in a week is also what nobody else can maintain.
Quick Thinkers|Apostleship.ask: What have you built that only you understand?

Quick Thinkers|Discernment.recognize: You read a person in the first minute and you are right more often than chance allows. What is impossible to check from inside is that a judgment formed in a minute is one you will spend a year finding evidence for.
Quick Thinkers|Discernment.ask: Who have you never revised your first impression of?

Quick Thinkers|Evangelism.recognize: You have an answer for every objection and you have it immediately, so nobody derails you. The cost is that an objection answered in two seconds was not heard, and the person raising it knows that better than you do.
Quick Thinkers|Evangelism.ask: Who raised a real doubt and got a rehearsed answer?

Quick Thinkers|Exhortation.recognize: Someone tells you they are stuck and you have already found the way through for them, and often it works. What you cannot see is that a person handed the answer that quickly hears that their problem was not very hard.
Quick Thinkers|Exhortation.ask: Who felt small after you fixed their problem?

Quick Thinkers|Faith.recognize: You can commit to something in the length of a conversation, and God has used that willingness more than once. The blind spot is that a decision made that fast cannot be told apart from an impulse, even by you, especially afterwards.
Quick Thinkers|Faith.ask: What have you committed to and regretted within a month?

Quick Thinkers|Giving.recognize: You say yes to a need on the spot, before you have talked yourself out of it, and a great deal of good has come of that. The cost is that the slow, dull, ongoing giving has never held your attention the way a sudden one does.
Quick Thinkers|Giving.ask: What are you still giving to that you began three years ago?

Quick Thinkers|Healing.recognize: You find the thing to say when everyone else is silent, and it usually helps. What is invisible from where you stand is that the silence you filled was doing work, and some wounds only open in a pause nobody hurried.
Quick Thinkers|Healing.ask: How long is the longest silence you have let stand?

Quick Thinkers|Interpretation.recognize: You can take a hard passage apart on your feet, in front of people, without notes. The blind spot is that what you produce on your feet is what you already thought, and scripture has not surprised you in a long while.
Quick Thinkers|Interpretation.ask: When did a text last tell you something you did not expect?

Quick Thinkers|Knowledge.recognize: You pick things up alarmingly fast and can hold a conversation on a subject you met yesterday. What is hard to admit is that you have almost nothing you have studied for years, because the early part is the part you enjoy.
Quick Thinkers|Knowledge.ask: What subject have you stayed with past the interesting stage?

Quick Thinkers|Leadership.recognize: Decisions do not queue up under you. Something arrives, you settle it, the room proceeds. The cost is that your team has stopped bringing you the complicated things, because complicated things get simple answers here.
Quick Thinkers|Leadership.ask: What decision did you make that you should have slept on?

Quick Thinkers|Mercy.recognize: You know what to do for a hurting person before anyone else has worked out what is wrong, and you do it. The blind spot is that loss has no shortcut in it, and a person who can only go slowly cannot stay alongside you.
Quick Thinkers|Mercy.ask: Who fell behind you in their grief?

Quick Thinkers|Miracles.recognize: You believe God can act now, today, in this conversation, and you pray that way without working up to it. The cost is that you also want it now, and a God who takes eleven years is one you have almost no practice with.
Quick Thinkers|Miracles.ask: What have you been waiting on God for since before last year?

Quick Thinkers|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: A person in trouble gets an answer from you the same hour, and that is why they come. What you cannot feel is that they now bring you problems already shaped into the kind you settle quickly, and the slow ones stay home.
Quick Thinkers|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What is the longest anyone has taken to tell you something?

Quick Thinkers|Prophecy.recognize: You name the wrong thing in the moment, in the room, while it is happening, and that takes real nerve. The blind spot is that the sentence which arrives instantly is rarely the sentence you would have chosen an hour later.
Quick Thinkers|Prophecy.ask: What did you say in the room that you would edit now?

Quick Thinkers|Service.recognize: You sort the practical crisis while others are still describing it, and events run because you were there. What is hidden from you is how many people watched you do it and concluded they had nothing to offer.
Quick Thinkers|Service.ask: Who watched you work and decided they were not needed?

Quick Thinkers|Teaching.recognize: Nobody can lose you with a question, and your class trusts that completely. The cost is that a question you can settle in five seconds is one you have stopped finding interesting, and the ones worth an hour never get one.
Quick Thinkers|Teaching.ask: Which question deserved a whole evening and got two minutes?

Quick Thinkers|Tongues.recognize: You are never lost for words in prayer and you can pray aloud for others with no preparation at all. What is hard to look at is whether you have any prayer life that is not verbal, and what happens when you have nothing to say.
Quick Thinkers|Tongues.ask: When did you last pray without words?

Quick Thinkers|Wisdom.recognize: Your judgment arrives fully formed and it is usually sound, which is why people ask you rather than think it through themselves. The blind spot is that wisdom and quickness are not the same faculty, and you have only ever tested one of them.
Quick Thinkers|Wisdom.ask: What advice have you given that you never went back and checked?

Rational|Administration.recognize: You will not run a system on tradition or sentiment. If it cannot be justified it goes, and what remains actually works. What you cannot tell from inside is how much of what you cut was carrying something for somebody that no argument would have shown you.
Rational|Administration.ask: What did you cut that somebody quietly grieved?

Rational|Apostleship.recognize: You test a new work against evidence before you commit, and the ventures you back tend to survive. The blind spot is that a call to a hard place has almost never made a good case for itself on paper.
Rational|Apostleship.ask: What has God asked of you that made no sense?

Rational|Discernment.recognize: You will not act on an impression you cannot defend, which has kept you from accusing innocent people. The cost is that when the Spirit hands you something with no evidence attached, you have already trained yourself to set it aside.
Rational|Discernment.ask: What did you feel, dismiss, and turn out to be right about?

Rational|Evangelism.recognize: You can make the case for Christianity to a skeptic without flinching, and thinking people take you seriously because of it. What is hard to face is that nobody has ever been argued into the kingdom, and you keep having the argument.
Rational|Evangelism.ask: Who won the debate with you and stayed lost?

Rational|Exhortation.recognize: You encourage people with evidence rather than sentiment, so when you tell someone they can do it, it carries weight. The blind spot is that a person in despair is not making an error you can correct.
Rational|Exhortation.ask: Who needed you to sit down, not to explain?

Rational|Faith.recognize: Your faith has been examined and it holds up, and doubters find you safe because their questions do not frighten you. The cost is that a faith you can fully account for is one you have quietly capped at the size of your own mind.
Rational|Faith.ask: What do you believe about God that you cannot defend?

Rational|Giving.recognize: You give where the evidence says it will do the most good, and very little of your money is wasted. What you cannot weigh is the beggar who fails every test you apply and is still in front of you.
Rational|Giving.ask: Who did you turn down because the case was weak?

Rational|Healing.recognize: You help a hurting person by finding what is actually wrong, and you have cut through a great deal of confusion. The blind spot is that being understood is not the same as being loved, and you are much better at the first.
Rational|Healing.ask: Who did you diagnose when they wanted to be held?

Rational|Interpretation.recognize: You will not accept a reading that does not hold together, so what you teach is coherent and nobody is misled. What is invisible from inside is that scripture contains things which do not resolve, and you have kept explaining them until they did.
Rational|Interpretation.ask: Which contradiction in the Bible have you never let stand?

Rational|Knowledge.recognize: You know why you believe what you know and you can show the working, which makes you genuinely trustworthy. The cost is that whatever you cannot show working for has quietly stopped counting as knowledge at all.
Rational|Knowledge.ask: What do you know that you could not prove?

Rational|Leadership.recognize: Your decisions can be explained, and your team never suspects favoritism, because the argument is always on the table. What you cannot feel is how it lands when someone brings you a hope, or a fear, and gets an analysis back.
Rational|Leadership.ask: Who brought you a feeling and got a case?

Rational|Mercy.recognize: You do not fall apart when someone else does, and that steadiness has been a real refuge for people in chaos. The blind spot is that you have decided the tears are the problem, when they are usually the treatment.
Rational|Mercy.ask: Who wept in front of you, and what did you do?

Rational|Miracles.recognize: You examine the claim before you repeat it, which has spared your church a lot of embarrassment. What is hard to admit is that you now find it easier to explain a thing away than to be wrong in front of people.
Rational|Miracles.ask: What have you explained away that God may have done?

Rational|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: People in your care get straight answers and never false hope, and there is a kind of safety in that. The cost is that a person who is not thinking clearly does not need to be shown that they are not thinking clearly.
Rational|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needed you to just agree with them for an hour?

Rational|Prophecy.recognize: You will not call something wrong until you can prove it, so when you do speak, it holds. The blind spot is that some evils cannot be proved to the person doing them, and waiting for proof has let a few of them run.
Rational|Prophecy.ask: What are you waiting for proof of, while it continues?

Rational|Service.recognize: You will not do a job the wasteful way just because it has always been done that way, and things work better for it. What is hidden from you is that some of the waste was how people got to be together while they worked.
Rational|Service.ask: What did you make efficient that people used to enjoy?

Rational|Teaching.recognize: Your teaching can be followed and checked, and nobody leaves your class believing something on a bad footing. The cost is that a room can understand you completely and be moved by nothing.
Rational|Teaching.ask: When did your teaching last cost someone something?

Rational|Tongues.recognize: You are honest about what you do not understand and you will not fake a spiritual experience, which is more integrity than most rooms hold. The blind spot is that you have made a virtue of avoiding the one part of this life you cannot govern.
Rational|Tongues.ask: What would it cost you to pray something you could not account for?

Rational|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you decisions because you will take the feeling out and show them what is actually so, and your advice ages well. What you cannot see is how often the thing they were feeling was the most accurate information in the room.
Rational|Wisdom.ask: Whose gut did you talk them out of?

Rational and Practical|Administration.recognize: You build what works and nothing more, so your systems are lean and people can actually follow them. What you cannot tell from inside is that a church is not only a machine for getting things done, and some of what you trimmed was where people belonged.
Rational and Practical|Administration.ask: What did you trim that people used to enjoy?

Rational and Practical|Apostleship.recognize: You begin a work by asking what it would genuinely take and then getting that, which is why yours do not collapse in year two. The blind spot is that a calling assessed for feasibility is one you may have quietly declined.
Rational and Practical|Apostleship.ask: What did you judge unworkable that God had asked for?

Rational and Practical|Discernment.recognize: You spot the broken thing in a situation and you can usually say what would repair it. The cost is that not everything wrong in a room is a fault. Some of it is sin, and sin is not repaired, it is repented of.
Rational and Practical|Discernment.ask: What did you try to fix that needed confession?

Rational and Practical|Evangelism.recognize: You show people what following Christ would actually look like on a Tuesday, and that concreteness reaches people no sermon reached. What is hard to face is that a gospel offered as something that works has not been offered as something that is true.
Rational and Practical|Evangelism.ask: Who came to Christ because it would help them?

Rational and Practical|Exhortation.recognize: You give a discouraged person something they can do today, and doing it usually helps. The blind spot is that some discouragement has no fix in it, and being handed one tells the person they have now failed twice.
Rational and Practical|Exhortation.ask: Who took your advice, and it did not work?

Rational and Practical|Faith.recognize: Your faith shows up as things done rather than things felt, and people can see it working across your week. The cost is that a faith measured by what it produces has no way to survive a season that produces nothing.
Rational and Practical|Faith.ask: What is your faith worth in a year where nothing works?

Rational and Practical|Giving.recognize: You fund what will actually change something, and you can tell the difference between a need and a habit. What you cannot weigh is the gift that accomplishes nothing except that a person felt loved.
Rational and Practical|Giving.ask: What have you given purely because someone would be glad?

Rational and Practical|Healing.recognize: You get a hurting person's practical life back under them, the rent, the childcare, the appointment, and for some people that has been the beginning of real recovery. The blind spot is that you treat the parts of them you can mend and leave the rest alone.
Rational and Practical|Healing.ask: What in that person cannot be mended, and have you named it?

Rational and Practical|Interpretation.recognize: You always land on what the passage requires on Monday, and nobody leaves your study wondering what to do with it. The cost is that scripture is not primarily instructions, and the parts that are only worship keep getting skipped.
Rational and Practical|Interpretation.ask: When did you last teach a text with nothing to apply?

Rational and Practical|Knowledge.recognize: You learn what you will actually put to work and you learn it properly, so nothing you know is decorative. What is hard to admit is that some things are worth knowing because they are true, and you have never had patience for those.
Rational and Practical|Knowledge.ask: What have you learned that will never be applied?

Rational and Practical|Leadership.recognize: You keep the team pointed at what matters and you cut what does not, which is why nobody under you feels their work is pointless. The blind spot is that people are not only their output, and yours have noticed which parts of them you engage.
Rational and Practical|Leadership.ask: What do you know about your team that is not about their work?

Rational and Practical|Mercy.recognize: You turn up with the thing that is needed, the ride, the meal, the money, and it is real help arriving at the right hour. The cost is that once you have handed it over you leave, because the part that cannot be mended is not a part you know what to do with.
Rational and Practical|Mercy.ask: How long did you stay after you dropped it off?

Rational and Practical|Miracles.recognize: You pray for what is needed rather than for spectacle, and there is nothing showy anywhere in your faith. The blind spot is that you have narrowed your asking down to things which could plausibly have happened anyway.
Rational and Practical|Miracles.ask: What is the largest thing you have prayed for this year?

Rational and Practical|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people's lives get better in concrete ways because you attend to the practical, and that is real care. What is hidden from you is that you have not asked one of them what they are afraid of, because there would be nothing to do with the answer.
Rational and Practical|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What is the person closest to you in ministry afraid of?

Rational and Practical|Prophecy.recognize: When you name something wrong you also say what should happen instead, so it never lands as mere complaint. The cost is that some things need to be named and then sat with, and you have never let one sit.
Rational and Practical|Prophecy.ask: What sin did you turn into an action item?

Rational and Practical|Service.recognize: You do the job the way that works, in the fewest movements, and everything you touch runs better afterwards. The blind spot is that people were not always in the way. Sometimes they were the point of the job.
Rational and Practical|Service.ask: Who did you work around to get it done faster?

Rational and Practical|Teaching.recognize: Everything you teach can be put to work, and your class leaves with something in hand. What you cannot see is that a Christian formed only on the applicable has no idea what to do with God when nothing is being required of them.
Rational and Practical|Teaching.ask: What have you taught that had no takeaway?

Rational and Practical|Tongues.recognize: You are honest that you would rather be doing something than sitting in a prayer meeting, and you do a great deal. What is hard to face is that prayer produces nothing you can point at, and you have never been able to value what produces nothing.
Rational and Practical|Tongues.ask: How long have you gone without praying alone?

Rational and Practical|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice can be acted on, which is why people come to you rather than to someone more profound. The blind spot is that some situations have no action in them at all, and you will invent one rather than tell a person to wait.
Rational and Practical|Wisdom.ask: Who did you give something to do when they should have waited?

Receptive|Administration.recognize: Your door is open and anyone can bring you a change to how things run, so nothing calcifies under you. What you cannot tell from inside is that whoever asks last usually wins, and your team worked that out a while ago.
Receptive|Administration.ask: Who gets their way with you by asking twice?

Receptive|Apostleship.recognize: You take what a new place offers rather than importing what worked before, so you fit in where others would not. The cost is that a work with no fixed shape takes the shape of whoever is loudest in it.
Receptive|Apostleship.ask: What in your work came from you and not from them?

Receptive|Discernment.recognize: You take people at their word and hear them out fully, which is why they tell you things. The blind spot is that openness and agreement look identical from outside, and you have been quoted as endorsing things you were only listening to.
Receptive|Discernment.ask: Who thinks you agreed with them?

Receptive|Evangelism.recognize: You let people say what they actually believe without correcting them, and that is why they keep talking to you about God. What is hard to see is where listening ends, and whether anyone you have listened to has ever heard you disagree.
Receptive|Evangelism.ask: When did you last say a plain no to somebody's beliefs?

Receptive|Exhortation.recognize: You take on board what people tell you about yourself, which makes your encouragement land, because it is not coming from someone pretending to have arrived. The cost is that you have absorbed criticism that was simply wrong.
Receptive|Exhortation.ask: What have you changed about yourself on bad advice?

Receptive|Faith.recognize: You are genuinely open to God doing it differently than you expected, and that has kept you from getting stuck. The blind spot is that a faith which gives ground easily gives it to everything, including to the last person who called it foolish.
Receptive|Faith.ask: What have you stopped believing because someone pushed?

Receptive|Giving.recognize: You can be given to as well as give, which is rarer than it looks and lets other people minister to you. What you cannot see is that you also say yes to funding things you do not believe in, because refusing in the room is hard.
Receptive|Giving.ask: What are you paying for that you never wanted to?

Receptive|Healing.recognize: Hurting people talk to you because you take whatever they bring without recoiling, and nothing they say is too much. The cost is that you take it in and hold it, and nobody has ever asked what happens to it after they leave.
Receptive|Healing.ask: Who carries what you have been told?

Receptive|Interpretation.recognize: You hold your reading loosely and will change it when shown something better, which is why your teaching improves. The blind spot is that a position which yields to any pressure has never actually been held.
Receptive|Interpretation.ask: What reading have you defended against someone senior?

Receptive|Knowledge.recognize: You learn from anyone, including people others write off, so you know things your peers do not. What is hard to admit is that you take on ideas with the same ease you take on people, and some of them should have been resisted.
Receptive|Knowledge.ask: Whose thinking did you absorb without examining it?

Receptive|Leadership.recognize: Your team can tell you anything and you will consider it seriously, so good ideas get to you that get to nobody else. The cost is that a leader persuadable by everyone ends up carrying a course that is nobody's, including yours.
Receptive|Leadership.ask: What are you leading toward that you did not choose?

Receptive|Mercy.recognize: You let people be as they are without needing them to improve, and the exhausted find rest with you. The blind spot is that the same gentleness which will not push has also never told anyone the truth about what they are doing.
Receptive|Mercy.ask: Who needed a no from you and got understanding instead?

Receptive|Miracles.recognize: You are open to God doing whatever he wants, with no theology fencing it off, and things happen around people like you. The cost is that you are equally open to whatever anyone else says God is doing, and you have never tested one of those claims.
Receptive|Miracles.ask: What have you accepted as God's work without checking?

Receptive|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people can bring you anything at all, and they do, because nothing they confess makes you flinch. What is hidden from you is that a shepherd who never resists cannot fence anything off, and some of them badly needed a fence.
Receptive|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who did you let carry on doing something harmful?

Receptive|Prophecy.recognize: You take correction well and will own a fault publicly, which gives you real credibility when you name something in somebody else. The blind spot is that naming it has got harder every year, because being easy to be around became the thing you protect.
Receptive|Prophecy.ask: What have you known was wrong and not said this year?

Receptive|Service.recognize: You take whatever job you are given without negotiating, and teams rely on you for exactly that. The cost is that nobody knows what you are good at, because you have never once said what you would rather be doing.
Receptive|Service.ask: What would you actually like to do here?

Receptive|Teaching.recognize: Your class can push back and you will take it seriously, so people learn to think rather than to copy. What you cannot feel is that a room which always gets its way has stopped being taught.
Receptive|Teaching.ask: When did you last hold a position your class disliked?

Receptive|Tongues.recognize: You come to God with your hands open rather than with a list, and there is something unforced about your prayer that others notice. The blind spot is that openness can be a way of never asking for anything, and God has not heard you want something in a while.
Receptive|Tongues.ask: What do you actually want from God?

Receptive|Wisdom.recognize: You take advice as readily as you give it, and that humility is why what you say can be trusted. The cost is that you have several people advising you who contradict each other, and you have agreed with all of them.
Receptive|Wisdom.ask: Which of your advisers are you actually following?

Reliable|Administration.recognize: What you say will be done is done, on the date, without a reminder, and whole systems are built on that assumption. What you cannot tell from inside is how much has been quietly assigned to you because you are the only one nobody has to chase.
Reliable|Administration.ask: How many things would fail next month if you stopped?

Reliable|Apostleship.recognize: A work you commit to gets your commitment for years rather than months, which is why the hard places suit you. The blind spot is that you will stay long past the point the work needed you, because leaving would look like breaking your word.
Reliable|Apostleship.ask: What are you still doing that should have ended?

Reliable|Discernment.recognize: People trust your read on a situation because you have never once overstated one. The cost is that you have also learned to say only what you can back up, and the uneasy feeling you cannot evidence never gets voiced.
Reliable|Discernment.ask: What are you uneasy about that you have not mentioned?

Reliable|Evangelism.recognize: The person you are walking toward faith knows you will be there next week and the week after, and that steadiness has reached people no argument reached. What is hard to see is how many you are walking with at once, and which of them get the version of you that is running late.

Reliable|Exhortation.recognize: You are the one who follows up months later, when everyone else has forgotten, and people are still going because of it. The blind spot is that you now carry a list of people whose progress feels like your responsibility.
Reliable|Exhortation.ask: Whose growth are you holding that is not yours to hold?

Reliable|Faith.recognize: You show up to the thing you promised God you would do, on the mornings it means nothing to you, and that has built something real. The cost is that faithfulness has become a load-bearing wall in your identity, and you cannot afford to drop anything.
Reliable|Faith.ask: What would it mean about you to let one thing go?

Reliable|Giving.recognize: Your giving arrives every month without fail, and ministries budget on your word rather than your intention. The blind spot is that you have not revisited the figure in years, and it may now be either too easy or too much.
Reliable|Giving.ask: What figure did you set, and in which year?

Reliable|Healing.recognize: You are still visiting the person everyone else stopped visiting, because you said that you would, and it has made the difference for them. What is invisible from where you stand is that you are running on the promise now, and they can tell.
Reliable|Healing.ask: Who are you visiting out of obligation?

Reliable|Interpretation.recognize: You prepare properly every single week, so nobody in your group has ever had a wasted evening. The cost is that preparation became non-negotiable, and you have taught while ill, grieving, and empty rather than ask anyone to cover.
Reliable|Interpretation.ask: When did you last let somebody else take your week?

Reliable|Knowledge.recognize: If you say you will find out, you find out, and people bring you questions on that basis. The blind spot is how many open questions you are carrying for other people right now, and that none of them know about the others.
Reliable|Knowledge.ask: How many things have you promised to look into?

Reliable|Leadership.recognize: Your team knows exactly what they will get from you, and that predictability is why they can plan their own lives. What you cannot feel is that being the fixed point means you absorb every shock, and nobody has asked how that is going.
Reliable|Leadership.ask: Who takes the weight when you are the one struggling?

Reliable|Mercy.recognize: You are still checking on the person a year after the funeral, when the casseroles have long stopped. The cost is that you have never told anyone how many people are on that list, and it has only ever grown.
Reliable|Mercy.ask: Who is on your list that you dread contacting?

Reliable|Miracles.recognize: You pray for the same person every day for years without needing to see anything, which is a rarer faith than the dramatic kind. The blind spot is that you have never let yourself stop, even where God has clearly said no.
Reliable|Miracles.ask: What have you prayed so long that you no longer mean it?

Reliable|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know you will pick up, and that certainty is most of what your care actually consists of. What is hidden from you is that you have made yourself the thing they lean on, and you cannot fall ill without it costing them.
Reliable|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What happens to your people the week you are ill?

Reliable|Prophecy.recognize: When you say something is wrong, people believe it, because you have never been the one who cries wolf. The cost is that you set the bar for speaking so high that you have watched several things go by.
Reliable|Prophecy.ask: What did you let pass because you were not certain enough?

Reliable|Service.recognize: You are on every rota and you have never missed one, and the whole operation quietly assumes you. The blind spot is that the load has grown by a little every year and you have not once said it was too much.
Reliable|Service.ask: When did you last say no to a rota?

Reliable|Teaching.recognize: You have taught the same class every week for years and never cancelled, and that constancy has formed people more than the content did. The cost is that you are running low and there is no plan for a term without you.
Reliable|Teaching.ask: Who could teach your class if you could not?

Reliable|Tongues.recognize: You pray at the same hour whether or not anything is happening, and that has held you through seasons which would have ended other people. The blind spot is that a discipline this solid can also be somewhere to hide from a God who might ask for something new.
Reliable|Tongues.ask: When did God last change what your prayer life looks like?

Reliable|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you knowing you will still be there next year with the same answer, and consistency is most of why your advice is trusted. The cost is that you have given the same answer for years, and the world it was built for has changed.
Reliable|Wisdom.ask: What advice have you given for a decade without revisiting?

Research-Oriented|Administration.recognize: You will not change a system on somebody's say-so. You go and find out how it actually works first, and your changes hold because of it. What you cannot tell from inside is how many small decisions are sitting in a queue behind your checking.
Research-Oriented|Administration.ask: What is waiting on you right now?

Research-Oriented|Apostleship.recognize: You study a place properly before you go, its history, its people, what has already failed there, and you arrive knowing things. The blind spot is that study can go on indefinitely, and a work still being researched is a work that has not begun.
Research-Oriented|Apostleship.ask: How long have you been preparing to start something?

Research-Oriented|Discernment.recognize: You will not repeat an accusation you have not looked into, and several reputations are intact because of that. The cost is that some situations only ever offer a warning in the gut, and you have let those go by while you looked for something firmer.
Research-Oriented|Discernment.ask: What did you set aside because you could not substantiate it?

Research-Oriented|Evangelism.recognize: You have actually read what other people believe, so nobody talks to you and feels caricatured. What is hard to see is that you can prepare for a conversation indefinitely, and the people who know you best have never heard you say it plainly.
Research-Oriented|Evangelism.ask: Which friend have you been getting ready to talk to for years?

Research-Oriented|Exhortation.recognize: You do not encourage anyone on a hunch. You know what they are actually capable of because you went and looked, which makes your confidence in them worth having. The blind spot is that a person in a bad week needs it before you have finished looking.
Research-Oriented|Exhortation.ask: Who needed a word from you last month and got one this month?

Research-Oriented|Faith.recognize: You have gone into the hard questions rather than avoiding them, and your faith is not fragile. The cost is that you have made a habit of needing one more answer, and there is always one more answer available.
Research-Oriented|Faith.ask: What are you still investigating instead of obeying?

Research-Oriented|Giving.recognize: You look into a charity before you fund it, and your money goes where it will not be wasted. The blind spot is that the person in front of you is not an organisation, and you have made a few of them wait while you checked up on them.
Research-Oriented|Giving.ask: Who did you make prove their need?

Research-Oriented|Healing.recognize: You find out what is actually going on with someone rather than assuming, and people feel taken seriously by you. The cost is that a person bleeding in front of you does not need to be understood accurately first.
Research-Oriented|Healing.ask: Who did you question when they wanted your arms?

Research-Oriented|Interpretation.recognize: You go to the commentaries, the context, the original language, and what you teach is sound. The blind spot is that a passage can be studied until it is safe, and the ones that would have cut you have all been thoroughly accounted for.
Research-Oriented|Interpretation.ask: Which text have you studied so long that it no longer frightens you?

Research-Oriented|Knowledge.recognize: You know the difference between something you read and something you checked, which almost nobody does any more. The cost is that you have made certainty the price of speaking, and rooms have gone without what you know.
Research-Oriented|Knowledge.ask: What did you not say because you were only ninety percent sure?

Research-Oriented|Leadership.recognize: Your team knows decisions here are made on real information rather than instinct, and that trust was earned. The blind spot is that a leader who always needs a little more information is training a team to expect nothing to happen this month.
Research-Oriented|Leadership.ask: What has your team stopped waiting for?

Research-Oriented|Mercy.recognize: You find out what a suffering person actually needs instead of guessing, and what you bring is the right thing. What you cannot feel is that the interval between the news and your arrival is where they were alone.
Research-Oriented|Mercy.ask: How long did it take you to get there?

Research-Oriented|Miracles.recognize: You test a claim before you celebrate it, and your church has been spared some ugly disappointments. The blind spot is that a habit of examining has quietly become a habit of not asking, and you cannot recall the last thing you begged God for.
Research-Oriented|Miracles.ask: What have you asked God for without hedging?

Research-Oriented|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know your people's actual circumstances, not the version they present, because you took an interest and paid attention over years. The cost is that knowing a person thoroughly can substitute for being close to them.
Research-Oriented|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Which of your people could describe your inner life?

Research-Oriented|Prophecy.recognize: When you say something is wrong you have the receipts, and nobody can dismiss you as reactive. The blind spot is that gathering receipts takes months, and the harm carries on for exactly as long as you gather.
Research-Oriented|Prophecy.ask: How long have you been building a case?

Research-Oriented|Service.recognize: You find out how a job should properly be done before you do it, so what you build lasts. The cost is that the job was often small and urgent, and the reading took longer than doing it badly twice would have.
Research-Oriented|Service.ask: What did you research that you should have just attempted?

Research-Oriented|Teaching.recognize: You never teach beyond what you actually know, and your class is not being fed anybody's guesses. The blind spot is that a room does not only need accuracy, and you have kept back a half-formed thought that would have opened something.
Research-Oriented|Teaching.ask: What have you not taught because you had not finished studying it?

Research-Oriented|Tongues.recognize: You want to understand what is happening before you join in, and that has kept you from a great deal of pretending. The cost is that this is the one part of the Christian life designed to happen before you understand it.
Research-Oriented|Tongues.ask: What would you have to give up to pray without understanding?

Research-Oriented|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is grounded in what you actually looked into rather than what you assume, and it holds up years later. The blind spot is that a person deciding this week cannot use an answer you are still working on.
Research-Oriented|Wisdom.ask: Who chose without you while you were checking?

Results Oriented|Administration.recognize: You judge a system by what it delivers, not by how tidy it looks, and you will scrap a beautiful process that produces nothing. What you cannot tell from inside is that some of what you scrapped was doing something that shows up in no report.
Results Oriented|Administration.ask: What did you cut that had no measurable output?

Results Oriented|Apostleship.recognize: You get a work actually standing rather than talked about, and there are churches in existence because you refused to let a thing stay a proposal. The blind spot is that speed of establishment and depth of root are not the same thing.
Results Oriented|Apostleship.ask: What did you get running that had no roots?

Results Oriented|Discernment.recognize: You can tell early which venture will come to nothing, and you have saved people from pouring years into one. The cost is that you read people the same way, and you have quietly written off a few who were only slow.
Results Oriented|Discernment.ask: Who did you give up on too early?

Results Oriented|Evangelism.recognize: You are not satisfied with a good conversation, you want the person actually to come to Christ, and that seriousness has borne fruit. What is hard to see is that a person can feel it when they are the thing you are trying to achieve.
Results Oriented|Evangelism.ask: Who felt like a target rather than a friend?

Results Oriented|Exhortation.recognize: You do not encourage people vaguely, you get them to the thing they said they would do, and they arrive. The blind spot is that some people needed to be loved through a season where they achieved nothing at all.
Results Oriented|Exhortation.ask: Who have you stayed close to through a fruitless year?

Results Oriented|Faith.recognize: You will pay for what you believe God wants, and you have paid, in money and in years, and nobody who knows you thinks your faith is talk. The cost is that you have spent things which were not yours to spend, and called each one obedience.
Results Oriented|Faith.ask: What did your faith cost somebody other than you?

Results Oriented|Giving.recognize: You give where you can watch it work, and you follow up to find out whether it did. The blind spot is that you have made your giving conditional on a return you can observe, and God's economy has never run that way.
Results Oriented|Giving.ask: What have you funded and never checked on?

Results Oriented|Healing.recognize: You get a hurting person to the other side and you will not let go halfway, and people have come through because of that. The cost is that recovery on your schedule is still your schedule, and one or two of them are performing for you now.
Results Oriented|Healing.ask: Who is pretending to be better for your benefit?

Results Oriented|Interpretation.recognize: You teach a passage toward what it should produce in a life, and your groups do not drift into abstraction. The blind spot is that some scripture produces nothing at all, it is only for beholding, and you have skipped it every year.
Results Oriented|Interpretation.ask: Which passages do you never reach?

Results Oriented|Knowledge.recognize: You learn what will change something and you stop when you have enough to act, which is more discipline than most scholars manage. The cost is that you have never known anything for its own sake, and it shows in how you pray.
Results Oriented|Knowledge.ask: What have you studied with no use in mind?

Results Oriented|Leadership.recognize: Your teams deliver, consistently, and people join you because working under you means the thing will actually happen. What you cannot feel is the tally of people who were spent getting there, and that none of them told you.
Results Oriented|Leadership.ask: Who burned out under you, and where are they now?

Results Oriented|Mercy.recognize: You do not just feel for someone, you get their situation changed, and there are families whose lives are different because of you. The blind spot is that a person whose situation cannot change makes you uncomfortable, and you visit less.
Results Oriented|Mercy.ask: Who have you stopped visiting because nothing improves?

Results Oriented|Miracles.recognize: You pray for what needs to happen and you stay at it until it does, and you have watched God move. The cost is that prayer has become another way of getting things done, and you would not recognise a no if it came.
Results Oriented|Miracles.ask: What has God said no to that you kept asking for?

Results Oriented|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people grow, measurably, and you could name what has changed in each of them this year. The blind spot is that they know they are being tracked, and the ones who are not progressing have quietly moved to another group.
Results Oriented|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who left your group without telling you why?

Results Oriented|Prophecy.recognize: You name what is wrong because you want it put right, not because you enjoy naming it, and things do get put right. The cost is that repentance is not a deliverable, and you have pushed people toward looking repentant.
Results Oriented|Prophecy.ask: Who apologised to you without meaning it?

Results Oriented|Service.recognize: The job gets done, all of it, to the end, and you do not leave a task half-standing for somebody else. The blind spot is that you have done the last third of several people's work, and they no longer expect to be held to it.
Results Oriented|Service.ask: Whose part have you been quietly completing?

Results Oriented|Teaching.recognize: You teach toward something you can actually watch happen in your class, and you do not mistake attendance for learning. The cost is that formation is slow and mostly invisible, and you have written off your best year as a failure.
Results Oriented|Teaching.ask: Which year of teaching did you count as wasted?

Results Oriented|Tongues.recognize: You pray for things and you notice what comes of it, so your prayer life is not sentimental. The blind spot is that this is the one practice with nothing to show for it, and it is the first thing to go in a busy month.
Results Oriented|Tongues.ask: What did prayer lose to this week?

Results Oriented|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you because your advice actually gets them somewhere, and you will not leave anyone with something merely thoughtful. The cost is that some decisions are not problems to be got past, and you have hurried a person through one.
Results Oriented|Wisdom.ask: Who did you push toward a decision they were not ready for?

Sensitive and Warm|Administration.recognize: You run things in a way that takes account of what people are carrying, so nobody on your rota feels like a slot. The blind spot is that you have left people in roles they are not doing well, because moving them would hurt.
Sensitive and Warm|Administration.ask: Who is in a role you know they cannot do?

Sensitive and Warm|Apostleship.recognize: You go to a new place and people feel welcomed before they feel evangelised, which is why doors open for you. The cost is that a work needs someone willing to be disliked in year two, and you have never been able to be that person.
Sensitive and Warm|Apostleship.ask: Who needed a hard thing from you and did not get it?

Sensitive and Warm|Discernment.recognize: You can tell when someone is fragile and you handle them accordingly, and people trust you with what they hide from others. The blind spot is that you handle people who are not fragile at all the same way, and they know they are being managed.
Sensitive and Warm|Discernment.ask: Who are you being careful with who does not need it?

Sensitive and Warm|Evangelism.recognize: Nobody feels judged talking to you about faith, and people who had written off the church will still sit with you. The cost is that the gospel contains a word about sin, and yours has arrived so gently that some of them never heard it.
Sensitive and Warm|Evangelism.ask: Which friend has heard only the kind half of it?

Sensitive and Warm|Exhortation.recognize: You know how to put a hard thing so that it can actually be taken, and people change because of you rather than shutting down. The blind spot is that you have rounded some things down so far that the person heard reassurance.
Sensitive and Warm|Exhortation.ask: What did you say so kindly that it did not land?

Sensitive and Warm|Faith.recognize: You do not push your faith at people or make anyone feel small for doubting, and doubters stay near you. The cost is that you have let a friend go on believing something false, because correcting it would have been unkind.
Sensitive and Warm|Faith.ask: What are you letting someone believe that is not true?

Sensitive and Warm|Giving.recognize: You give in a way that costs the receiver nothing in dignity, and people can take from you without feeling reduced. The blind spot is that some people needed the discomfort of asking, and you removed it every occasion.
Sensitive and Warm|Giving.ask: Who have you funded past the point it helped them?

Sensitive and Warm|Healing.recognize: Hurting people rest with you, because there is no pressure in your presence and nothing is being required of them. The cost is that healing eventually requires something to be required, and you have asked nothing of anyone in years.
Sensitive and Warm|Healing.ask: Who is at ease with you and not getting better?

Sensitive and Warm|Interpretation.recognize: You teach the hard passages with real care for who is in the room, and nobody has been crushed by scripture on your watch. The blind spot is that a text can be cushioned until it says nothing, and you could not tell where that line is.
Sensitive and Warm|Interpretation.ask: Which passage do you always take the edge off?

Sensitive and Warm|Knowledge.recognize: You share what you know without making anyone feel stupid, so people ask you the basic questions they would ask nobody else. The cost is that you have agreed with things you knew to be wrong rather than embarrass someone.
Sensitive and Warm|Knowledge.ask: When did you last correct somebody in front of others?

Sensitive and Warm|Leadership.recognize: People are not afraid of you, and your team brings you bad news early because of it. The blind spot is that you have carried underperformance for years rather than have one difficult conversation, and the rest of the team knows exactly who.
Sensitive and Warm|Leadership.ask: Who should have been moved on two years ago?

Sensitive and Warm|Mercy.recognize: You make suffering people feel held, and there is nothing performed about it, they can tell that it is real. The cost is that consolation is not the whole of it, and some of what you offered was about your own difficulty with their pain.
Sensitive and Warm|Mercy.ask: Whose pain do you find hardest to sit near?

Sensitive and Warm|Miracles.recognize: You pray for people gently and they are not frightened of it, which matters more than most believers in healing will admit. The blind spot is that you also lower what you ask for, so that nobody is disappointed if nothing happens.
Sensitive and Warm|Miracles.ask: What did you not pray aloud because it might not happen?

Sensitive and Warm|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people feel safe with you in a way that is rare and worth a great deal. The cost is that safety and growth are not the same, and you have built a group where nothing much is asked of anyone.
Sensitive and Warm|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What have you asked of your people this year?

Sensitive and Warm|Prophecy.recognize: When you do name something wrong it lands, precisely because you are not the person who is forever naming things. The blind spot is how rarely that happens, and that you keep a list of things you have decided are not worth the upset.
Sensitive and Warm|Prophecy.ask: What is on the list you have decided not to raise?

Sensitive and Warm|Service.recognize: You serve in a way that leaves people feeling cared for rather than processed, and that is not common. The cost is that you take on work to spare somebody else the effort, and they never found out they could bear it.
Sensitive and Warm|Service.ask: Whose share have you been carrying to spare them?

Sensitive and Warm|Teaching.recognize: Nobody is humiliated in your class, and people who were burned by teachers before will learn from you. The blind spot is that you have steered around the doctrines that upset people, and your class is unprepared for a hard season.
Sensitive and Warm|Teaching.ask: What would your class do with real suffering?

Sensitive and Warm|Tongues.recognize: Your prayer draws people in rather than shutting them out, and the nervous will pray aloud beside you. The cost is that you keep the room comfortable, and you have never let a prayer meeting go somewhere difficult.
Sensitive and Warm|Tongues.ask: When did a prayer meeting last become uncomfortable?

Sensitive and Warm|Wisdom.recognize: People come to you knowing they will be treated kindly whatever they confess, and that is why they come at all. The blind spot is that some of them needed a hard answer and got a gentle one, and went away and did it anyway.
Sensitive and Warm|Wisdom.ask: Who did you not talk out of it?

Sensitive to Others|Administration.recognize: You build around the people you actually have rather than an ideal team, so nothing you run asks more of someone than they can give. The blind spot is that your own name is on nothing, and you have designed a system you can be left out of.
Sensitive to Others|Administration.ask: What in this ministry is yours?

Sensitive to Others|Apostleship.recognize: You fit yourself to a new culture rather than making it fit you, and you are trusted quickly in places outsiders usually are not. The cost is that you have accommodated so thoroughly that nobody there knows what you actually think.
Sensitive to Others|Apostleship.ask: What do you believe that you have not said there?

Sensitive to Others|Discernment.recognize: You pick up when your presence is unwelcome and you make yourself scarce before anyone has to say it. The blind spot is that you also read discomfort where there is none, and rooms you were wanted in have gone without you.
Sensitive to Others|Discernment.ask: Where did you leave that nobody wanted you to leave?

Sensitive to Others|Evangelism.recognize: You never push, so nobody has ever felt cornered by you, and that reputation is why people talk to you at all. The cost is that you have gone quiet at exactly the moment a person was ready to be asked something.
Sensitive to Others|Evangelism.ask: Who was ready, and did you ask?

Sensitive to Others|Exhortation.recognize: You tailor what you say to what the person can actually take, and it lands because of that. The blind spot is that you have edited yourself down so far in some conversations that nothing was left to land.
Sensitive to Others|Exhortation.ask: What did you trim until it disappeared?

Sensitive to Others|Faith.recognize: You do not make your faith anyone else's problem, and people who are hostile to Christians are not hostile to you. The cost is that you have made yourself small around unbelief so often that your own faith now has less room in your life.
Sensitive to Others|Faith.ask: Where do you not bring your faith?

Sensitive to Others|Giving.recognize: You give in a way that puts nobody under obligation, quietly, often without your name on it. The blind spot is that you take nothing back, ever, and the people who love you have no way to give to you.
Sensitive to Others|Giving.ask: Who has been trying to give you something?

Sensitive to Others|Healing.recognize: You are careful with hurting people and you never crowd them, and they know they can be near you without being worked on. The cost is that you have needs of your own in that room and have never once mentioned them.
Sensitive to Others|Healing.ask: Who knows what this year has cost you?

Sensitive to Others|Interpretation.recognize: You teach with an ear for who is listening, and you will not use a passage as a weapon. The blind spot is that you have let a room's discomfort decide your teaching, and the text now says only what they can bear.
Sensitive to Others|Interpretation.ask: Whose reaction do you write around?

Sensitive to Others|Knowledge.recognize: You never make what you know a burden to anyone, and you will let a conversation go by rather than dominate it. The cost is that a room has repeatedly settled on something wrong while the one person who knew better said nothing.
Sensitive to Others|Knowledge.ask: Which wrong conclusion did you watch a room reach?

Sensitive to Others|Leadership.recognize: You lead in a way that fits itself to your people, and nobody under you feels steamrollered. The blind spot is that a team also needs to know where its leader stands, and yours could not tell you what you want.
Sensitive to Others|Leadership.ask: What do you want that your team has never heard?

Sensitive to Others|Mercy.recognize: You are careful never to make a suffering person feel like a burden, and that carefulness is itself a kindness. The cost is that you take up so little room that they cannot tell whether they are a burden or not, and some of them worry about it.
Sensitive to Others|Mercy.ask: Who is worried about how much they take from you?

Sensitive to Others|Miracles.recognize: You will not put anyone on the spot in prayer, and nobody has been embarrassed at your hands. The blind spot is that you have talked yourself out of asking for something large because of how it might land on somebody in the room.
Sensitive to Others|Miracles.ask: What did you not ask for because of who was listening?

Sensitive to Others|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You take great care not to intrude, and your people never feel watched. The cost is that you have waited to be invited into things you should have walked into, and a few of them read your restraint as not caring.
Sensitive to Others|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who thinks you did not want to be involved?

Sensitive to Others|Prophecy.recognize: You will not name a thing in a way that humiliates anyone, and when you speak, dignity survives. The blind spot is that you have gone silent so often for the sake of the room that some things have run for years unchallenged.
Sensitive to Others|Prophecy.ask: What has run unchallenged because you did not want to disturb anything?

Sensitive to Others|Service.recognize: You slot yourself wherever the gap is and never make anybody rearrange around you. The cost is that you now hold every job nobody wanted, and nobody arranged that deliberately, including you.
Sensitive to Others|Service.ask: How did you end up with what you are doing?

Sensitive to Others|Teaching.recognize: You watch the room and you teach the people rather than the notes, so nobody is left behind in your class. The blind spot is that you defer to the loudest reaction in the room, and one person has been steering your teaching for months.
Sensitive to Others|Teaching.ask: Who in your class are you teaching around?

Sensitive to Others|Tongues.recognize: You are careful never to make prayer awkward for anyone else, and the self-conscious can pray near you. The cost is that you have never prayed in your own voice in front of another person.
Sensitive to Others|Tongues.ask: Would anyone recognise how you pray alone?

Sensitive to Others|Wisdom.recognize: You give advice in a way that leaves the person free, and nobody has ever felt managed by you. The blind spot is that leaving someone free can also be a way of not risking yourself, and a few of them wanted you to say it straight.
Sensitive to Others|Wisdom.ask: Who asked what you thought, and did you tell them?

Sociable|Administration.recognize: Nothing you run feels bureaucratic, because you know everyone involved by name and it happens over coffee rather than by email. The blind spot is that a system held together by your relationships falls over the week you are unavailable.
Sociable|Administration.ask: What would stop working if you did not know everybody?

Sociable|Apostleship.recognize: You land in a new place and within a month you know half the street, which is how the work gets its first footing. The cost is that going wide is easy for you and going deep is not, and a work needs someone who stayed with three people.
Sociable|Apostleship.ask: Which three people are you actually building on?

Sociable|Discernment.recognize: You have a wide sense of what is going on across a whole church, because you talk to everyone in it. The blind spot is that you also hear everything, and you have formed views about people out of what other people said.
Sociable|Discernment.ask: Who have you judged on hearsay?

Sociable|Evangelism.recognize: You meet more unbelievers in a week than most Christians meet in a year, and you are genuinely liked by them. The cost is that being liked is pleasant, and there are friendships you have protected by never bringing it up.
Sociable|Evangelism.ask: Which friend would you lose if you said it?

Sociable|Exhortation.recognize: You raise a room without effort and people leave a conversation with you feeling better than they arrived. The blind spot is that you move on quickly, and the person who needed a second hour got twenty minutes and a fond goodbye.
Sociable|Exhortation.ask: Who needed longer than you gave them?

Sociable|Faith.recognize: Your faith is lived among people rather than in private, and nobody has to guess where you stand because they see you constantly. The cost is that you have almost no practice at being alone with God, and it unsettles you a little.
Sociable|Faith.ask: How long can you be alone before you reach for someone?

Sociable|Giving.recognize: You are generous in the moment, with meals, rounds, lifts, and your house is always open. The blind spot is that this is also how you are liked, and you have never given to anyone who could not be present to thank you.
Sociable|Giving.ask: What have you given where nobody knew it was you?

Sociable|Healing.recognize: You surround a hurting person with people, and loneliness rarely survives near you. The cost is that some grief needs one person for a long stretch rather than many for an evening, and the long stretch is what you find hard.
Sociable|Healing.ask: Who did you gather people around instead of staying with?

Sociable|Interpretation.recognize: You teach in conversation rather than monologue, and your groups actually talk, which is rarer than it sounds. The blind spot is that a discussion you enjoyed is not the same as a text being understood, and you rarely land it.
Sociable|Interpretation.ask: What did your group conclude last week?

Sociable|Knowledge.recognize: You learn from people rather than books, and you know an enormous amount about what is actually happening. The cost is that all of it came from a conversation, and you have never sat alone with a hard subject long enough to master it.
Sociable|Knowledge.ask: What have you learned alone this year?

Sociable|Leadership.recognize: Your team likes each other, and that is not an accident, you built it. The blind spot is that being among them is also how you avoid the parts of leading that happen alone, and the decisions nobody can help you with are all overdue.
Sociable|Leadership.ask: Which decision are you avoiding by staying busy with people?

Sociable|Mercy.recognize: You notice the person nobody is talking to and you go over, every occasion, without being asked. The cost is that you go over to a great many, and not one of them has had you for long enough to say the hard part.
Sociable|Mercy.ask: Who started to tell you something and did not finish?

Sociable|Miracles.recognize: You pray readily with others and something rises in a room you are in, because you bring people together and they believe more than they would alone. The blind spot is that you have very little private history with God to draw on when the room is empty.
Sociable|Miracles.ask: What has God done in your life that no one else saw?

Sociable|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You know everybody, their spouse, their job, their children's names, and people feel known by you at a scale most pastors cannot manage. The cost is that being known by name is not the same as being known, and nobody has told you the worst thing.
Sociable|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who has told you something they have told nobody else?

Sociable|Prophecy.recognize: You can say a hard thing without the relationship breaking, because there is so much goodwill toward you. The blind spot is that goodwill is the thing you are most careful with, and there are things you will not say in order to protect it.

Sociable|Service.recognize: You make working together enjoyable, and people sign up for the setup shift because you will be on it. The cost is that you do not work alone well, and the unglamorous solitary jobs have all quietly gone to somebody else.
Sociable|Service.ask: Which job here does nobody see anyone doing?

Sociable|Teaching.recognize: Your class is a place people come for each other as much as for the content, and that is why attendance holds. The blind spot is that you have optimised for the room being good, and you would struggle to say what anyone has learned.
Sociable|Teaching.ask: What would your class say they learned last term?

Sociable|Tongues.recognize: You pray easily with others and have never found it awkward, which frees the room. The cost is that your prayer life is almost entirely corporate, and God has not had you on your own in a while.
Sociable|Tongues.ask: When did you last pray alone for an hour?

Sociable|Wisdom.recognize: You have advisers everywhere and you can get five views on a decision before the end of the day. The blind spot is that you have used all that talking to put off a decision that was always going to be yours alone.
Sociable|Wisdom.ask: What are you still gathering opinions on?

Spontaneous|Administration.recognize: You can throw together whatever the day needs and it works, and the event ran because you improvised. The blind spot is that the people around you have no way to prepare, and their week is spent absorbing your changes.
Spontaneous|Administration.ask: Whose week did you rearrange this month?

Spontaneous|Apostleship.recognize: You will go now, with what you have, and you have started things that would never have survived a committee. The cost is that a work begun on a Tuesday afternoon needs someone still there in three years, and that has not always been you.
Spontaneous|Apostleship.ask: What did you begin and leave?

Spontaneous|Discernment.recognize: You act the moment something feels wrong, without waiting to build a case, and you have caught real things early. The blind spot is that you also act on a mood, and from inside you cannot tell those two apart.
Spontaneous|Discernment.ask: How do you tell a warning from a bad morning?

Spontaneous|Evangelism.recognize: You will talk to anyone about Christ in the middle of anything, with no preparation, and it works because it is obviously not a technique. The cost is that a conversation you began on the spot is one you have not always come back for.
Spontaneous|Evangelism.ask: Who did you talk to once and never again?

Spontaneous|Exhortation.recognize: You say the encouraging thing the moment it occurs to you, and people get it while it still matters. The blind spot is that you say the discouraging thing the moment it occurs to you as well, and the same quickness produced both.
Spontaneous|Exhortation.ask: What did you say before you had thought about it?

Spontaneous|Faith.recognize: You will step out on something with no arrangements made, and God has met you there more than once. The cost is that other people are usually holding the consequences, and you have not always asked them first.
Spontaneous|Faith.ask: Who paid for your last step of faith?

Spontaneous|Giving.recognize: You give on the spot, whatever is in your pocket, and people have been helped at the exact hour they needed it. The blind spot is that the ongoing commitments you made in the same mood are the ones that quietly lapsed.
Spontaneous|Giving.ask: What are you still meant to be giving to?

Spontaneous|Healing.recognize: You will drop everything and go to someone the moment you hear, and that has meant a great deal to people. The cost is that healing is slow and mostly unglamorous, and it is the ninth visit you find hard, not the first.
Spontaneous|Healing.ask: Who did you go to in the crisis and not since?

Spontaneous|Interpretation.recognize: You will follow a passage wherever it goes in the moment, and your groups have had evenings nobody planned that they still talk about. The blind spot is that a group also needs to get through a book, and yours has not completed one.
Spontaneous|Interpretation.ask: Which study did you abandon halfway?

Spontaneous|Knowledge.recognize: You learn by chasing whatever catches you, and you know a startling range of things as a result. The cost is that your knowledge has holes exactly where each subject got boring, and you do not know where those holes are.
Spontaneous|Knowledge.ask: What did you stop learning at the dull part?

Spontaneous|Leadership.recognize: You can change course the day the situation changes, and your team is never stuck defending last year's decision. The blind spot is that they cannot plan anything, and the good people who need to plan have started to leave.
Spontaneous|Leadership.ask: Who left because they could not predict you?

Spontaneous|Mercy.recognize: You go to people the moment you feel it, so your kindness arrives fast and unannounced and is never calculated. The cost is that steadiness is most of what a suffering person actually needs, and yours comes in bursts.
Spontaneous|Mercy.ask: Who gets you intensely and then not at all?

Spontaneous|Miracles.recognize: You will pray for a stranger in a car park because it occurred to you, and things have happened. The blind spot is that you rarely stay to find out what came of it, and you have no idea what most of those prayers cost the person afterwards.
Spontaneous|Miracles.ask: What became of the last person you prayed for that way?

Spontaneous|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people get you at unexpected hours and in unexpected places, and there is nothing institutional about your care. The cost is that they cannot rely on it, and the ones who needed something regular have found it elsewhere.
Spontaneous|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who in your care needs a standing arrangement they do not have?

Spontaneous|Prophecy.recognize: You say the thing while the room is still in it, and it has real force because it is not rehearsed. The blind spot is that you have said several things you would not have said an hour later, and none of them can be taken back.
Spontaneous|Prophecy.ask: What would you unsay if you could?

Spontaneous|Service.recognize: You spot the need and you are already doing it, with no discussion, and a great deal gets done around you. The cost is that you begin more than you complete, and somebody else has been closing your loops for years.

Spontaneous|Teaching.recognize: You will follow the room's question rather than your notes, and your class has gone places a prepared lesson never would. The blind spot is that you have relied on that so long you no longer prepare, and the difference is starting to show.
Spontaneous|Teaching.ask: How long did you spend preparing last week?

Spontaneous|Tongues.recognize: Prayer comes to you anywhere, in the car, mid-conversation, and there is nothing stiff about your life with God. The cost is that you have never built anything you hold to, and the seasons you did not feel like praying are simply blank.
Spontaneous|Tongues.ask: What does your prayer life look like when you do not feel like it?

Spontaneous|Wisdom.recognize: You give people an answer while the moment is still live, and it often turns out to be right. The blind spot is that you have never gone back to check the ones that were not, and nobody returns to tell you.
Spontaneous|Wisdom.ask: Which of your answers went badly for someone?

Strong Practical Skills|Administration.recognize: Whatever the ministry needs doing, you can do it, so nothing waits while somebody looks for a specialist. The blind spot is that the list of things only you can do has grown every year, and nobody ever decided to put you there.
Strong Practical Skills|Administration.ask: What is on your plate that nobody assigned you?

Strong Practical Skills|Apostleship.recognize: You can make a new work function with almost nothing, wiring it, fixing it, driving it, and it stands because you are physically able to make it stand. The cost is that you built a thing which needs a person like you, and there is not another one.
Strong Practical Skills|Apostleship.ask: Who could take over what you set up?

Strong Practical Skills|Discernment.recognize: You can tell when a job or a scheme will not work, because you have done the work and you know what it takes. The blind spot is that this reliable judgment about things has quietly become your judgment about people too.
Strong Practical Skills|Discernment.ask: Who did you write off as useless?

Strong Practical Skills|Evangelism.recognize: You reach people by turning up and fixing something for them, and men who would never sit through a service will talk to you in a driveway. The cost is that the fixing is where you are comfortable, and some of them have never heard you say why you came.
Strong Practical Skills|Evangelism.ask: Who have you helped for years and never told?

Strong Practical Skills|Exhortation.recognize: You encourage people by doing it alongside them, and they get going because you were there doing it too. The blind spot is that a person who cannot do what you do learns something about themselves while you demonstrate it.
Strong Practical Skills|Exhortation.ask: Who felt small watching you work?

Strong Practical Skills|Faith.recognize: You act on faith by getting to work, and there is nothing abstract about what you believe. The cost is that you have never had to trust God for anything you could not have sorted out yourself given a free weekend.
Strong Practical Skills|Faith.ask: What have you needed God for that your own two arms could not reach?

Strong Practical Skills|Giving.recognize: You give your labour rather than your money, and what you give is worth far more than the cheque you would have written. The blind spot is that giving your work means you are always present for it, and you have never given anonymously.
Strong Practical Skills|Giving.ask: What have you given that nobody could trace to you?

Strong Practical Skills|Healing.recognize: You show up at a house in crisis and the boiler is working again by evening, and that is real love arriving in a form the family can use. The cost is that when there is nothing to mend, you do not know how to stay in the room.
Strong Practical Skills|Healing.ask: How long do you last in a room with nothing to fix?

Strong Practical Skills|Interpretation.recognize: You take a passage and show people what it looks like on a building site, and men who found scripture remote suddenly have it. The blind spot is that you only teach what can be demonstrated, and a great deal of it cannot.
Strong Practical Skills|Interpretation.ask: What in scripture can you not show anyone how to do?

Strong Practical Skills|Knowledge.recognize: You know how things actually work, not in theory, and people come to you because you have taken one apart. The cost is that you dismiss what cannot be taken apart, and you have said so in front of people who study for a living.
Strong Practical Skills|Knowledge.ask: Whose learning have you dismissed as pointless?

Strong Practical Skills|Leadership.recognize: You lead by being the one who can do every job on the team, and nobody follows you resentfully, because you have worked their shift. The blind spot is that you step in whenever it goes slowly, and no one under you has ever finished struggling with something.
Strong Practical Skills|Leadership.ask: Who did you take a job off before they had learned it?

Strong Practical Skills|Mercy.recognize: You are at the house with a van, a ladder, a toolbox, the week after the funeral, and what you do is worth more than words would have been. The cost is that the work also means you never have to sit down, and you have not sat down yet.
Strong Practical Skills|Mercy.ask: When did you last visit somebody with nothing to do there?

Strong Practical Skills|Miracles.recognize: You pray, and then you get up and do what you can, and God has often worked in the gap between those two. The blind spot is that you have shrunk that gap to almost nothing, and very little is left in your life that would require him.
Strong Practical Skills|Miracles.ask: What would collapse if God did not act?
