Strong Practical Skills|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know that if something breaks you will be there, and that is not a small kind of care. The cost is that you have made your ministry the practical parts, and the man whose marriage is failing needs something you do not offer.
Strong Practical Skills|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who needed to talk and got a repair instead?

Strong Practical Skills|Prophecy.recognize: You say what is wrong with something plainly, the way you would about a bad joint or a bodged wire, and there is nothing personal in it. The blind spot is that people are not joints, and they do not hear it the way another tradesman would.
Strong Practical Skills|Prophecy.ask: Who took what you said far harder than you meant it?

Strong Practical Skills|Service.recognize: There is almost nothing around this church you cannot do, and a great deal of it has quietly become yours. The cost is that you have never once said a job was too much, and everyone has drawn the obvious conclusion.
Strong Practical Skills|Service.ask: What did you take on this year that you should have refused?

Strong Practical Skills|Teaching.recognize: You teach by showing, and people who learn nothing from a talk learn from you. The blind spot is that you have no way to teach what cannot be shown, and you have quietly stopped teaching those parts.
Strong Practical Skills|Teaching.ask: What have you dropped from your teaching because you could not demonstrate it?

Strong Practical Skills|Tongues.recognize: You are honest that you would rather be doing something than sitting still, and the work you do is worship of a real kind. The cost is that prayer asks you to be of no use for an hour, and that is the one thing you have never managed.
Strong Practical Skills|Tongues.ask: When did you last sit with God and do nothing?

Strong Practical Skills|Wisdom.recognize: Your advice is worth having because it comes from someone who has actually done the thing rather than read about it. The blind spot is that you treat every question as a practical one, and some of what people bring you is not.
Strong Practical Skills|Wisdom.ask: Who brought you something that had no practical answer?

Strong Sense of Duty|Administration.recognize: You take on what needs doing because it needs doing, and the unglamorous roles in this church are filled by people like you. The blind spot is that you have never once asked whether a role needs to exist, only whether you would fill it.
Strong Sense of Duty|Administration.ask: What are you doing that ought to simply stop?

Strong Sense of Duty|Apostleship.recognize: You will go where you are needed rather than where you would like to go, and hard postings get filled because of that. The cost is that you have never asked what God actually made you for, because what was required always arrived first.
Strong Sense of Duty|Apostleship.ask: What would you do if nothing were required of you?

Strong Sense of Duty|Discernment.recognize: You can tell when something is being neglected that somebody ought to be attending to, and you are usually right about it. The blind spot is that noticing a gap has become the same thing as being the one who fills it.
Strong Sense of Duty|Discernment.ask: What did you notice last that was not yours to fix?

Strong Sense of Duty|Evangelism.recognize: You speak about Christ because you believe you must, and that faithfulness has put the gospel in front of people who would never have heard it. The cost is that a person can tell the difference between being loved and being covered.
Strong Sense of Duty|Evangelism.ask: Who have you spoken to out of conscience rather than care?

Strong Sense of Duty|Exhortation.recognize: You go and encourage the person nobody else remembered, because it was the right thing and you do right things. The blind spot is that they can tell it was the right thing, and being somebody's right thing is a lonely position.
Strong Sense of Duty|Exhortation.ask: Who do you visit because you ought to?

Strong Sense of Duty|Faith.recognize: You keep your promises to God whether or not you feel anything, and there are years of yours that only faithfulness explains. The cost is that ought has grown so large in your life that you would no longer recognise wanting to.
Strong Sense of Duty|Faith.ask: When did you last do something for God because you wanted to?

Strong Sense of Duty|Giving.recognize: You give what you are supposed to give, on principle, before anything else is spent, and you have never once been late. The blind spot is that you have also never given anything you were not required to give.
Strong Sense of Duty|Giving.ask: What have you given beyond what you owed?

Strong Sense of Duty|Healing.recognize: You visit the sick because visiting the sick is what a Christian does, and you have visited more of them than anyone knows. The cost is that duty gets you into the room and then tells you nothing about what to do once you are there.
Strong Sense of Duty|Healing.ask: What do you talk about once you have arrived?

Strong Sense of Duty|Interpretation.recognize: You prepare because people are relying on you and you will not let them down, and your teaching is faithful to the text. The blind spot is that you have not opened scripture for yourself, outside preparation, in a very long while.
Strong Sense of Duty|Interpretation.ask: When did you last read the Bible with nothing to prepare?

Strong Sense of Duty|Knowledge.recognize: You learn what a person in your position is supposed to know, thoroughly, and nobody could accuse you of coasting. The cost is that you have never followed a question that was not on the list, and no longer know what would interest you.
Strong Sense of Duty|Knowledge.ask: What would you study if no one needed you to?

Strong Sense of Duty|Leadership.recognize: You took the role because somebody had to and nobody else would, and you have done it properly for years. The blind spot is that a leader who is only there from necessity leads people who can feel it, and they are only there from necessity too.
Strong Sense of Duty|Leadership.ask: Would you take this role again if asked today?

Strong Sense of Duty|Mercy.recognize: You are at the funeral, the hospital, the difficult visit, because these are the things one does, and your presence has meant a great deal. The cost is that nobody has ever asked whether you wanted to be there, including you.
Strong Sense of Duty|Mercy.ask: Which of these visits do you dread?

Strong Sense of Duty|Miracles.recognize: You pray for the sick whenever you are asked to, faithfully, whatever you inwardly suspect will come of it. The blind spot is that this is the one part of the Christian life which cannot be done out of duty, and you have done it that way for years.
Strong Sense of Duty|Miracles.ask: What do you actually believe will happen?

Strong Sense of Duty|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Nobody in your care is neglected, because you have a clear sense of what is owed to each of them and you meet it. The cost is that they are receiving what is due to them, and a few have worked out that this is not the same as being loved.
Strong Sense of Duty|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Which of your people do you actually enjoy?

Strong Sense of Duty|Prophecy.recognize: You say the hard thing because it would be wrong not to, not because you enjoy it, and that gives your words real weight. The blind spot is that you have said several things which were true and which nobody had asked you to be the one to say.
Strong Sense of Duty|Prophecy.ask: What did you say because you felt you had to?

Strong Sense of Duty|Service.recognize: The job gets done because you said you would do it, and you have never let a rota down in your life. The cost is that you now do a great many things you took on years ago and have not wanted to do for most of that stretch.
Strong Sense of Duty|Service.ask: What did you agree to that you have wanted out of for years?

Strong Sense of Duty|Teaching.recognize: You teach because the class needed a teacher and nobody else came forward, and you have prepared properly every week regardless. The blind spot is that a class can tell whether their teacher wanted to be there, and yours have worked it out.
Strong Sense of Duty|Teaching.ask: What would happen if you said you were done?

Strong Sense of Duty|Tongues.recognize: You pray at the hours you said you would, whether or not it is doing anything for you, and you have never let the practice slide. The cost is that prayer is the one place nothing is being demanded of you, and you have made a demand of it anyway.
Strong Sense of Duty|Tongues.ask: What would prayer be if you were not meant to do it?

Strong Sense of Duty|Wisdom.recognize: People bring you decisions because you will tell them what they ought to do, and you will not soften it to be liked. The blind spot is that not everything in a life is a question of what one ought to do, and you have made a few of them so.
Strong Sense of Duty|Wisdom.ask: Whose decision did you turn into a duty?

Strong-willed|Administration.recognize: You will not let a system be watered down by whoever complained most recently, and what you build survives pressure. The blind spot is that some of those complaints were correct, and you can no longer tell which, because you stopped weighing them.
Strong-willed|Administration.ask: Which complaint have you dismissed more than twice?

Strong-willed|Apostleship.recognize: You will keep a new work going through the years nobody believes in it, and things exist because you would not let them die. The cost is that you would also keep one going long after God had finished with it.
Strong-willed|Apostleship.ask: What have you refused to let die?

Strong-willed|Discernment.recognize: Once you have read a situation you are not talked out of it, and that has protected people from being smooth-talked. The blind spot is that a first read you cannot revise is a first read you will spend years justifying.
Strong-willed|Discernment.ask: When did you last change your mind about someone?

Strong-willed|Evangelism.recognize: You do not retreat when a conversation turns hostile, and people who wanted to shut you up have found that you do not shut up. The cost is that some of them were not arguing, they were asking, and you argued anyway.
Strong-willed|Evangelism.ask: Who asked you a real question and got a fight?

Strong-willed|Exhortation.recognize: You will not let a person give up on themselves, and you have outlasted somebody's despair more than once. The blind spot is that the same immovability means you cannot hear it when a person tells you they need to stop.
Strong-willed|Exhortation.ask: Who told you they were done, and did you accept it?

Strong-willed|Faith.recognize: Your faith does not bend when it is unpopular or expensive, and people around you have held on because you did. The cost is that you cannot tell conviction from refusing to be beaten, and neither can anybody else.
Strong-willed|Faith.ask: What do you believe partly because someone told you not to?

Strong-willed|Giving.recognize: You committed to something and you will not be moved off it, whatever your own year looks like, and ministries have survived on that. The blind spot is that you will not be moved onto anything new either, and the need has changed since then.
Strong-willed|Giving.ask: What need has arisen that you refused to fund?

Strong-willed|Healing.recognize: You will not give up on a person other people have written off, and one or two of them are alive because of it. The cost is that you also will not let go of someone who needs releasing, and you cannot tell those two apart.
Strong-willed|Healing.ask: Who are you holding onto for your own sake?

Strong-willed|Interpretation.recognize: You will hold an unpopular reading of a text if you believe it is right, and you do not teach to the room. The blind spot is that the last person to change your mind about a passage did it a very long while ago.
Strong-willed|Interpretation.ask: Which of your readings has moved in ten years?

Strong-willed|Knowledge.recognize: You will not be pushed into agreeing with something you have not been shown, and that has kept a lot of nonsense out of your church. The cost is that showing you now takes more effort than most people will spend, so nobody bothers.
Strong-willed|Knowledge.ask: Who stopped trying to persuade you?

Strong-willed|Leadership.recognize: You hold the line when a team wants to abandon something hard, and things have been completed under you that would otherwise have collapsed. The blind spot is that your team has learned disagreement is a long and exhausting road.
Strong-willed|Leadership.ask: When did your team last change your decision?

Strong-willed|Mercy.recognize: You keep showing up for someone long after everyone else has run out of patience, and that persistence is a mercy few can offer. The cost is that you have decided what they need, and you are going to give it to them whether or not it is that.
Strong-willed|Mercy.ask: Who told you what they needed, and did you believe them?

Strong-willed|Miracles.recognize: You will pray for the same impossible thing for years without embarrassment, and that stubbornness is closer to faith than most people's caution. The blind spot is that you have never let God reply differently than you asked.
Strong-willed|Miracles.ask: What would it take for you to accept a different reply?

Strong-willed|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You will not let one of your people go, and there are people still in this church because you would not release them. The cost is that a few of them stayed because leaving you was harder than staying, which is not the same as being kept.
Strong-willed|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Who is still here because it would be difficult to leave you?

Strong-willed|Prophecy.recognize: You say the wrong thing is wrong and you go on saying it after the room has moved on, and sometimes that is the only reason it gets addressed. The blind spot is that you have made it about being the one who was right.
Strong-willed|Prophecy.ask: What would you lose if somebody else fixed the problem?

Strong-willed|Service.recognize: You will complete a job in conditions that would have sent anyone else home, and there is work here that exists only because you refused to quit it. The cost is that you have taught the people around you that asking for help is weakness.
Strong-willed|Service.ask: When did you last ask somebody for help?

Strong-willed|Teaching.recognize: You will teach what the text says even when the class does not want it, and nobody is being flattered in your room. The blind spot is that a question you have already settled gets treated as an attack, and your class stopped raising those.
Strong-willed|Teaching.ask: Which question does your class no longer bring you?

Strong-willed|Tongues.recognize: You have prayed through seasons that would have ended other people's prayer lives, because you simply would not stop. The cost is that you cannot tell whether you are submitting to God in it or outlasting him.
Strong-willed|Tongues.ask: When did prayer last change what you wanted?

Strong-willed|Wisdom.recognize: You give the same advice under pressure that you gave without it, and nobody has seen you fold to make a conversation easier. The blind spot is that you have not sought a second opinion on anything in years.
Strong-willed|Wisdom.ask: Whose advice did you last actually take?

Supportive|Administration.recognize: You make other people's ministries work, in the arrangements nobody sees, and several things run because you are underneath them. The blind spot is that you have propped two or three of them up so long that nobody has asked whether they should still be running.
Supportive|Administration.ask: Which ministry would end if you stepped out?

Supportive|Apostleship.recognize: You are the one who goes with the one who was sent, and hard works have survived because somebody was there beside the founder. The cost is that you have never asked whether God sent you somewhere of your own.
Supportive|Apostleship.ask: Where would you go if nobody needed a second?

Supportive|Discernment.recognize: You can tell what a leader is about to need before they know it, and you have positioned things for people more than once. The blind spot is that you also see when they are going wrong, and helping them has become how you avoid saying it.
Supportive|Discernment.ask: What have you seen in the person you serve and never said?

Supportive|Evangelism.recognize: You are the one who drives, sets up, prays, and makes the evangelist's work possible, and souls have come in because of that. The cost is that you have decided you are not the one who speaks, and nobody made that decision but you.
Supportive|Evangelism.ask: Who would you talk to if it were your job?

Supportive|Exhortation.recognize: You are with the struggling person for as long as it takes, and people have come through things because you would not let them do it alone. The blind spot is that some of them are now unable to do anything without you present.
Supportive|Exhortation.ask: Who cannot attempt it unless you are watching?

Supportive|Faith.recognize: You hold up other people's faith when theirs is failing, and there are believers still believing because you kept believing near them. The cost is that nobody has ever done that for you, and you have not told anyone that you need it.
Supportive|Faith.ask: When your own faith went, who noticed?

Supportive|Giving.recognize: You fund other people's callings without needing any part in them, and things exist because your money was underneath them. The blind spot is that you have paid for something which was failing on its own terms, and the money delayed a necessary ending.
Supportive|Giving.ask: What have you kept afloat that should have sunk?

Supportive|Healing.recognize: You are the one still there in month eight, when the crisis is old news, and that steady presence has done more than any intervention. The cost is that your help has become part of how they cope, and neither of you has noticed.
Supportive|Healing.ask: Who has stopped getting better and grown comfortable?

Supportive|Interpretation.recognize: You make somebody else's teaching land, with the questions you ask and the way you take it seriously in front of the room. The blind spot is that you have views of your own which this room has never heard.
Supportive|Interpretation.ask: What did you think about the text that you did not say?

Supportive|Knowledge.recognize: You find what another person needs to know and put it in front of them, without needing to be the one who knows it. The cost is that you have made yourself useful to people whose work you would not argue for if asked.
Supportive|Knowledge.ask: Whose project are you helping that you do not believe in?

Supportive|Leadership.recognize: You make the leader above you look good and you mean it, and there is nothing false in your loyalty. The blind spot is that your steadiness underneath a poor decision has helped several poor decisions survive.
Supportive|Leadership.ask: Which of their decisions did you help along that you thought was wrong?

Supportive|Mercy.recognize: You are the one who keeps turning up for the person everybody else found exhausting, and they have not been abandoned because of you. The cost is that you have absorbed the consequences of their choices so consistently that they have never met one.
Supportive|Mercy.ask: What has that person never had to face?

Supportive|Miracles.recognize: You pray alongside the one who is asking, and rooms are stronger for your being in them, though you never lead. The blind spot is that you have never asked God for anything on your own behalf.
Supportive|Miracles.ask: What is your own unmet need?

Supportive|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You are the second pair of arms in everybody's care for everybody else, and people are held who would otherwise have fallen. The cost is that you are on nobody's list, and there is no one whose job it is to notice you.

Supportive|Prophecy.recognize: You make it possible for the person who says the hard thing to go on saying it, and hard things have survived in rooms because you were beside them. The blind spot is that you have never been the one to say it, and there are things only you know.
Supportive|Prophecy.ask: What do you know that only you could say?

Supportive|Service.recognize: Whatever anyone else is doing, you are underneath it making it possible, and you have never needed to be seen doing so. The cost is that you have no idea what you would do if you were not helping somebody else do theirs.

Supportive|Teaching.recognize: You keep a struggling student going, one conversation at a time, and people have learned who would have dropped out. The blind spot is that you have done some of their thinking for them, and they still cannot do it alone.
Supportive|Teaching.ask: Who still needs you to get through it?

Supportive|Tongues.recognize: You pray for other people constantly and there is nothing showy about it, just years of steady intercession nobody knows about. The cost is that you would find it strange, almost improper, to pray for yourself.
Supportive|Tongues.ask: When did you last pray for your own life?

Supportive|Wisdom.recognize: You help people think it through rather than telling them what to do, and they leave owning their own decision. The blind spot is that a few of them keep coming to think it through with you, and have not decided anything alone in years.
Supportive|Wisdom.ask: Who cannot decide without you now?

Very Loyal|Administration.recognize: You will not undermine a decision once it is made, even one you argued against, and systems hold under you because of it. The blind spot is that you have implemented things you knew were wrong and never raised them again.
Very Loyal|Administration.ask: What are you running that you argued against?

Very Loyal|Apostleship.recognize: You go where your church sends you and you stay, and works have been established because somebody was willing to be sent rather than to choose. The cost is that you would follow a leader somewhere God had not sent either of you.
Very Loyal|Apostleship.ask: Whose call are you following instead of your own?

Very Loyal|Discernment.recognize: You are hard to turn against someone, and people who have been gossiped about have found a friend in you. The blind spot is that you cannot see faults in the people you have bound yourself to, and you have been the last to know twice.
Very Loyal|Discernment.ask: Who were you the last to doubt?

Very Loyal|Evangelism.recognize: You keep on with the same friend, year after year, long past the point most Christians would have given up. The cost is that faithfulness to the friendship has quietly become the reason you no longer raise it.
Very Loyal|Evangelism.ask: How long since you last brought it up with them?

Very Loyal|Exhortation.recognize: You are in someone's corner permanently, and they know your encouragement is not conditional on how they are doing. The blind spot is that unconditional and honest are not the same, and yours stopped being honest a while ago.
Very Loyal|Exhortation.ask: When did you last tell that person something they did not want to hear?

Very Loyal|Faith.recognize: You have not left, through leaderships and seasons and things that drove other people out, and this church exists partly because people like you did not go. The cost is that you have confused faithfulness to a church with faithfulness to Christ.

Very Loyal|Giving.recognize: You have given to the same work for decades without wavering, and they have built on that certainty. The blind spot is that you have not asked in years whether it is still doing what it was doing when you started.
Very Loyal|Giving.ask: What is that ministry doing now?

Very Loyal|Healing.recognize: You are still there with the person everyone else stopped visiting, and your presence is the one constant in their recovery. The cost is that you would also cover for them, and you have already, more than once.
Very Loyal|Healing.ask: What have you concealed for someone you love?

Very Loyal|Interpretation.recognize: You teach what your tradition has always taught and you will not be moved by fashion, which has kept your group clear of a lot of nonsense. The blind spot is that you have never seriously examined the readings you inherited.
Very Loyal|Interpretation.ask: Which of your beliefs did you arrive at yourself?

Very Loyal|Knowledge.recognize: You will not repeat something damaging about a person you are bound to, and a great deal of gossip has died with you. The cost is that you will not hear it either, and one of those reports was true and needed acting on.
Very Loyal|Knowledge.ask: What did you refuse to listen to?

Very Loyal|Leadership.recognize: Your team knows you take the blame outward and give the credit inward, and they would follow you anywhere for it. The blind spot is that you have shielded people from consequences which would have grown them.
Very Loyal|Leadership.ask: Who has never met the result of their own mistake?

Very Loyal|Mercy.recognize: You do not drop people, ever, and there are those whose entire experience of being loved without conditions came from you. The cost is that you will make the case for someone against the plain facts, and you did it recently.
Very Loyal|Mercy.ask: Who did you argue for when you knew better?

Very Loyal|Miracles.recognize: You keep praying for the same person through years of nothing, because you do not give up on people. The blind spot is that you would also refuse to hear God saying something different about them.
Very Loyal|Miracles.ask: What might God be saying about them that you will not hear?

Very Loyal|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: Your people know you will never speak of them elsewhere, and that is why they tell you things. The cost is that you have kept a confidence which should have been broken, and the harm went on for as long as you kept it.
Very Loyal|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: What are you holding that somebody else should know?

Very Loyal|Prophecy.recognize: You will say the hard thing about anyone except the people you are bound to, and about everyone else you are fearless. The blind spot is exactly that exception, and everybody around you can see the shape of it.
Very Loyal|Prophecy.ask: Who is exempt from your honesty?

Very Loyal|Service.recognize: You have served the same ministry for twenty years and never once threatened to walk, and it was built on that. The cost is that you served it through a decade when it should have been closed and begun again as something else.
Very Loyal|Service.ask: What here has been the same for too long?

Very Loyal|Teaching.recognize: You do not undercut other teachers in front of your class, and there is no rivalry in you at all. The blind spot is that something false taught by a colleague has gone uncorrected because correcting it felt disloyal.
Very Loyal|Teaching.ask: What have you let your class go on believing?

Very Loyal|Tongues.recognize: You pray the way you were taught to pray, in the tradition that formed you, and there is nothing borrowed or fashionable about it. The cost is that you have never let God take your prayer life anywhere your church would find strange.
Very Loyal|Tongues.ask: What would you not do in prayer because of who taught you?

Very Loyal|Wisdom.recognize: People know your advice will never be used against them and never repeated, and that is most of why they ask you. The blind spot is that you give the person you are bound to a gentler reply than you give anyone else.

Very Responsible|Administration.recognize: If something under you goes wrong, you say so before anyone finds out, and nothing is hidden in your part of the operation. The blind spot is that you have taken the blame for failures which belonged to other people, and they let you.
Very Responsible|Administration.ask: Whose mistake did you own as your own?

Very Responsible|Apostleship.recognize: You do not begin a work you cannot see through, so nothing you have started was left stranded. The cost is that you have declined things God may have been calling you to, because you could not guarantee the ending.
Very Responsible|Apostleship.ask: What did you refuse because you could not promise to see it through?

Very Responsible|Discernment.recognize: You notice when something is going wrong and you treat it as yours to raise, so problems get named early around you. The blind spot is that you have started treating other people's failures as proof that you did not supervise well enough.
Very Responsible|Discernment.ask: What went wrong that had nothing to do with you?

Very Responsible|Evangelism.recognize: You feel the weight of the people you know who are far from God, and that weight has made you speak when it was uncomfortable. The cost is that their response is not yours to produce, and you have grieved it as though it were.
Very Responsible|Evangelism.ask: Whose refusal are you treating as your failure?

Very Responsible|Exhortation.recognize: When you tell someone you will help them get there, you mean it, and you are still involved six months later. The blind spot is that their progress has become something you are graded on, and they can feel that.
Very Responsible|Exhortation.ask: Whose growth would embarrass you if it stopped?

Very Responsible|Faith.recognize: You do what you have undertaken before God whether or not it goes well, and there is no gap between what you promised and what you do. The cost is that you now hold yourself liable for results which only God controls.
Very Responsible|Faith.ask: What are you blaming yourself for that God did?

Very Responsible|Giving.recognize: You treat other people's money as though it were held in trust, because it is, and the records are impeccable. The blind spot is that the same care has stopped you giving anything away without a scheme attached to it.
Very Responsible|Giving.ask: What have you given that you could not justify?

Very Responsible|Healing.recognize: When somebody is in trouble you take it on rather than passing it along, and people are not shuffled around on your watch. The cost is that you have taken on situations well beyond what you are equipped for, and told nobody.
Very Responsible|Healing.ask: What are you dealing with that needs a professional?

Very Responsible|Interpretation.recognize: You know that teaching scripture wrongly is a serious matter, and you prepare like a man who will be asked about it. The blind spot is that this weight has made you cautious, and your class receives only what you are certain of.
Very Responsible|Interpretation.ask: What would you teach if you would not be held to it?

Very Responsible|Knowledge.recognize: You will correct something you said last year if you have since found out it was wrong, publicly, which almost nobody does. The cost is that you have made yourself the guarantor of everything you have ever said, and it is a great deal to hold.
Very Responsible|Knowledge.ask: Which of your own words do you still regret?

Very Responsible|Leadership.recognize: Nothing fails under you without you naming your own part in it first, and your team has never seen you point at somebody else. The blind spot is that you have taken so much of it on yourself that nobody under you has learned to own anything.
Very Responsible|Leadership.ask: Who on your team has never had to explain a failure?

Very Responsible|Mercy.recognize: You do not only feel for people, you take on the practical weight of their situation and see it through. The cost is that you have made yourself liable for results in lives which are not yours to run.

Very Responsible|Miracles.recognize: You are careful about promising anyone anything in prayer, because you know what a raised hope costs a person. The blind spot is that this care has made your praying small, and you have started managing God's reputation for him.
Very Responsible|Miracles.ask: What are you protecting God from by not asking?

Very Responsible|Pastor/Shepherd.recognize: You take the care of your people seriously, as a charge you will be asked about one day, and none of them are neglected. The cost is that you have taken on their choices as well as their care, and you lie awake over decisions that were theirs.
Very Responsible|Pastor/Shepherd.ask: Whose decision kept you awake last week?

Very Responsible|Prophecy.recognize: You will name a wrong thing even where naming it makes it yours to deal with, which is why most people stay quiet. The blind spot is that you now own several problems you merely identified, and nobody else has picked one up.
Very Responsible|Prophecy.ask: What did you name that then became yours?

Very Responsible|Service.recognize: If you said you would do it, it is done, and you have never left anybody checking. The cost is that you also complete what other people abandoned, silently, and the ministry has no idea how much of it is like that.
Very Responsible|Service.ask: How much of your work was originally somebody else's?

Very Responsible|Teaching.recognize: You take seriously that people will believe what you tell them, and you have never taught something you had not tested. The blind spot is that you hold yourself liable for what they do with it, and one student's failure has stayed with you for years.
Very Responsible|Teaching.ask: Which former student do you still feel you failed?

Very Responsible|Tongues.recognize: You pray for the people in your charge by name, every one, because you regard it as owed to them. The cost is that prayer has become another duty you would be at fault for dropping, and it is heavy now.
Very Responsible|Tongues.ask: What does prayer feel like when you are behind on it?

Very Responsible|Wisdom.recognize: You are careful what you tell people, because you know they may act on it, and your advice is weighed before it is given. The blind spot is that you then own their decision, and you have borne the results of choices which were never yours.
Very Responsible|Wisdom.ask: Whose bad decision are you still holding?

wordBank.note: Each item carries a three-word bank: its original essence word plus two synonyms. A card prints six words, three from each side. essence/action/shadow are unchanged -- bank is additive. Asserted by scripts/verify_word_bank.js.
